Lane A12 recorded ClusterAddonProfile as a preset kind serving only authored add-ons. That point is settled by a decision and is not a finding. Only the overstated description is a finding ([API-132](#api-132)).

#### Recommended shapes

These are the audit's proposals. Each is the smallest change that resolves the cited findings.

**1. Take the ClusterAddon inputs surface out of v1alpha1 ([API-30](#api-30), [API-34](#api-34), [API-47](#api-47)).**
`spec.inputs`, its `cephConsumerAttachment` effect and `ClusterAddonBinding.spec.addonConfigs` have no consumer and no tracking item. Even so, the effect widens Environment cluster selection. The ClusterAddon and Entitlement rows marked "none tracked" also break the warning's own promise to name an item ([API-34](#api-34)). The other option, an admission refusal under api.md's compiler-boundary rule, is an owner choice that [API-30](#api-30) leaves open. `spec.steps` stays as it is, because D183 (Q115 c) keeps it.

```text
# before
kind: ClusterAddon
spec:
  inputs:
    - {name: storage, resourceKind: CephConsumer,
       effects: [{cephConsumerAttachment: {}}]}
  olm: {...}
kind: ClusterAddonBinding
spec: {addonRefs: [widgets],
       addonConfigs: [{addonRef: widgets, inputs: [...]}]}
# after: inputs and addonConfigs are unknown fields;
# the shapes move to specs/deferred/add-ons-design.md
kind: ClusterAddon
spec: {olm: {...}}
```

Breaks: any input that authors these fields. No executable add-on uses them, because selecting one refuses at plan. The work also removes three diagnostic rows, one unrealized row and the Environment selection clause.

**2. One catalog-source rule for packages and authored add-ons ([API-31](#api-31), [API-33](#api-33)).**
The priority and poll-interval refusals apply only to authored catalogs. Only fdf refuses an unowned source that is not a default catalog. [API-31](#api-31) offers a second option: keep the package exemption, but state it with its reason. [API-33](#api-33) recommends stating the rule once in the shared Subscription section, so that a source must be the package's own catalogSource.name or a default catalog, and a package that is meant to differ says why in its own section.

```text
# before: package arm admits what the authored arm refuses
packages:
  fdf:
    subscription:
      source: <any name>
      catalogSource: {name: <owned>, image: <digest>,
                      priority: -100, pollInterval: 10s}
# after: one rule in the shared Subscription section
      source: <a default catalog or an owned catalogSource.name>
      catalogSource: {name: <owned>, image: <digest>,
                      priority: -150, pollInterval: 10m}
```

Breaks: every package catalog authored at priority -100 or above, or with a poll interval under one minute. It also breaks every OLM package whose `source` names an unowned custom catalog.

**3. One routing table for Ceph service bindings ([API-05](#api-05), [API-46](#api-46), [API-44](#api-44)).**
The routing rule is stated three ways. One of them refuses the oauth2-proxy bindings that a tested example needs. The proposal states it once, in ceph-native-api.md#secret-bindings, and makes api/ceph.md link to it. That fix covers [API-05](#api-05). The same edit lets the api/ceph.md family list link to the native records instead of copying them ([API-46](#api-46)), and adds the NVMe-oF listeners to the listener list ([API-44](#api-44)).

```text
service type          -> executing block
rgw, rgw ingress      -> gateway block
grafana, snmp-gateway -> monitoring unit
mgmt-gateway, oauth2-proxy -> management gateway unit
nvmeof                -> nvmeof unit
nfs, nfs ingress      -> none
any other entry       -> refuses at plan
```

Breaks: no input. The tested oauth2-proxy bindings become valid under the text.

**4. Move IBM package coordinates into the distribution arm ([ARC-04](#arc-04)).**
Today the repository, its key, the trust bundle and the package versions sit at the top level, while `oss.mirror` sits inside its own arm. That breaks api.md's union rule and gives operators two places that say where packages come from.

```text
# before
spec:
  distribution: {ibm: {callHome: enabled, packages: {source: vendor}}}
  packageVersion: <v>
  packageRepository: <url>      # IBM default when omitted
  packageRepositoryKey: <url>
  cephadm: {ansible: {packageVersion: <v>}}
  nfsGanesha: {packageVersion: <v>}
# after
spec:
  distribution:
    ibm:
      callHome: enabled
      packages: {version: <v>, repository: <url>,
                 repositoryKey: <url>, trustBundleRef: <bundle>}
      cephadmAnsible: {version: <v>}
      nfsGanesha: {version: <v>}
```

Breaks: every IBM CephCluster input and every example. The `distribution.oss` suppression entry goes away. Whether `distribution` becomes required stays with the owner's open answer to Q127.

**5. CephReplication owns the mirroring mode ([API-85](#api-85)).**
Today the operator writes the mode on both pools, and the mode is realized only when a CephReplication names the pool.

```text
# before
kind: CephPool        # both pools
spec: {role: rbd, mirroring: {mode: image}}
kind: CephReplication
spec: {clusterRef: a, type: rbd, poolRef: p, peerClusterRef: b,
       peerPoolRef: q, imageRefs: [disk-1]}
# after
kind: CephPool
spec: {role: rbd}
kind: CephReplication
spec: {clusterRef: a, type: rbd, poolRef: p, peerClusterRef: b,
       peerPoolRef: q, mode: image, imageRefs: [disk-1]}
```

Breaks: every CephPool that authors `mirroring`. [API-85](#api-85) leaves `type` and arm nesting alone until an RGW arm is designed.

**6. Derive the NVMe-oF listeners ([API-88](#api-88), [API-28](#api-28)).**
`listeners` must equal the gateway hosts at port 4420, so it is a hand-kept copy of the service placement. The field becomes optional and derived, following the D183 Q83 (b) precedent. The same change adds a trust-extent paragraph: a host NQN is asserted by the initiator and does not authenticate it ([API-28](#api-28)).

```text
# before
spec:
  serviceRef: nvmeof.<group>.<id>
  listeners: [{host: node-04}, {host: node-05}]
  hosts: [<initiator nqn>]
# after
spec:
  serviceRef: nvmeof.<group>.<id>
  # listeners derived: one at 4420 on each gateway host;
  # an authored set must equal it
  hosts: [<initiator nqn>]
```

Breaks: no input. The examples drop the derived values.

**7. One service-reference spelling and no single-value fields ([API-10](#api-10), [API-86](#api-86)).**
Of the sibling kinds, only CephNFSExport spells its service reference `serviceID`, and the reference test cannot see that field. `CephPool.application` and `CephFilesystem.mdsServiceRef` each admit only one legal value.

```text
# before
kind: CephNFSExport
spec: {clusterRef: c, serviceID: shares, subvolumeRef: docs}
kind: CephPool
spec: {role: rbd, application: rbd}
kind: CephFilesystem
spec: {clusterRef: c, mdsServiceRef: mds.files, ...}
# after
kind: CephNFSExport
spec: {clusterRef: c, serviceRef: shares, subvolumeRef: docs}
kind: CephPool
spec: {role: rbd}
kind: CephFilesystem
spec: {clusterRef: c, ...}       # binds mds.<name>
```

Breaks: every NFS export input, plus any pool or filesystem that authors the removed fields. [API-10](#api-10) also proposes `tiebreaker.nodeRef` for the stretch tiebreaker.

**8. Key the OpenShift virtual-media rule on delivery mode and list the inert fields ([API-22](#api-22), [API-24](#api-24)).**
The rule is keyed on bare metal, but a libvirt cluster also fetches its media. Without the field, a libvirt cluster passes admission and fails later, during request derivation. [API-24](#api-24) adds the inert-field rows that should warn `api.deferred`.

```text
# before
redfishVirtualMedia.artifactServerEndpoint:
  required when any bound machine uses bare metal
# after
redfishVirtualMedia.artifactServerEndpoint:
  required when any node takes fetched delivery;
  refused when every node takes pushed delivery
inert, warns api.deferred:
  spec.install.platform.vsphere.nodeNetworking
  spec.install.platform.<any arm> on a single-node cluster
  spec.install.agent.bootArtifacts in connected mode
```

Breaks: a libvirt cluster input that omits the endpoint now refuses at admission instead of failing late.

#### Is the number of storage kinds earned?

Mostly, yes. There are fifteen Ceph kinds: CephCluster plus fourteen resource kinds. By lane A11's own reading, every resource kind except CephSMBResource gives one owned native object its own errors and its own removal boundary, and none is a command bag. Lane A11 also reads the thin kinds, CephObjectUser and CephObjectBucket, as earning their place as reference and credential-custody targets. Both readings are the auditor's working observations, not verified findings. The shared contract supports the split. Every resource names its owner through a required `clusterRef`, and no owner is found by matching a native name (specs/ceph-resources.md:33-40). The cost is in the fields, not in the number of kinds. Several fields repeat a derived value or admit one value only ([API-85](#api-85), [API-86](#api-86), [API-88](#api-88)). Two kinds keep two field tables for one kind ([API-27](#api-27)). Merging kinds would not fix any of that. Removing those fields would.

### 5.4 Authoring friction and the examples

Verdict: the input contract holds together. Authoring it costs too much, and the examples teach that cost. In four cold reads, the auditors counted 14 to 41 objects per scenario and 8 to 16 facts stated more than once. The worst problems are not the repeated facts. They are contradictions on destructive paths ([API-03](#api-03), [REC-02](#rec-02), [DOC-01](#doc-01)) and refusals that arrive only after effects ([API-06](#api-06), [REC-15](#rec-15), [API-37](#api-37)). The examples are honest about placeholders (examples/README.md:65-73). They also carry one stale offline procedure ([DOC-02](#doc-02)) and a hand-written workaround for [API-06](#api-06) in every Ceph example. 59% of their YAML files are byte-identical copies, and no page says how operators should share objects between environments ([API-131](#api-131)).

| Scenario | Objects the operator writes | Facts stated more than once | Worst frictions (finding ids) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| libvirt lab: OpenShift, Ceph, Data Foundation | 41 in lab-compact-df (about 37 needed) | about 16 | [API-06](#api-06), [API-36](#api-36), [API-37](#api-37), [API-98](#api-98), [DOC-04](#doc-04), [DOC-12](#doc-12) |
| Bare metal through vendor BMCs | about 31 | about 9, typed 30+ times | [API-03](#api-03), [REC-02](#rec-02), [DOC-01](#doc-01), [API-38](#api-38), [REC-15](#rec-15), [API-99](#api-99), [CLI-33](#cli-33) |
| KubeVirt machines | 14 (external host), 28 (host built in the same context) | 8 | [API-16](#api-16), [API-39](#api-39), [DOC-05](#doc-05), [DOC-06](#doc-06), [DOC-07](#doc-07), [REC-16](#rec-16), [DOC-13](#doc-13) |
| Infrastructure services and networks | 19 (managed), 18 (external) | 8 | [DOC-02](#doc-02), [API-40](#api-40), [API-41](#api-41), [CLI-03](#cli-03), [API-101](#api-101), [API-102](#api-102), [DOC-14](#doc-14), [DOC-15](#doc-15) |

The counts are the auditors' own (lanes A15 to A18). The 41 objects match a per-kind count of the example's files.

**Frictions by class**

- **Undetermined value.** No operator page gives the generic journey from context to destroy ([DOC-04](#doc-04)). No operator page maps an intent to its kind and field ([DOC-15](#doc-15)). No operator page says where the exact WWN, serial, size and MAC values come from ([CLI-33](#cli-33)). The nested KubeVirt example requires an RWX class on a host that the same apply builds, and does not say when to create it ([DOC-05](#doc-05)).
- **Repeated fact.** Each physical disk identity is restated in four places per host ([API-99](#api-99)). The IBM registry key goes in two Secrets, and nothing checks before installation that the pull secret carries it ([API-37](#api-37)). The noProxy list is repeated across objects ([API-102](#api-102)). A hosted KubeVirt segment restates its Network, and nothing checks it ([API-39](#api-39)). 38 example default routes repeat their Network's gateway ([API-41](#api-41)). Examples author values that normalization already derives ([DOC-26](#doc-26)).
- **Misleading name.** The realized KubeVirt arm is defined on a page titled "Refused machine arms" ([API-16](#api-16)). ClusterAddonProfile promises reusable configuration that it cannot hold ([API-132](#api-132)). The phrase "the Environment's directory is the scope" names the wrong boundary ([API-57](#api-57)).
- **Hidden default.** Under default domains, the Ceph node FQDN default can never match the installed hostname ([API-06](#api-06)). With no root hint, the default is the firmware boot volume, while other pages still refuse that case ([API-03](#api-03)). An omitted route silently drops the Network gateway ([API-41](#api-41)). An install-profile proxy with no configured repositories has no effect, and nothing warns ([API-101](#api-101)).
- **Leaked implementation.** One WWN root disk is spelled differently for managed OS and for the agent installer ([API-38](#api-38)). OSD paths follow the libvirt bus mapping, and nothing checks them before host preparation ([API-36](#api-36)). KubeVirt platform derivation is special-cased and the spec gives no reason ([API-100](#api-100)).
- **Example and spec disagree.** The disconnected example cites controller install flags that were removed ([DOC-02](#doc-02)). Pages disagree on whether a physical OpenShift node installs ([DOC-01](#doc-01)) and whether the erase policy must name the root disk ([REC-02](#rec-02)). The KubeVirt examples ask the operator for DNS records that managed DNS publishes ([DOC-06](#doc-06)). They also claim a virtctl pin that their Environment never declares ([DOC-07](#doc-07)). Other mismatches: a BMC described as one port ([DOC-12](#doc-12)), the KubeVirt RHEL limit left unstated ([DOC-13](#doc-13)), spec.downloads absent from the guide ([DOC-14](#doc-14)), and the runbook-location rule ([DOC-23](#doc-23)).
- **Late refusal.** These gaps are caught only after effects, or by no gate:

| Gap | Caught today | Finding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ceph node FQDN mismatch | `host.dns` preflight, after the OS installs | [API-06](#api-06) |
| Physical Ceph host with no erase coverage | at destroy; the only exit is orphaning | [REC-15](#rec-15) |
| libvirt OSD path the profile does not realize | at host preparation | [API-36](#api-36) |
| Missing cp.icr.io entry | at image pull, after the cluster installs | [API-37](#api-37) |
| Managed Proxy behind an egress proxy | when its clients pull | [API-40](#api-40) |
| Wrong external DNS, NTP or proxy | in the consumer; the contract contradicts itself | [CLI-03](#cli-03) |
| macspoofchk on with installer VIPs | no gate refuses it | [REC-16](#rec-16) |

**What the tracked examples show and do not show**

The examples cover a lot. There are 35 scenarios and 920 YAML files, and they use 32 of the 35 catalogued kinds (specs/api.md:395-405). A test holds each scenario to a category and scenario layout, an environment.yaml, a README and an index row (test/architecture/docs_test.go:571-598).

- **Kinds no example uses.** LoadBalancer and ClusterAddonProfile are realized, but no worked input exists for either ([DOC-28](#doc-28)). CustomPlaybook is absent by design. Five Ceph kinds and ClusterAddon each appear in one example only.
- **Arms and fields not shown.** Lane E01's table, not separately verified, lists okd, disconnected install mode, the redhatCeph Entitlement, the oss distribution, spec.dependencyVersions and spec.downloads. The dependencyVersions gap is the one behind [DOC-07](#doc-07).
- **Copies.** 548 of 920 YAML files (59%) share one of 76 contents with another example. dns.yaml and ntp.yaml each appear 33 times, and artifact-server.yaml 32 times. READMEs describe scenarios as "lab-sno plus" a few files. Import takes one directory and follows no links, and no page says composition belongs to an external renderer. So the only visible way to share is a fork ([API-131](#api-131)). The layout convention behind those copies is never written down ([DOC-27](#doc-27)).
- **What the copies teach.** Every Ceph example overrides each node FQDN by hand to work around [API-06](#api-06); lane E01 counted 45 overrides. The fix proposed for [API-06](#api-06) would let the examples drop them ([DOC-26](#doc-26)).

**Proposals, ordered** (all are the audit's proposals and the smallest change each finding allows)

Make the root optional in the erase rules ([REC-02](#rec-02)). Drop the physical OpenShift refusal ([DOC-01](#doc-01)). Replace the removed wheel flags ([DOC-02](#doc-02)).

Do not add a repeatable `--input-dir` before a consumer needs it ([API-131](#api-131)). Add worked LoadBalancer and ClusterAddonProfile inputs ([DOC-28](#doc-28)). Fix the ClusterAddonProfile description ([API-132](#api-132)) and the scope wording ([API-57](#api-57)).

### 5.5 Benchmark against the APIs operators already know

Verdict: the grammar matches Kubernetes API conventions where operators rely on them. It is stricter where an error would cost data or leak a credential. Its departures (no `status`, lowerCamel enums, plain-string `Ref`s) are deliberate and fit a file-based day-0 tool. Seven differences carry a cost, and all are Low except one. The Medium one is [API-10](#api-10): some references escape the typed reference classes. Every external statement below was checked by lane A19 or A20 on a named page. Comparisons whose reference side was left unverified are not included: list merge keys, durations, deprecation policy, the apimachinery error shape, Cluster API, Rook, install-config and Kubernetes Secret selectors.

**Grammar conventions (reference: Kubernetes API conventions, verified)**

| Convention area | Reference practice | Bootwright | Verdict | Finding |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Object identity | group/version/kind, namespace/name; labels for selection | One flat namespace per kind; `metadata` holds only `name` and `labels` (specs/api.md:232-257) | Deliberate difference; labels have no stated effect | [API-60](#api-60) |
| Desired vs observed | `spec` and `status` on one object | `spec` only; observed state lives in the context, evidence and `diff` (specs/api.md:538-547) | Deliberate difference | — |
| Conditions | `conditions[]` with type, status, reason | None; block evidence and diagnostics | Deliberate difference | — |
| Optional, required, zero | Each field is optional or required; unset is distinct from zero | Presence-preserving values; explicit `null` refused (specs/api.md:146-152) | Aligned, stricter | [API-110](#api-110) (profile sizes default to a refused 0) |
| Visible defaults | Defaults written into the stored object | Effective output shows defaults (specs/api.md:520-528) | Aligned, with an internal contradiction | [API-103](#api-103) |
| References | `fooName` for a name, `fooRef` for an object reference | One `Ref`/`Refs` suffix for plain names, test-enforced (specs/api.md:261-268, 366-383) | Deliberate difference; costly where a reference stays untyped | [API-10](#api-10) |
| Unions | One-of members, optional discriminator | Presence arms; enums only for block-less variants; one tested rule (specs/api.md:309-326) | Aligned, cleaner | [API-103](#api-103) (rule 4) |
| Enum values | UpperCamel | lowerCamel for Bootwright-owned values, native spellings kept (specs/api.md:372-375, D183) | Deliberate difference | — |
| Units | Unit in the field name with an integer, or a typed quantity | `sizeBytes`, `memoryMiB`, `diskGiB` integers; `targetSizeBytes` takes a suffixed string | Costly difference | [API-104](#api-104) |
| Field naming | lowerCamel, unit suffixes | lowerCamel; reserved `type` and `management` (specs/api.md:366-383) | Aligned except two gaps | [API-10](#api-10), [API-104](#api-104) |

Bootwright also goes further than the reference in places, and its own text says so. Unknown fields are refused at every typed level, with bounded did-you-mean hints (specs/api.md:154-166). A refusal never echoes an authored scalar value, since that value may be a credential (specs/api.md:168-187). YAML 1.1/1.2 ambiguities are closed: no aliases, merge keys, tags or nulls, and leading-zero integers are refused (specs/api.md:110-122). Three costs rest on Bootwright's own text, not on a comparison. The diagnostic field-path grammar is never defined ([API-105](#api-105)). Two fields admit only one legal value ([API-86](#api-86)). The family text names a profile field that does not exist ([API-59](#api-59)).

**Domain shapes (reference pages as the lanes verified them)**

| Bootwright shape | Reference API | Where Bootwright is clearer | Where it differs at a cost |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Machine` bare-metal `bmc.address` | Metal3 BareMetalHost `bmc.address` with driver schemes (book.metal3.io supported hardware) | One canonical `/redfish/v1/Systems/<id>` address; driver schemes refused; boot method kept out of the address (specs/api/machines.md:606-619) | — |
| `Machine` root device | Metal3 `rootDeviceHints`, one block (book.metal3.io root device hints) | Reuses Metal3's hint names; refuses kernel names such as `/dev/sda` for a destructive target (specs/api/machines.md:637-680) | Disk identities split across `spec.hardware` and the arm, with no stated placement rule ([API-107](#api-107)); field tables omit admitted fields ([API-109](#api-109)) |
| `OpenShiftCluster` base domain | Hive ClusterDeployment `baseDomain`, set per cluster (Hive using-hive docs) | Platform derived explicitly; mixed endpoint sources refused (specs/api/openshift-clusters.md:147-173) | One Environment zone sets every cluster's `baseDomain`, and the limit is not stated ([API-106](#api-106)) |
| `ClusterAddon.spec.olm.subscription` | OLM Subscription: `spec.name` is the package; `spec.config` (operator-framework/api subscription types; OLM subscription-config design doc) | Manual approval, with only `startingCSV` approved (specs/api/addons.md:123) | `subscription.name` means the object, not the package ([API-108](#api-108)); not having Subscription config is not marked as deliberate ([API-111](#api-111)) |

The lanes recorded other strengths in Bootwright's own text, without an external check. Machine roles come from the objects that reference the Machine, so no role label can drift from its bindings (specs/api/machines.md:346-351). Substrates are presence arms, so a new substrate is one new arm (specs/api/machines.md:36-40). Typed Secrets replace name-and-key selectors, and each consumer checks the type it accepts (specs/api/secrets.md:24-31). cephadm service documents stay native, in snake_case (specs/api/ceph.md:3-15).

**Audit proposals, smallest change first.** Each one follows the record of its finding.

- [API-10](#api-10): rename `tiebreaker.node` to `tiebreaker.nodeRef` and give it the nested topology-node type. Type the CephNFSExport `serviceID` as `serviceRef`; it keeps the bare ID that ceph-resources.md:48 allows. Then drop 'a topology node name' and `serviceID` from the class table's Written column.
- [API-108](#api-108): rename `subscription.name` to `subscription.objectName`. Add one sentence saying that OLM's `spec.name` is `subscription.package` here.
- [API-104](#api-104): make `targetSizeBytes` an integer, like `quota.maxBytes`. Add no general quantity section until a second consumer exists.
- [API-110](#api-110): make libvirt and vSphere profile sizes required, with a minimum of 1.
- [API-106](#api-106) and [API-111](#api-111): add one sentence each that states the limit (one base zone per Environment; Subscription config left to GitOps under D199). Park the capability until a consumer is named.
- [API-103](#api-103), [API-105](#api-105), [API-107](#api-107), [API-109](#api-109): spec text only. Reconcile rule 4 with the Secret source carve-out, define the path grammar, state where the disk-lifecycle policies belong, and complete the field tables.

Keep these differences on purpose: no `status` or conditions, lowerCamel enums, a single `Ref` suffix, and the stricter decoding and value-free diagnostics. Each one fits a file-based day-0 tool, and the enum casing and the `Ref` suffix are test-enforced. Align with the reference where operators copy fields directly from it: OLM's Subscription keys ([API-108](#api-108)), unit-named integer sizes ([API-104](#api-104)), and required fields that are actually reported as missing ([API-110](#api-110)). Close the internal gaps that weaken the strictness Bootwright claims, starting with typing every reference ([API-10](#api-10)).

## 6. The CLI and its output contract

### 6.1 Verdict

The CLI contract is strong on safety. It has a fixed invocation precedence, one confirmation rule bound to step digests, a strict JSON envelope and a diagnostic registry held by a test. Commands that read secrets prove the target before they read any custody, and SSH sessions prove the host key before they offer a credential. The weak point is the journey after a completed apply. `plan`, `status`, `context update` and `diff` give different answers about an edited or drifted context ([CLI-01](#cli-01), [CLI-09](#cli-09), [REC-03](#rec-03), [CLI-10](#cli-10), [CLI-39](#cli-39)). The second weakness is drift between the catalog and the pages that restate it: flag spellings, `--stage` scope, effects, result fields and structured-output refusals ([CLI-05](#cli-05), [CLI-06](#cli-06), [CLI-07](#cli-07), [CLI-15](#cli-15), [CLI-16](#cli-16), [CLI-19](#cli-19)). The operator guide has good reference sections, but it has no generic first-run path, and its `cluster exec` default is wrong ([DOC-03](#doc-03), [DOC-04](#doc-04)). Across the cli area the audit verified 62 findings: one High, 30 Medium and 31 Low. None is blocking.

### 6.2 Command grammar

| Command group | Verdict | Keep | Change (finding ids) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Global flags and parsing | adequate | Precedence order and stubs that take no effect (specs/cli.md:52-92); raw argument bounds (specs/cli.md:96-119); the payload rule for the four exec-style commands (specs/cli.md:220-233); flag scope derived from dispatch (specs/cli/commands.md:8-22); closed completion (specs/cli/commands.md:289-332) | One empty-list rule instead of seven ([CLI-04](#cli-04), [CLI-12](#cli-12)); one meaning for `-f` and `--input-dir` ([CLI-07](#cli-07), [CLI-58](#cli-58)); a single owner for privilege ([CLI-34](#cli-34)); state each `--dry-run` boundary ([CLI-35](#cli-35)) |
| Context and controller commands | adequate | Context-free list; `controller check` names the next step | JSON contract for `controller install` ([CLI-15](#cli-15)); result rows for `rebind` and `uninstall` ([CLI-16](#cli-16)); catalog headings match the help groups ([CLI-49](#cli-49)) |
| Validate, preflight and render | needs work | `validate` has two modes and is context-free with `-f`; preflight says what it does not observe (specs/cli/output.md:603-616) | `--stage` scope and default ([CLI-06](#cli-06)); rename `--trust-on-first-use` ([CLI-08](#cli-08), [CLI-29](#cli-29)); exit status for unknown and pending checks ([CLI-42](#cli-42)); one check row shape ([CLI-44](#cli-44)); `render effective` input spelling ([CLI-07](#cli-07)) |
| Plan, apply, destroy and status | needs work | Settled-verb rule (specs/cli.md:594-603); authorizations checked before the prompt and before registration (specs/cli.md:605-611); "stages are not strata" (specs/state-reconciliation.md:1071-1074); status candidates gated by each verb's own decision (specs/cli.md:741-753) | Preview and next step over a completed apply ([CLI-01](#cli-01), [CLI-09](#cli-09), [CLI-37](#cli-37)); exit status of each outcome ([CLI-38](#cli-38)); `--authorize` grammar ([CLI-50](#cli-50)); Effects cells ([CLI-19](#cli-19), [CLI-36](#cli-36)) |

| Disclosure commands | needs work | Target and applicability proved before any custody read (specs/cli.md:1123-1126) | Object-user keys missing from the output contract ([CLI-11](#cli-11)); empty keyring flags ([CLI-12](#cli-12)); reveals under a sudo output log ([CLI-26](#cli-26)) |
| Power and file copy | adequate | Never acts on the controller host (specs/cli.md:1643-1652); `machine cp` paths are literal and bounded (specs/cli/machine-copy.md:11-19) | Result shape depends on how many Machines were named ([CLI-17](#cli-17)); "will reconcile" wording ([REC-81](#rec-81)); `machine cp` missing from the admitted utilities ([SCO-03](#sco-03)); power during an incomplete operation ([CLI-55](#cli-55)) |

### 6.3 The lifecycle journey

The first run is well specified. `plan` makes exactly the decision of the verb it previews and has no effects. `apply` freezes the plan, checks authorizations, asks once, then registers, and prints a receipt even after an interrupt (specs/cli.md:620-627). A failed or interrupted apply continues its frozen plan. A repeated verb on a completed context settles and points to `diff --observe` (specs/cli.md:594-603).

After an edit to a completed context, the specs give conflicting answers.

| Case | What the spec says | Conflict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `plan` over a completed apply | It previews the destroy (cli.md:589-591, state-reconciliation.md:1259) | Other pages say it previews the additive apply when only add-ons were added ([CLI-01](#cli-01)) |
| `plan` receipt | `next: destroy` | The shared `next` rule does not say it applies to the previewed operation, and `status` reads `none` ([CLI-37](#cli-37)) |
| `status` over a completed apply | Offers nothing | An additive apply would pass, and readiness skips the Secrets it would bind ([CLI-09](#cli-09)) |
| `context update` | Warns that apply refuses the input until destroy | Additive input is admitted ([REC-03](#rec-03)) |
| `diff` with unchanged input | Points to `status` | `status` offers nothing for drift ([CLI-39](#cli-39)) |

So before any effect, only the `diff` Input line says that an edit will apply additively (specs/cli.md:882). The `context update` warning and the `plan` preview contradict it ([REC-03](#rec-03), [CLI-01](#cli-01)). The exit status of a paused destroy and of an `unknown` result is only implied ([CLI-38](#cli-38)).

Stage selection is sound in principle: `--stage` and `--until` only gate which blocks start, and the plan stays complete (specs/state-reconciliation.md:14-15). The rule paragraph omits preflight and gives the wrong default for it ([CLI-06](#cli-06)). Over a completed apply, `--stage` inherits the [CLI-01](#cli-01) conflict.

Confirmation is defined once (specs/cli.md:245-281). When structured output is selected or no terminal can answer, a missing `--yes` fails three ways: exit 1 with a repeat that adds `--yes`, `cli.usage` exit 2, or no stated code ([CLI-05](#cli-05)). With standard output redirected, a host-key or `data-loss` prompt can be accepted without the plan it confirms ever being shown ([CLI-27](#cli-27)). `secret generate --renew` replaces material with no confirmation ([CLI-22](#cli-22)).

### 6.4 The output contract

**Streams and exit statuses.** One table covers every mode (specs/cli/output.md:5-37). Its exception list for human stdout on failure is closed, and several command contracts break it ([CLI-43](#cli-43)). Exit 3 of `diff --exit-code` leaves out `unmanaged`. It also stays 0 for field-equal add-on drift, which is the case GitOps co-management produces ([CLI-10](#cli-10)). Preflight has no stated exit for unknown or pending checks ([CLI-42](#cli-42)).

**JSON documents.** The envelope is strict: fixed field order, `ok` true if and only if exit 0, one document (specs/cli/output.md:229-246). The table of stable result fields has fallen behind the prose. It has no rows for `controller rebind`, `controller uninstall` or `machine cp`, and it leaves out `authorizations`, `files` and `objectUsers` ([CLI-16](#cli-16), [CLI-41](#cli-41), [CLI-11](#cli-11)). The JSON contract for `controller install` contradicts itself ([CLI-15](#cli-15)). A failure on one power target returns `result: null`, while a failure among several returns rows ([CLI-17](#cli-17)). `cluster info` promises OpenShift endpoints and a node list that it never emits ([CLI-30](#cli-30)).

**Diagnostic taxonomy.** The registry is closed and held to the code by a test (specs/cli/output.md:996-1010). Its gaps are in meaning, not in coverage:

- `lifecycle.unsupported` carries 17 named Ceph runtime refusals beyond its registered meaning ([CLI-31](#cli-31)).
- Adapter refusal tokens have no registry that pairs each token with its code ([CLI-24](#cli-24)).
- Placeholders in refusal text are undefined, and one names the wrong Secret ([CLI-32](#cli-32)).
- OpenShift and Ceph remedies that say "correct `<cluster>`" name no field or value ([CLI-61](#cli-61)). The remediation rule does not say where a command remedy ends and a prose remedy begins ([CLI-62](#cli-62)).
- The registry has no severity column, and `secret.store` is both a code and the namespace of seven codes ([CLI-45](#cli-45), [CLI-48](#cli-48)).

**Logs.** The `Logs` and `Follow` fields and the safe reader are sound. Bounds and retention counting are incomplete ([CLI-47](#cli-47)). Secrecy of retained adapter output covers only tasks that read bound material. It does not cover credentials the tools produce ([ARC-05](#arc-05)).

**Compatibility.** Two pages promise without condition that JSON result schemas stay stable, and the section calls paths, flags and fields public contracts that need a "compatibility review" it never defines. No page says how a surface may move before 1.0 ([CLI-18](#cli-18)). The audit proposes that it say, under D241, that before 1.0 a surface moves only by changing the spec in the same commit, with no alias, in a commit marked breaking, and that `schemaVersion` stays `v1alpha1`.

### 6.5 Operator documentation

The help rules (specs/cli/commands.md:199-218), the version output (specs/cli/commands.md:248-287) and completion are exact and test-bound. In the operator guide, these reference sections agree with the catalog flag for flag: host preparation (docs/operator-guide.md:57-139), sudo (docs/operator-guide.md:190-243) and following a run (docs/operator-guide.md:363-401). The proxy destination list is held to the code by a test (docs/operator-guide.md:165-188). The guide restates a lot of spec text, and the newest decisions are where that text has drifted:

- **Wrong behaviour.** `cluster exec` without `--node` runs on the administrator node, not the first node ([DOC-03](#doc-03)). Setup downloads no wheels ([DOC-09](#doc-09)). No spec bounds Ctrl-C to one minute inside a package transaction ([DOC-10](#doc-10)). Two other pages still cite removed `controller install` flags ([DOC-02](#doc-02)).
- **Missing spine.** No page gives the generic order from `context init` to `context delete`, and the pages disagree about who owns a journey ([DOC-04](#doc-04), [DOC-23](#doc-23)). Recovery from a failed apply sits under a build-change heading ([DOC-16](#doc-16)). The unattended apply example omits the digest-bound `--authorize` rule ([DOC-17](#doc-17)).
- **Smaller drift.** Examples name a context that does not declare those Machines or clusters ([DOC-18](#doc-18)). The guide gives a Python range wrong for the lock ([DOC-21](#doc-21)), omits uninstall from the proxied route ([DOC-22](#doc-22)), and carries milestone gate state that milestones own ([DOC-19](#doc-19)).

### 6.6 What to change

These are the audit's proposals, in order of priority, each kept to the smallest change.

1. Write one rule for a completed apply in specs/cli.md, then point state-reconciliation.md, contexts.md, the `status` candidates and the receipt at it. Additive input previews and offers `apply`. Any other edit previews the destroy ([CLI-01](#cli-01), [CLI-09](#cli-09), [CLI-37](#cli-37), [REC-03](#rec-03), [CLI-39](#cli-39)).
2. Fix the guide's `cluster exec` default and the wheel, Ctrl-C and removed-flag sentences ([DOC-03](#doc-03), [DOC-09](#doc-09), [DOC-10](#doc-10), [DOC-02](#doc-02)).
3. Settle `diff --exit-code`: either count a partial real side toward exit 3, or reword "test for drift". Add `unmanaged` to the exit table ([CLI-10](#cli-10)).
4. State one structured-output refusal for a missing `--yes`, and one JSON rule for `controller install` ([CLI-05](#cli-05), [CLI-15](#cli-15)).
5. Correct the `--stage` paragraph for preflight. Rename `--trust-on-first-use` to `--observe-host-keys`, with no alias, since D241 allows it ([CLI-06](#cli-06), [CLI-08](#cli-08), [CLI-29](#cli-29)).
6. Replace the comma-list bullets with one rule: a supplied list needs at least one member, and an empty value is `cli.usage` exit 2. Make empty keyring flags follow it ([CLI-04](#cli-04), [CLI-12](#cli-12)).
7. Give `-f` the single meaning of desired-state input, and rename the Context-file flag to `--config` ([CLI-07](#cli-07)).
8. Derive the result-field table from the command tree with a test. Add the missing rows and fields, and make the power-verb failure shape independent of count ([CLI-16](#cli-16), [CLI-41](#cli-41), [CLI-11](#cli-11), [CLI-17](#cli-17)). Correct the `cluster info` text so that only managed Ceph entries promise endpoints and the node remedies name the CephCluster's node roster, adding no field ([CLI-30](#cli-30)).
9. Make the Effects column true: name the cache-only rebuild in each affected cell, and define how a cell with flag clauses is read ([CLI-19](#cli-19), [CLI-20](#cli-20), [CLI-36](#cli-36)).
10. Add the pre-1.0 sentence to Compatibility, and pin `schemaVersion` at `v1alpha1` until 1.0 ([CLI-18](#cli-18)).
11. Widen the `lifecycle.unsupported` registry row, add a table of Ceph refusal tokens with a test, and define the refusal placeholders ([CLI-31](#cli-31), [CLI-24](#cli-24), [CLI-32](#cli-32)).
12. Extend the `no_log` rule to credentials that tools produce and print ([ARC-05](#arc-05)).
13. Add a short "Run your own environment" section to the operator guide that links each step to its spec, and move recovery from a failed apply under its own heading ([DOC-04](#doc-04), [DOC-16](#doc-16), [DOC-17](#doc-17)).
14. Add `machine cp` to the admitted utilities in specs/project.md ([SCO-03](#sco-03)).

## 7. Architecture

### 7.1 Generic flow and specialization

**Verdict.** The spec does promise a general flow, and its design is right. Families are defined by domain. Selection is deterministic, with exactly one match. Ports belong to their consumers. An edit to the general flow is declared a missing seam (specs/architecture.md:66-86, 1164-1175, 500-502). Fitness tests hold this promise for substrate arms, implementation identity constants and the literal "ceph". The identity guard does not cover the install arm or arm field paths, which the spec says it rejects ([ARC-32](#arc-32)). Distribution values and service implementation values, which the spec also lists as selectors, are not guarded either, though the spec does not claim they are ([ARC-32](#arc-32)). The promise also fails in three places. The composition root makes domain decisions the spec forbids there ([ARC-26](#arc-26)). The extension touch lists are internally inconsistent ([ARC-07](#arc-07), [ARC-28](#arc-28)). Several general pages and packages state rules in terms of one implementation ([ARC-10](#arc-10), [CLI-25](#cli-25), [ARC-71](#arc-71)). No finding cited in 7.1 or 7.2 is High or Blocking. Most of these gaps are latent today: they would surface with the second substrate, storage family or installer.

**Architecture promises against their guards**

| Promise | Stated at | Held by | Gap |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| General flow names no family kind, arm, identity or Ceph literal | architecture.md:66-86 | `TestGeneralFlowNamesNoImplementation` | Narrow literal net; Workspace unguarded ([ARC-32](#arc-32), [ARC-71](#arc-71), [CLI-25](#cli-25)) |
| Outside owners reach arm specifics only through an owner capability, "arm field path" included | architecture.md:1196-1205 | `TestNoProductionCodeBranchesOnAnArmOrImplementationOutsideItsOwner` | No field-path detector; install arm uncovered ([ARC-32](#arc-32)); arm-named helpers pass ([ARC-72](#arc-72)); installer rule in Machine admission ([ARC-70](#arc-70)) |
| Exactly one implementation claims each object, or the object is refused | architecture.md:1168-1195 | `TestEveryExampleObjectIsClaimedOncePerFamily` (examples only, by design) | none found |
| No implicit latest version, nearest-version fallback or ambient selection | architecture.md:1170-1171 | Prose only | none found |
| Policy never branches on implementation identity | architecture.md:1173-1174 | Identity guard, partly | [ARC-10](#arc-10), [ARC-58](#arc-58) |
| Wiring makes no domain decision and writes no presentation | architecture.md:363-365 | `TestCompositionRootBuildsNoDiagnostics` (narrow) | [ARC-26](#arc-26), [ARC-79](#arc-79), [ARC-80](#arc-80) |

**General specifications that name an implementation.** Lane R05 counted 376 term hits across ten general pages. Its own approximate split is: 100 cross-links, 136 registry rows, 130 general rules written in one implementation's terms and 10 carved special cases. The lane judged the registry rows mostly correct by design: the general rules iterate them. Verified leaks:

The leak also runs the other way. Specific pages own rules that are generic. Several generic libvirt capacity admission rules, namely the reuse credit, memory and reserve rules, live only on the Ceph page ([ARC-19](#arc-19)). Libvirt provider preconditions are rows of the OpenShift refusal table ([ARC-21](#arc-21)). The cross-kind address-holder catalog lives on the OpenShift page ([ARC-03](#arc-03)).

**General code that names an implementation.** These are lane R06's own approximate counts of implementation identifiers per package:

Lane R06 observed that the guard's literal check matches arm values, identity values, the exact literal "ceph" and the substring "/ceph/", and does not match "cephadm", "redfish", "anaconda", "openshift" or Go identifiers. [ARC-32](#arc-32) records where the guard falls short of the spec's own claim: arm field paths and the install arm. The candidate "storage preflight imported by the general flow" was refuted and is not a defect.

**Composition root.** The spec admits one kind of logic in wiring: the closed list of composition translators at architecture.md:179-188. `cmd/bootwright` decides more than that:

- `controllerSockets` (wiring_firewall.go) picks each service's protocols by kind. `hostPortChecks` (wiring_host_ports.go) maps requirements to statuses and writes operator remedy text. `installProofs` (wiring_inspection.go) judges an install by implementation, verb and state. None of these is a named exception ([ARC-26](#arc-26)). Lane R02's part of the same finding adds the KubeVirt host-requirement closures, which compute add-on and network policy.
- The kind-keyed transport choice is a second copy of a fact the infrastructure-services spec owns, separate from the adapter's own table ([ARC-79](#arc-79)). The managed-service definition list is repeated at three production sites ([ARC-80](#arc-80)).
- `cephDependencyProofs.DataDisk` sends every Machine block's evidence to the libvirt reader, whatever arm produced it ([ARC-29](#arc-29)).

Outside composition, the agent-installer predicate sits in the API registry, and Controller branches on it ([ARC-58](#arc-58)).

Lanes R02 and R06 also observed two things that were not verified on their own. First, `ApplyAdmission`, `ListenerAdmission` and `PlanInspection` are single function slots filled with closure chains named after implementations (lane R02). Second, composition binds one storage inspector and one storage preflight with no per-kind dispatch (lane R06).

Audit proposal, smallest change (resolves [ARC-26](#arc-26), [ARC-79](#arc-79), [ARC-29](#arc-29)):
- Record a backlog item for the drift. Under it, move socket derivation to the service owners, host-port rows and remedies to `managedos/installation`, and the "installed" predicate to Container cluster.
- Make `DataDisk` choose its reader by `proof.Block.Implementation`, and return not-recognized for an implementation with no reader.
- Extend `TestCompositionRootBuildsNoDiagnostics` to refuse `api.<Kind>` comparisons and status or remedy literals in `cmd/bootwright`.

Do not widen the translation exception to cover the drift. Hold a family-level substrate proof port until a second producer exists (P19).

Strengths that hold across the map:
- The resolver is an immutable allowlist keyed by API kind and implementation identity, with no global registry, ambient discovery or plugin path (specs/architecture.md:615-620). Code matches it on exact (kind, implementation) (cmd/bootwright/wiring_reconciliation.go:103-132).
- Playbooks are bound as data, so a capability names no playbook (specs/architecture.md:615-617).
- Only the substrate dispatcher table names an arm's role, and an unlisted arm fails closed before lookup (specs/architecture.md:903-910). Its touch set still needs the [ARC-07](#arc-07) fix.

### 7.3 Extension scenarios

Verdict: none of the four extensions is additive today. Each one edits general specs, general code or another implementation, beyond the floor that `specs/architecture.md` promises. The extension machinery itself is sound. Selection is exact and fails closed (specs/architecture.md:1166-1176). An arm-identity allowlist is a test, not only a statement (test/architecture/implementation_identity_test.go:24-101). Stages name kinds of work, so a new kind needs no stage or engine edit (specs/state-reconciliation.md:1062-1074). The seam rule makes any general edit a separately reviewed step (specs/architecture.md:500-502). What is wrong is that the stated touch sets are incomplete and that facts which belong to one binding are kept in general places.

In each table, a row that carries an id rests on a verified finding. Every other row is the dry run's own observation (lanes R07 to R10), and the "Avoidable?" cell gives that lane's own judgement.

#### What every extension edits today

- **A touch list that is not complete.** The list is incomplete for arms ([ARC-28](#arc-28)) and contradicts itself on the dispatcher ([ARC-07](#arc-07)). The skill says no list exists ([ARC-06](#arc-06), [ARC-77](#arc-77)). A new kind ([ARC-75](#arc-75)) and a new service definition ([ARC-78](#arc-78)) have no procedure at all. A step for the controller-host footprint is also missing ([ARC-83](#arc-83)).
- **Spec tables written per kind, not per category.** These are the closure and unclaimed tables ([API-138](#api-138)), add-on and substrate references ([API-137](#api-137)), cluster discovery output ([CLI-25](#cli-25)), cross-kind address claims ([ARC-03](#arc-03)) and the managed DNS derivation ([ARC-52](#arc-52)).
- **Playbook names with no implementation token outside substrates.** This affects both the cluster and the storage dry runs ([ARC-65](#arc-65)).
- **Binding facts held in general switches or in composition.** These are arm facts ([ARC-73](#arc-73)), the Ceph proof reader ([ARC-29](#arc-29)), agent-installer selection ([ARC-58](#arc-58)), cluster access ([ARC-74](#arc-74)), service transports ([ARC-79](#arc-79)) and definition lists ([ARC-80](#arc-80)). Composition also makes domain decisions that the spec forbids there ([ARC-26](#arc-26)).
- **Rules owned by the wrong domain.** Libvirt preconditions sit in the cluster refusal table ([ARC-21](#arc-21)), and generic capacity rules sit on the Ceph page ([ARC-19](#arc-19)).
- **Selection sections and guards that promise more than they hold.** See [ARC-02](#arc-02), [ARC-76](#arc-76), and [ARC-32](#arc-32) (the identity guard covers substrate arms only).

#### What would make each extension additive (the audit's proposals)

1. **Make the procedure true.** Correct step 5 and add one substrate-arm step that links the exemption paragraph ([ARC-07](#arc-07), [ARC-28](#arc-28)). Add the controller-host step ([ARC-83](#arc-83)). Point the skill at the list instead of paraphrasing it ([ARC-06](#arc-06), [ARC-77](#arc-77)). Add "Adding a cluster kind" as a list of links, and leave the external-storage rule out until it has a consumer ([ARC-75](#arc-75)). Add the kind-catalog and Definition step ([ARC-78](#arc-78)). This is spec and skill text only.
2. **Write shared tables by category.** Use "one containerCluster root (today OpenShiftCluster)" in the closure, unclaimed, `clusterRef` and discovery rows ([API-137](#api-137), [API-138](#api-138), [CLI-25](#cli-25)). Leave the role registry as it is, and state that the first additional kind of a category whose role kinds differ makes roles per kind ([API-139](#api-139), P19).
3. **Give implementations a playbook token** once a capability has a second implementation, and enforce it in the naming test ([ARC-65](#arc-65)).
4. **Move facts to their owner, with no new interface.** An arm with no facts row refuses instead of defaulting ([ARC-73](#arc-73)). `DataDisk` picks its reader by the producing implementation ([ARC-29](#arc-29)). Host packages become one `containercluster.Facts` field ([ARC-58](#arc-58)). `Definition` carries `Transports`, and composition keeps one definition list ([ARC-79](#arc-79), [ARC-80](#arc-80)). Port and credential refusals move to the libvirt provider ([ARC-21](#arc-21)), and capacity rules move to substrates.md ([ARC-19](#arc-19)).
5. **Name selectors fully.** The Ceph selector names its `spec.distribution` arm ([ARC-76](#arc-76)). The services selection section gains its Implementations part ([ARC-02](#arc-02)).

None of these adds a registry or port without a consumer. The proposals deliberately exclude a substrate arm-descriptor registry, a service-kind registry and a managed-control-plane layout until an item needs them.

| NTP and proxy, managed or external | specs/infrastructure-services.md (Managed network services); specs/api/infrastructure-services.md | installation proxy in-tree (openshift-coverage.md:107); the lane reads the M1 baseline (D156) | [CLI-03](#cli-03), [API-20](#api-20), [API-40](#api-40), [API-48](#api-48), [API-61](#api-61), [API-80](#api-80), [API-98](#api-98), [API-101](#api-101), [API-102](#api-102), [REC-51](#rec-51), [CON-12](#con-12) |

The immediate portfolio can be told apart from the family scope in substance, but no page names it as such. specs/project.md:18-33 lists one committed portfolio that also holds vSphere, ACM, OpenShift GitOps and GitLab, and the extension envelope at specs/project.md:35-41 is the only other tier. Carrying the rest costs little in the general flow, because every arm is dispatched through one machine port, and an arm with no port fails closed (specs/substrates.md:41-56). Where it does distort, the cost lands on the portfolio's own records. The physical-node and KubeVirt-package coverage rows trail owner decisions ([SCO-01](#sco-01), [SCO-02](#sco-02)). The add-on coverage page still lists delivered per-interface MetalLB forwarding as left out ([API-32](#api-32)). The ledger rule no longer describes the runs the owner accepted ([DOC-11](#doc-11)). The lane's concern that M3 and M4 completion waits on items outside the immediate portfolio is covered by an owner decision and is not a finding.

## 8. Language responsibility matrix

### 8.1 Verdict

Mostly yes. The language table (specs/architecture.md:766-778) gives each language a Holds cell, a Never cell and a placement question, and new logic goes to the first row it answers yes to (specs/architecture.md:768). The Go and Ansible ownership bullets (specs/architecture.md:719-737) say why: Go decides, Ansible and Python reach and prove one selected effect. Tests hold the Python sites and the source-to-row map (specs/architecture.md:780-806). There is no High finding. The weak points are the wording of the Go/Python seam ([LNG-02](#lng-02), [LNG-03](#lng-03), [LNG-09](#lng-09)), zones no row covers ([LNG-01](#lng-01), the only Medium, plus [LNG-04](#lng-04), [LNG-05](#lng-05), [LNG-13](#lng-13)), a Shell rule that tracked scripts break ([LNG-12](#lng-12)), Go/Python twins with no stated contract ([LNG-10](#lng-10), [LNG-11](#lng-11)), and agent references that drift from the spec or miss paths ([LNG-06](#lng-06), [LNG-07](#lng-07), [LNG-08](#lng-08), [SKL-04](#skl-04)).

### 8.2 Decision matrix

The audit proposes this matrix as the rule. It is based on lane R11's working table and checked against SNAP. P means preferred, A allowed under the stated condition, X prohibited. "Today" gives where the rule is stated now, or names the finding that shows it is missing or conflicting.

| Kind of logic | Go | Ansible tasks | Python plugin or module | Python tooling | Shell and Make | Rule | Today |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Policy decision | P | X | X | X | X | Product meaning has one typed owner | architecture.md:719-737, 772 |
| Planning | P | X | X | X | X | Plans freeze in Go; an adapter sees one request | architecture.md:725-726, 736-737 |
| Implementation selection | P (freezes it) | A: the dispatcher table, keyed by a value Go froze | X | X | X | Authored data and gathered facts never pick code | architecture.md:724, 898-917 |
| Rendering native input | P: projections that depend on desired state | A: a template with a fixed layout and no variant branch | A: a filter | X | X | Same request, same bytes | architecture.md:699-711, 778; filters unnamed ([LNG-04](#lng-04)) |
| Bounded remote effect | X (except sshlocal) | P: a module task under argument specs | A: a protocol or transport that no builtin gives | X | X | Every managed contact crosses an adapter | architecture.md:730-737, 773-774 |
| Remote observation | X (except sshlocal) | P: allowlisted read-only modules | A: bounded native-API clients | X | X | Bounded evidence; unknown never means absent | architecture.md:733-735, 872-874; `read` verb ([ARC-66](#arc-66)) |
| Parsing native output | A: output of its own local runner or read-only port | A: consume a module's typed result | P | A: repository content | X | One parser per format | architecture.md:772 vs 739-749 ([LNG-03](#lng-03)); placement ([LNG-04](#lng-04)) |
| Retries and timeouts | P: deadlines and continuation | A: bounds fixed by the request | A: fixed, spec-owned rounds | A | X | Bounded and replay-safe | architecture.md:925-929; ansible.md:49-53 |
| Secret handling | P: store, custody, redaction | A: no_log data only | A: substitution at write time | X | A: Make hands settings over as a build secret | Never in templates, logs or build arguments | ansible.md:59-63; Makefile:15-18; architecture.md:778 |
| Privilege | P: decides the scope | A: `become` scoped to the operation | A: the one admitted `sudo -n` worker shape | X | X | Go decides least privilege; automation applies it | architecture.md:773; security.md:257-267 |
| Local file publication | P: the publication capability | A: on a managed host, atomic | A: on a managed host | A: caches and outputs only | A: a wrapper resolves a cache path | One publication owner | architecture.md:699-711; ansible.md:44-46 |
| Test orchestration | A: Go and architecture tests | X | A: collection unit tests | P: launchers | A: run a pinned launcher | Selection logic is tested code | python.md:74-85; Make missing ([LNG-05](#lng-05)) |
| Build | P: the standard-library Go step | X | X | A | A: compose targets, stamp, container build | It must run where only Go exists | architecture.md:798-804; Make missing ([LNG-05](#lng-05)) |
| Hooks | X | X | X | P: logic in a launcher | A: a short POSIX `sh` guard | Hooks run every turn and stay small | python.md:78-81; spec missing ([LNG-12](#lng-12)) |
| Completion | P: candidates from the command tree | X | X | X | A: one shim per shell, no candidate logic | One source of candidates | architecture.md:775; formatting.md:127 conflicts ([LNG-06](#lng-06)) |

Proposal: keep one owner. Do not publish a second table. Put only the cells marked missing or conflicting into the existing table and the paragraph below it (see 8.5).

### 8.3 Prohibited uses

- Ansible YAML runs a command through a shell (specs/architecture.md:773). The reference restates this in drifted words ([LNG-08](#lng-08)).
- Ansible or Python chooses a workflow, provider or variant from authored data or gathered facts (specs/architecture.md:773-774, 898-901).
- Python orders work across blocks, authorizes, or writes operation state (specs/architecture.md:774).
- Python judges a block's declared postcondition (specs/architecture.md:774, 1091-1095). The bare wording can be read as forbidding readbacks inside an adapter that the spec allows ([LNG-09](#lng-09), [ARC-64](#arc-64)).
- Python starts a process outside its site's one bounded runner, encodes canonical JSON outside its one module, or sends a remote command string outside the process boundary (specs/architecture.md:774, 786-798).
- Go contacts a managed component, except Machine's direct SSH sessions (specs/architecture.md:772, 756-758). An Ansible role installs a host package (specs/architecture.md:745-747).
- A rendered document reads files, the network or secrets at render time, or branches to select a variant (specs/architecture.md:778).
- Shell holds selection logic or parses repository content (specs/architecture.md:775). Three tracked scripts break this rule, and the spec does not name them as exceptions ([LNG-12](#lng-12)).
- Proposed: a Make recipe holds selection logic or parses repository content beyond one stated value. No rule says this today ([LNG-05](#lng-05)).
- Proposed: Python that Go ships in the executable imports beyond the standard library or uses syntax above the managed-host floor. No rule says this today ([LNG-01](#lng-01)).

### 8.4 Where the boundary is crossed or unspecified today

These are lane R12's own counts of non-test lines unless marked otherwise:

| Language or plugin type | Files | Lines |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Go (internal, cmd) | - | 152523 |
| Python collection, total | 172 | 47320 (Ceph 22526) |
| of which module utilities | 79 | 35994 |
| of which modules | 59 | 7957 |
| of which action plugins | 25 | 2731 |
| of which filters | 8 | 580 |
| of which callback | 1 | 58 |
| Ansible YAML | - | 18899 |
| Jinja templates | 12 | 415 |
| Python repository tools | 5 | 2282 |
| Python case workloads | 2 | 405 |
| Shell under scripts/ and e2e/ | 9 and 4 | 391 and 328 |

By the same count, tests hold 235213 Go lines and 81806 Python collection lines. Python is about a third the size of Go, and almost half of that Python is Ceph. The seam definitions therefore carry a lot of weight.

Zones that no rule covers:

- A Python worker at internal/machine/sshlocal/copy_worker.py (419 lines) runs on a Machine. No language row covers it, the language-row test does not scan internal/, and no floor test or sites test checks it ([LNG-01](#lng-01)).
- Filter and callback plugins are not in the Python row. Parsing native output inside role YAML has no stated placement ([LNG-04](#lng-04)). The Python site rule has no site for module utilities, filters or the callback ([LNG-13](#lng-13)).
- Make recipes have no row, yet they hold loops and parse go.mod and the docs-check list ([LNG-05](#lng-05)).
- A value or computation that Python duplicates from Go has no stated parity convention; ad hoc tests or comments hold each case ([LNG-10](#lng-10)). "Canonical JSON" names two byte encodings ([LNG-11](#lng-11)).

Rules that conflict with themselves or with practice:

- Read literally, the Go placement question also captures sequencing inside one adapter call, and the first-match sentence does not mention the paragraph that places repository tools ([LNG-02](#lng-02)).
- Read literally, the Go row's Never cell forbids the local parsing that the same section allows ([LNG-03](#lng-03)).
- "Never judges a postcondition" can be read as forbidding spec-owned readbacks such as the Ceph stretch stages ([LNG-09](#lng-09)). Python and Go predicates already differ for the package tree ([ARC-64](#arc-64)).
- The Shell row is absolute, but scripts/quick-test, scripts/check-commits and the stop hook break it. Their exceptions live only in python.md and B967 ([LNG-12](#lng-12)).
- Read-only allowlisting walks only `observe`, so the power `read` verb escapes it ([ARC-66](#arc-66)).

Agent guidance that drifts from the spec:

- formatting.md requires POSIX sh for scripts that the spec makes bash ([LNG-06](#lng-06)).
- python.md and ansible.md restate the prohibitions in drifted words ([LNG-08](#lng-08)).
- The rule for which imports a shipped worker may use differs between architecture.md and python.md ([SKL-04](#skl-04)).
- No path-scoped rule covers scripts/ or e2e/ ([LNG-07](#lng-07)).

Lane R12 also recorded Python units that hold desired-versus-observed comparisons (KubeVirt `frozen_difference`, the Redfish firmware convergence). These are its own observations and were not verified. [LNG-09](#lng-09) covers the verified part of that concern.

### 8.5 What to change

This is the audit's proposal, smallest change first within each step. Each step edits text in specs/architecture.md#language-responsibility or the reference it names.

1. Add a row for Python in the executable, and extend the language-row test's source roots and the floor and sites checks to `internal/**/*.py` ([LNG-01](#lng-01)).
2. Narrow the seam wording:
   - Change the Python Never cell to "judges whether evidence proves a block's declared postcondition", and call the Ceph stage checks "stage conditions" ([LNG-09](#lng-09), [ARC-64](#arc-64)).
   - Limit the Go Never cell to a managed component's native output ([LNG-03](#lng-03)).
   - Change the Go question to "which effect runs, in what order across blocks", and send repository tools to the paragraph below the table ([LNG-02](#lng-02)).
3. Add filter and callback plugins to the Python row's Holds. State that parsing native output into a closed structure belongs in Python. Add filters and the callback to the controller site. State that every module utility keeps the managed-host floor ([LNG-04](#lng-04), [LNG-13](#lng-13)).
4. Under the table, add one sentence naming the shell exceptions in a list that only shrinks, and have python.md link to it ([LNG-12](#lng-12)). Add one sentence on what a Make recipe may hold ([LNG-05](#lng-05)).
5. Add a parity sentence: a constant that Python duplicates from Go names its Go owner, and a test holds the two equal ([LNG-10](#lng-10)). Limit "canonical JSON" to the Go form, and name the ASCII form that adapter records use ([LNG-11](#lng-11)).
6. Align the references:
   - Scope the POSIX sh rule in formatting.md ([LNG-06](#lng-06)).
   - Replace the restated prohibitions with links ([LNG-08](#lng-08)).
   - Make architecture.md's rule for which imports a shipped worker may use match python.md ([SKL-04](#skl-04)).
   - Add .claude/rules/scripts.md for scripts/ and e2e/ ([LNG-07](#lng-07)).
7. Apply the read-only allowlist to the `read` verb as well as `observe` ([ARC-66](#arc-66)).

### 9.2 The lifecycle engine: operations, attempts, continuation, removal, comparison, safety gates

**Verdict.** The engine's safety core is sound. The core rules: an unknown outcome is never read as absence, a removal is planned from the frozen plan, an operation owns every block it started, every transition re-proves its state under the exclusive lock, and continuation is keyed on contract digests, not on automation bytes. Three rules are not sound as written, and each needs a small edit. A loosened ownership observation can reach a destroy because nothing on the removal side detects it ([REC-07](#rec-07)). An owner-approved operator upgrade decays into a destroy remedy ([REC-13](#rec-13)). The `context update` warning contradicts the additive apply ([REC-03](#rec-03)). Two Medium rules are also unsafe: the matching-backup restore remedy ([REC-32](#rec-32)) and the discard offered for an unreadable setup record ([REC-72](#rec-72)). The other defects are drift and incompleteness. Restated rules have fallen out of step with their owners, lists that claim to be complete are not, and the newest journey (additive apply, GitOps handoff) is under-specified. Almost every fix is a spec-text edit. [CLI-21](#cli-21) adds an output field, [CLI-10](#cli-10) may change an exit status, and [REC-71](#rec-71) adds an API invariant.

### 9.3 Contexts, the store, locking and crash consistency

Verdict: the durable-state mechanics are sound at their core. The lock hierarchy cannot deadlock. Every interrupted transition of context state has an order and a command that finishes it; the controller's first binding is the exception ([REC-56](#rec-56)). Deletion never removes what it cannot verify. The defects are at the edges. Three are High. A power command from another context can cut power to a server that a `bmc:` reservation protects ([REC-10](#rec-10)). Two fresh-store remedies still tell the operator to remove the store by hand, which bypasses `controller uninstall` ([REC-05](#rec-05)). Security restates a cancellation carve-out that the runner's owner does not have ([REC-04](#rec-04)). The Medium findings are underspecified points of the crash and lock protocol: no stated fsync point, unbounded reader holds, a first-binding crash window with no exit, and a restore remedy that silently rolls back every context. Each fix is a sentence or a paragraph.

The scenarios that hold rest on checked passages. A fresh apply claims its operation directory before it raises evidence, and re-proves that evidence before it registers (state-reconciliation.md:229-247). An attempt record is published before its block record (state-reconciliation.md:1440-1463). Custody precedes the work-area inverse (state-reconciliation.md:738-766). A lost index releases evidence only when no `blocks/` lists anything (state-reconciliation.md:122-146). A durable releasing mark guards bridge removal (infrastructure-services.md:133). Root-lock timeouts record `failed` or `unknown` by whether an effect ran (contexts.md:440-446).

### 9.4 Security, secrets and the controller host

**Verdict.** The written security model is sound, and it is among the strongest parts of the corpus. The attacker model is explicit (specs/security.md:48-82). Remote principals have bounded trust (specs/security.md:84-103). Binding is immutable and split into classes (specs/secrets.md:315-335). Supply-chain widenings are named (specs/security.md:775-783). Two High findings break promises the pages make. First, uninstall can remove packages that were present before Bootwright ([REC-08](#rec-08)). Second, renewing or replacing a Secret can silently orphan the only copy of a disk recovery passphrase ([REC-12](#rec-12)). On the secrets side, the reveal and confirmation paths are weaker than the input path. The input side guards sudo's input log, but no reveal guards sudo's output log ([CLI-26](#cli-26)), and no confirmation defines "interactive" ([CLI-27](#cli-27)). Every correction proposed below is S or M effort. Most are spec text only. [REC-08](#rec-08) and [REC-37](#rec-37) change the stored receipt, and five corrections change CLI behavior ([REC-12](#rec-12), [CLI-08](#cli-08), [CLI-22](#cli-22), [CLI-26](#cli-26), [CLI-29](#cli-29)).

- dnf runs within the host's own repositories and signers, and never with `--nogpgcheck` or `--allowerasing` (specs/controller.md:293-303).

### 9.5 Substrates, operating systems and infrastructure services

Verdict: the rules on physical effects are rigorous, and the weak points are where pages meet. Inside one page, effects carry a proof, an unanswered read stays unknown, and a foreign object refuses. The defects are at the edges. Cross-context coordination of one physical server or one SSH host has holes ([REC-09](#rec-09), [REC-10](#rec-10), [REC-74](#rec-74), [REC-41](#rec-41)). D239's root-disk forms and the optional erase root never reached the owners of disk safety ([API-03](#api-03), [REC-02](#rec-02)). Managed-OS records the before-state too late, so two interruption windows can be read as nothing installed, and the retry installs again ([REC-11](#rec-11), [REC-46](#rec-46)). The only copy of the recovery passphrase can be replaced without a warning ([REC-12](#rec-12)). Network convergence has no verified finding against it. All of these are corrections to spec text. [REC-10](#rec-10) and [REC-41](#rec-41) add a check or a key, and [REC-46](#rec-46) optionally adds a record, inside mechanisms that already exist.

What holds, with the passages checked in the snapshot:

- The realized target is settled once and frozen. Every consumer hands its arm to one machine-port dispatcher, which fails closed (substrates.md:43-56).
- The bare-metal target proof needs the ComputerSystem identity and the complete MAC set. A partial inventory reads unknown (substrates.md:774-814).
- One MAC-set predicate serves every proof of a physical machine, the installer's included (state-reconciliation.md:2446-2450).
- The firmware sequence compares current and pending values, uses a one-time BiosSetup override and If-Match, and always sends ForceOff after a power-on (substrates.md:916-962).
- No power command can stop the controller host. The controller Machine is refused by name, and so is any target that reports the controller's UUID or MAC (substrates.md:1567-1570; cli.md:1643-1652).
- Network convergence relies on NetworkManager's checkpoint rollback, and the checkpoint outlasts the apply and reconnect budgets (managed-os.md:768-834). An interruption table derives the next step at every cut point (managed-os.md:896-908).
- On bare metal a disk is named only by a durable identity, and %pre proves it again with fail-closed behaviour (managed-os.md:1256-1326).
- The reservation keys have typed classes, each with one conflict relation, and a durable releasing marker (infrastructure-services.md:125-207). A known-hosts entry is parsed the way OpenSSH reads it, and no ambient SSH configuration is consulted (infrastructure-services.md:86-111).

Findings from these lanes that belong to other families appear in their own sections: [REC-70](#rec-70) and [REC-136](#rec-136) (contexts), [REC-71](#rec-71), [REC-137](#rec-137) and [REC-138](#rec-138) (Ceph), [REC-72](#rec-72) (controller state).

Each correction above is the audit's proposal. Each is the smallest text change that resolves the finding it names, and none adds a compatibility path.

Lane X07 walked 20 physical-safety and controller-host scenarios against the text. By its own reading, 13 are safe as written:

- A kernel name moves to another disk between boots.
- A root is duplicated, multipath, or has a cloned serial.
- A `clearOnInstall` target is really the root.
- A device-mapper stack spans an undeclared disk.
- A BMC address now fronts another server.
- A firmware run is killed while the machine is in setup.
- The controller host is declared as another bare-metal Machine.
- The controller Machine is stopped or erased.
- A managed network would cut off the controller.
- Destroy runs from an unbound host.
- An erase is interrupted.
- A context name is reused after an orphaned erase.
- An erase serial matches two disks.

These are the lane's unverified observations, not findings. The scenarios that a verified finding backs:

| Scenario | Outcome the text determines | Finding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No root hint on a physical worker | Two answers: refuse, or erase the derived `bootVolume` | [API-03](#api-03) |
| An erase policy that lists only data disks | One page requires the root, the other keeps it | [REC-02](#rec-02) |
| Erase target replaced after installation | Refuses with nothing written; no next action | [REC-67](#rec-67) |
| A member's `MACAddress` differs from its `PermanentMACAddress` | Property unspecified; the adapter takes the union, so the proof refuses | [REC-66](#rec-66) |
| Firmware enforce refused, then the context is destroyed | Override and pending settings stay; neither the remedy nor destroy says so | [REC-43](#rec-43) |
| Context A force-restarts a server that context B is installing | A's proof passes; B's claim is not consulted | [REC-10](#rec-10) |
| One server reached by DNS name and by IP, with no UUID | Two `bmc:` keys; installation, power and media proceed in both contexts | [REC-41](#rec-41) |

The lane marks the last two scenarios unsafe, and both let two contexts drive one server. In the second, both contexts can also install it. The audit proposes [REC-10](#rec-10)'s refusal as the first change. It does not close the second scenario: with no UUID, the two address spellings give two `bmc:` keys, so the check finds no conflict. [REC-41](#rec-41)'s `bmc-mac:` fallback key closes it.

### 9.6 Container clusters, storage and add-ons

**Verdict.** The destructive paths in these pages are specified with care. Identity is bound before any effect, ownership is proved by a recorded uid or FSID and never by a name, refusal tables are held by tests, and erase is bound to receipts. One rule is unsafe and blocks: the OpenShift observation reads a powered-off, installed cluster as "no effect", and a retry then reinstalls over it ([REC-01](#rec-01)). One High contradiction sits on the erase path ([REC-02](#rec-02)), and one on the physical root selector ([API-08](#api-08)). Most of the other defects are drift. Later decisions (D199 placement, D239 optional root, pushed delivery) reached some sections and not others ([REC-50](#rec-50), [API-52](#api-52), [REC-02](#rec-02), [API-08](#api-08), [REC-49](#rec-49), [ARC-20](#arc-20)). Most fixes are spec-text edits. [ARC-22](#arc-22) needs a design change. [ARC-24](#arc-24) and [REC-71](#rec-71) change the API, [REC-15](#rec-15) and [REC-60](#rec-60) add a CLI warning, [REC-61](#rec-61) touches stored state, and [ARC-21](#arc-21) moves rules between capabilities.

| Rule family | Where | Verdict | Findings |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

These passages are right, and they are the model for the fixes:

- Refusal rows carry their reason and remedy verbatim. A named test holds the table equal to `Unsupported`, and a row lifts only in the commit of the item that delivers what it refuses (specs/openshift-clusters.md:108-110, 157-166).
- A booted work area is never rebuilt, which protects the only administrator credential (specs/openshift-clusters.md:487-502). Completion is proved from the cluster's own ClusterVersion and from a client-certificate identity (specs/openshift-clusters.md:931-973).
- The FSID is bound before any remote effect and is never derived from a name (specs/ceph.md:772-785). Dynamic selectors are bound before the first destructive write (specs/ceph.md:1167-1173). Retirement needs matched erase receipts (specs/ceph.md:1286-1299).
- Package trust has one anchor and no fallback (specs/ceph.md:196-217). Stretch activation runs in recorded stages, and an interrupted stage never repeats (specs/ceph.md:623-687).
- Every native create writes an attempt record first. Adoption needs that record plus the frozen shape (specs/ceph.md:1438-1455).
- Add-ons are create-only, with approvals as the one exception (specs/add-ons.md:246-248). The approval patch tests the uid and the CSV list (specs/add-ons.md:328-339). The replacement chain is proved from surviving objects (specs/add-ons.md:471-507).

| Erase policy must or need not name the root | state-reconciliation.md:2490-2492; ceph.md:1277-1278; api/machines.md:750 | Contradicted | One destroy is admitted with the root kept, or refused, depending on the page read | Follow D239: the root is covered only "when the policy names it" | [REC-02](#rec-02) |

| Drift is reported and nothing repairs it | state-reconciliation.md:2038-2040 | Contradicted | An NFS export and a subvolume group are re-applied by the next apply | State the exception; one table: kind, drift outcome, owning rule | [REC-52](#rec-52) |
| Booted-mark, Evidence and Replay assume a published image | openshift-clusters.md:493-499, 572-584 | Gap | A push-only replay has no stated availability test | One "image is available" predicate | [REC-49](#rec-49) |
