**Unknown outcomes: what lane X02 walked.** The lane walked 20 failure scenarios. By its own count, 14 have a safe, determined outcome. Typed failures keep the effect `unknown` (specs/state-reconciliation.md:613-636). The FSID is never re-allocated on a lost reply (specs/ceph.md:772-779). Managed OS records a before-state ahead of its own power-off (specs/managed-os.md:666-683). Five scenarios are unsafe or undetermined, and one is a safe reinstall that the specs describe wrongly:

- An installed, powered-off OpenShift cluster reads as no effect and is reinstalled ([REC-01](#rec-01)).
- A destroy's removal check records `no-effect` on the apply's block from a media-only read, and that label survives a refused destroy ([REC-130](#rec-130)).
- An expired boot budget is `unknown` in substrates.md and `failed` in openshift-clusters.md ([REC-58](#rec-58)).
- A Ceph readiness timeout gives two outcomes ([REC-57](#rec-57)).
- A managed-OS destroy leaves an interrupted attempt's inserted media, and an imported certificate the Machine asked to remove, on the BMC with no report ([REC-44](#rec-44)).
- An installer power-off before the marker proof reads as "never installed" ([REC-46](#rec-46)).

Proposal: one rule across capabilities. An observation reads positive no effect only when the attempt's durable preparation records show the effect never began. It resolves [REC-01](#rec-01) and gives an optional fix for [REC-46](#rec-46), whose required fix is a wording change and an interruption row. It extends the Q66 pattern that is already in place.

**Removal: what lane X04 walked.** The lane walked 20 destroy scenarios. By its own count, 11 have a safe, determined outcome. Ownership covers every started block (specs/state-reconciliation.md:1652-1668). State is re-proved under the exclusive lock (specs/state-reconciliation.md:1908-1930). Erase binds identity end to end (specs/state-reconciliation.md:2510-2591). The open cases:

- The root-disk rule has two answers ([REC-02](#rec-02)).
- Physical Ceph without erase coverage has no exit but orphan context deletion, and no plan-time warning ([REC-15](#rec-15)).
- A surviving physical cluster loses its only kubeconfig at destroy ([REC-60](#rec-60)).
- A reinstalled, registered guest records unregistration complete while the service consumer remains ([REC-61](#rec-61)).
- A lost `mutation.json` forces abandonment although the operation records still prove ownership ([REC-132](#rec-132)).

Three other cases are not findings: a gone provided tiebreaker (tracked by B938), a gone KubeVirt host cluster (decided), and re-init after orphan deletion (tracked by B568).

## 10. Spec corpus structure and maintenance for agent efficiency

### 10.1 Verdict

The harness works for coding agents: a typical task loads 25k to 38k tokens of a corpus of about 1.25M. The one-owner-per-fact model is right, but no rule or test holds it, and no rule says the owner wins a disagreement ([COR-85](#cor-85)). Its cost is drift: by the auditors' estimate, about 127 KB of restated rule text across 14 sweeps, and most High contradictions here are a copy that lagged its owner ([API-03](#api-03), [REC-02](#rec-02), [REC-03](#rec-03), [REC-05](#rec-05), [DOC-01](#doc-01)). The index and budgets route well. Their gaps are whole-page rows ([COR-26](#cor-26)), an unbounded milestone read clause ([COR-30](#cor-30)) and exception tables that never expire ([COR-28](#cor-28)). The ID rules are sound, with one collision ([COR-59](#cor-59)). Milestone pages do not keep live work apart from history ([COR-13](#cor-13), [COR-66](#cor-66), [COR-67](#cor-67), [COR-68](#cor-68)). "Not yet met" is the weakest link: after in-tree delivery a present line can be stale, and an absent line proves nothing ([COR-02](#cor-02), [COR-03](#cor-03)). Knowledge leaks rules and procedure both ways and has no retirement rule ([COR-23](#cor-23), [COR-35](#cor-35), [COR-37](#cor-37)).

### 10.2 What the fitness suite already holds

All tests are in `test/architecture/`. The table names only the checks that hold a corpus convention.

| Convention | Held by | Is it the right check? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Always-read files stay small | `TestDocsStayWithinByteBudgets` (`docsByteBudgets`) | Yes. But three files that every edit must read have no budget ([COR-25](#cor-25)). |
| Milestone openings stay small | same, `#opening` keys | It measures only up to the first H2. The m2 to m4 Submilestones H2s (26 to 52 KB) sit outside it ([COR-68](#cor-68), [COR-78](#cor-78)). |
| An H2 section is at most 24 KiB | `TestDocsSpecSectionsStayWithinBudgets` | The rule is right. Its 9 exceptions date from 2026-10-27, and their owner B965 is parked, so for the largest loads the exceptions are now the rule ([COR-28](#cor-28)). |
| A leaf is at most 8 KiB | `TestDocsSpecLeavesStayWithinBudgets` | Wrong unit. It measures a leaf up to the next heading, but an anchor loads the whole subtree ([COR-32](#cor-32)). It has 18 exceptions under the same B965. |
| Every spec page is within two links of the index | `TestDocsEverySpecPageIsReachableFromTheIndex` | Yes. |
| Normative pages gain no delivery history | `TestDocsNormativePagesCiteNoNewDeliveryHistory` | Yes for specs. Delivery state in docs/ and delivery logs in milestone item detail sit outside it ([DOC-19](#doc-19), [COR-13](#cor-13)). |
| Not yet met links an open item | `TestDocsNotYetMetNamesAnUndeliveredItem` | Wrong predicate. It accepts "awaiting operator acceptance" ([COR-02](#cor-02)). It proves the item exists, not that the item owns the gap ([COR-05](#cor-05)). It misses markers that do not open a paragraph ([COR-06](#cor-06)). It cannot see a line that is missing ([COR-03](#cor-03)). |
| Links, anchors and cited paths resolve | `TestDocsLinksAndAnchorsResolve`, `TestDocsRepositoryPathsExist` | It strips `:line`, so line-number citations drift unseen: about 101 of them in backlog.md ([COR-09](#cor-09)). |
| Cited tests exist | `TestDocsCitedTestsExist` | Wrong scope. It keeps history live: 94 names pinned in delivered.md ([COR-58](#cor-58)). It misses unbackticked names ([COR-49](#cor-49)). |
| Decision links open their own entry | `TestDocsDecisionLinksTargetTheirOwnEntry` | Yes. |
| Every effectful command has an ask rule | `TestDocsAskRulesCoverEveryEffectfulCommand` | Right shape. But its `askRuleNoAsk` table exempts irreversible local commands such as `context delete --purge --allow-orphans` ([COR-01](#cor-01)). |
| Specialization catalog equals the registries | `TestDocsVersionSpecializationCatalogMatchesRegistries` | It forces table rows past the 2,000-character read limit ([COR-38](#cor-38)). |
| Examples are indexed | `TestDocsExamplesAreIndexed` | Yes. Example coverage of the kind catalog is held by no test ([DOC-28](#doc-28)). |
| One owner per fact | none | It is held by discipline only. No rule says the owner wins when a restatement disagrees with it ([COR-85](#cor-85)). |

Budgets only fall and fail when outgrown (test/architecture/docs_test.go:22-43, test/architecture/docs_gates_test.go:136-198). The Not yet met matcher is precise about what it tests, and tests itself (test/architecture/docs_test.go:713-849).

### 10.3 The retrieval path, quantified

Lane H02 counted the loads for eight tasks, with tokens taken as bytes / 4. "Always loaded" is AGENTS.md plus CLAUDE.md. "Routing" is the index, the milestone parts, the per-edit skills and the rules files. "Owning" is the spec text the task needs.

| Task | Always loaded | Routing | Owning content | Total tokens | Largest single load |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 Optional Machine field | 632 | 14,564 | 16,047 | 31,243 | api/machines `## Machine`, 6,575 |
| 2 Ceph adapter role defect | 632 | 13,429 | 11,539 | 25,600 | ceph.md Bootstrap, 6,123 |
| 3 CLI flag | 632 | 14,564 | 19,826 | 35,022 | architecture `## Go package structure`, 7,243 |
| 4 Close item, write record | 632 | 9,805 | 3,074 | 13,511 | milestones.md, 2,137 |
| 5 Built-in add-on package | 632 | 16,268 | 18,871 | 35,771 | add-on-coverage Built-in, 6,131 |
| 6 Lifecycle refusal message | 632 | 14,564 | 13,020 | 28,216 | state-recon Continuation, 5,444 |
| 7 Infrastructure service kind | 632 | 19,271 | 17,829 | 37,731 | api/infrastructure-services (whole), 4,548 |
| 8 One spec sentence | 632 | 8,116 | 1,000 | 9,747 | verification.md, 1,637 |

What drives the cost, by lane H02's own count:

- Routing is 37% to 83% of every total. The per-edit procedure stack (code-implementation, verification, git integration and the Go references) is about 8.9k tokens. That is 25% to 28% of a Go task and 58% of a one-sentence edit. Three of its files have no budget ([COR-25](#cor-25)).
- The largest single loads are sections on the exception list (Machine, Go package structure, Continuation and removal) or pages the index routes whole ([COR-26](#cor-26), [COR-28](#cor-28)).
- One index row sends an agent to a 28,971-byte section when a 1,267-byte leaf exists. That costs about 6.9k extra tokens, about a fifth of task 3 ([COR-27](#cor-27)).
- None of this counts a literal reading of "and what they link" in AGENTS.md. Followed literally, it pulls in whole linked pages, about 1 MB for M2 ([COR-30](#cor-30)). The rule itself is restated in four versions ([COR-24](#cor-24)).

The load buys precision when the index names an anchor (tasks 2 and 6). It is coarse when the index names a whole page or an exempt section (tasks 1, 3 and 7). The router is small: AGENTS.md is 2,516 bytes against a 2,516-byte budget (AGENTS.md:1-47), and the anchored table of large domains routes to leaves (specs/index.md:36-47). The index has no row for the extension contract, which is the owner's main growth path ([COR-27](#cor-27)).

The pattern is the same in every sweep. The owner page is right, and the copy lags behind a recent decision. D239's root-volume change never reached the managed-OS and disk-safety pages ([API-03](#api-03), [REC-02](#rec-02)). The 1-minute lock wait and D244's uninstall never reached controller.md or the controller-record remedies ([ARC-08](#arc-08), [REC-05](#rec-05)). The additive apply never reached the warning that context update prints ([REC-03](#rec-03)). Numbers rarely drift: the bounds table ties each row to its Go constant under a test (specs/contexts.md:585-625), and lanes D03 and D10 found no numeric drift. Prose rules drift. The corpus states the one-owner rule (specs/index.md:51-52), but it never says that the owner wins a disagreement ([COR-85](#cor-85)).

### 10.5 The milestone corpus

The milestone pages hold 2.03 MB, which is 40% of the 5.0 MB the audit measured. The normative specs, including deferred/, hold 2.22 MB (44%). Knowledge holds 0.55 MB (11%).

| Page | Bytes | Share of corpus | Live rule or open work (lane estimate) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| delivered.md | 799,029 | 16% | 0% to 10% per chunk (M06 to M19) |
| backlog.md: Parked | 261,266 | 5% | 85% to 97% (M01 to M04) |
| backlog.md: Audit remediation + Retired | 62,092 | 1% | ~25%. Answered Q62 to Q118 are ~60% of the chunk (M05) |
| backlog.md: Decisions | 293,970 | 6% | the decision log, not estimated here |
| m1.md | 98,774 | 2% | ~70% (lines 1 to 842), ~63% (lines 843 to 1477) |
| m2.md | 203,747 | 4% | 34% to 75% by chunk. Item detail lines 581 to 1504 are ~34% (M23) |
| m3.md | 138,512 | 3% | 64% to 85% |
| m4.md | 161,834 | 3% | ~80% to 85% |
| m5 to m7, milestones.md | 18,414 | &lt;1% | ~100%, except m5 and m6, which are retirement history |

The guidance tells agents to search delivered.md and backlog.md by ID and never read them whole (.agents/skills/milestones-and-knowledge/SKILL.md:17-19), so their size costs little until a search hits them. The cost falls on the item sections an agent must read. There, by the lanes' estimates, delivered-in-tree narrative, test inventories and restated protocol make up 15% to 66% of the bytes ([COR-13](#cor-13), [COR-81](#cor-81)). Inside delivered.md, guard-test lists take 20% to 29% of several chunks, and restated spec rules take up to 53% of one ([COR-52](#cor-52), [COR-60](#cor-60)).

The recurring defects, grouped:

- **Stale delivery state or routing:** [COR-12](#cor-12), [COR-19](#cor-19), [COR-42](#cor-42), [COR-44](#cor-44), [COR-72](#cor-72), [COR-74](#cor-74), [COR-14](#cor-14).
- **Exit evidence that demands a superseded or conflicting rule:** [COR-15](#cor-15), [COR-17](#cor-17), [COR-82](#cor-82). [COR-16](#cor-16) narrows destroy confirmation on a clause that no decision holds.
- **Rules or facts restated in items or records, several already drifted:** [COR-13](#cor-13), [COR-20](#cor-20), [COR-21](#cor-21), [COR-52](#cor-52), [COR-75](#cor-75), [COR-76](#cor-76), [COR-79](#cor-79).
- **Normative rules that live only in history:** [COR-10](#cor-10), [COR-11](#cor-11), [COR-55](#cor-55), [COR-84](#cor-84).
- **Breaches of the record shape:** [COR-40](#cor-40), [COR-41](#cor-41), [COR-46](#cor-46), [COR-56](#cor-56), [COR-59](#cor-59), [COR-62](#cor-62), [COR-63](#cor-63), [COR-77](#cor-77), [COR-83](#cor-83), [COR-31](#cor-31), [COR-51](#cor-51).
- **Citations that resolve nowhere or to the wrong lines:** [COR-09](#cor-09), [COR-47](#cor-47), [COR-49](#cor-49), [COR-50](#cor-50), [COR-53](#cor-53).

The authorization and ID rules hold up well. Scope keeps definition apart from authorization (specs/milestones.md:39-69). The item-state vocabulary is exact (specs/milestones.md:71-100). B numbers encode nothing and never change (specs/milestones.md:102-125). The pages fail on upkeep after writing, as the groups above show. Lane M02 notes that D116 keeps wording follow-ups parked, so a false sentence outlives the slice that found it. That is the owner's decision, and the proposals below respect it.

### 10.6 The "Not yet met" convention

Lane H03 found 53 spec lines with the marker; every cited item exists.

| Problem | Lines | Finding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Item already delivered in-tree, so the line is stale (B721, B67, B760) | 3 | [COR-02](#cor-02) |
| Item no longer owns the gap (B79 split to B1183; B1104) | 2 | [COR-05](#cor-05) |
| Non-goal written as an unmet rule ("is parked as", B561) | 1 | [COR-34](#cor-34) |
| Marker mid-line or in bold, so the check never sees it; one has no link | 6 | [COR-06](#cor-06) |
| False sentence with no line at all (B576, B571) | 2 | [COR-03](#cor-03) |
| Prose bypasses ("refused until B90", "Refused today (B99)", availability claims) | 13 in lane H03's table; 3 confirmed | [COR-33](#cor-33) |
| Unrealized rows marked "none tracked" | 3 | [API-34](#api-34) |

So 12 of the 53 lines (23%) are stale, mis-owned or unchecked. Refusal tables, the unrealized table and "lifts" lists also state unmet behaviour, but they are present-tense and test-held. The defect is prose that bypasses the form and implies availability outside any check ([COR-33](#cor-33)). The corpus names milestones as the owner of delivery state (specs/index.md:49-58).

An agent cannot answer "is this rule implemented" from the convention alone. A missing line does not mean yes ([COR-03](#cor-03)). A present line can be stale once its item reaches in-tree delivery ([COR-02](#cor-02)). In practice the agent must also read the item's row and section, about 1.3 KB per check by lane H02's median, and even then it learns delivery state rather than whether the code meets the rule. The audit proposes two cheap fixes: a sharper predicate and a retirement step at in-tree delivery (10.8, item 4).

### 10.7 The knowledge base

The knowledge base has 67 pages and 554 KB, including its 36 KB index. Lane H04 read the index and ten pages (about 98 KB). Of those ten, three are lessons only. Three mix in rules or procedure. Three are history or a dated audit, and one is a test-held registry.

What works:

- The index is a search surface keyed by symptom and error text, and it states that specs win when the two disagree (.agents/knowledge/index.md:3-5).
- The specialization catalog is held equal to the code (.agents/knowledge/version-specializations.md:12-17).
- History pages say that they are history (.agents/knowledge/native-root-reason-change.md:3-12).
- Evidence boundaries stop synthetic runs from being promoted (.agents/knowledge/ibm-ceph-version-constraints.md:274-283).
- Lessons follow a symptom, cause and fix shape (.agents/knowledge/installation-completion-proof.md:8-78).

What leaks:

- A dated audit with drifted citations is kept as a live page ([COR-07](#cor-07)).
- A continuation lesson disagrees with the Ceph recovery table on bootstrap attempts ([COR-08](#cor-08)).
- A skill hands its procedure to a knowledge page ([COR-35](#cor-35)).
- Two procedures give `bootwright apply` as an unqualified step without naming who runs it ([COR-36](#cor-36)).
- "Retire" is never defined, so a history page is indexed under "Desired-state API" ([COR-37](#cor-37)).
- The catalog test forces rows too long to read ([COR-38](#cor-38)).
- One lesson is misfiled ([COR-39](#cor-39)).

Lanes outside H04 found stale or spec-level content on other knowledge pages ([COR-22](#cor-22), [COR-23](#cor-23), [COR-88](#cor-88) to [COR-92](#cor-92)). Lane H04 observes that no gate checks knowledge pages beyond their links, paths and the catalog.

### 10.8 Proposed restructuring

These are the audit's proposals. Each is the smallest change that resolves its findings, and none removes a rule.

1. **Define the agent effect ban by effect, not by an inline list.** In AGENTS.md, point to the catalog's Effects column, name `controller rebind`, and cover native effects reached directly (Redfish, virsh, oc, cephadm). Add ask rules for the four irreversible local commands (context delete, secret delete, secret encryption rotate, media delete) and move them out of `askRuleNoAsk`. Reword the two knowledge procedures so the operator runs apply. Tokens: none saved; this closes a safety gap. Precision: one list instead of two that disagree. Resolves [COR-01](#cor-01), [COR-36](#cor-36), [COR-90](#cor-90).
2. **Bound the milestone read and keep it in one place.** In AGENTS.md, change "and what they link" to "the linked sections they need; search delivered.md and backlog.md by ID". The three other copies become links. Saves: the unbounded whole-page reads (about 250k tokens for M2 on a literal reading, lane H02). Precision: the same sections stay reachable. Resolves [COR-30](#cor-30), [COR-24](#cor-24).
3. **Add three sentences and two rows to the index.** The sentences: (a) a whole-page row means "list its H2 headings and load only the matching ones"; (b) the owner wins over a restatement; (c) the Claude-only convention moves into Conventions. The rows: one for the extension contract, and one KubeVirt/vSphere substrate route. Retarget the finding-code row to its leaf. Saves: about 6.9k tokens on task 3, and a whole-page load on task 7. The basis is lane H02's byte counts. Precision: anchors replace pages. Resolves [COR-26](#cor-26), [COR-27](#cor-27), [COR-85](#cor-85), [SKL-12](#skl-12). The index sits at its byte budget, so admit this as routing growth.
4. **Sharpen the Not yet met check.** Flag an item whose Delivery cell is "awaiting operator acceptance". Flag any marker that does not open a paragraph. Retire or re-point lines in the commit that delivers or splits an item. Add the two missing lines, rewrite the non-goal line and the three prose bypasses, and give the three "none tracked" rows an item. Saves: the item read on each check (about 1.3 KB, lane H02's median B section). Precision: a present line becomes trustworthy. Resolves [COR-02](#cor-02), [COR-03](#cor-03), [COR-05](#cor-05), [COR-06](#cor-06), [COR-33](#cor-33), [COR-34](#cor-34), [API-34](#api-34).
5. **Turn each High drift's restatement into a link to its owner, in the same change.** Saves: part of the ~127 KB that agents read twice, and the grep-for-copies step in every spec edit. Precision: one answer per question. Resolves [API-03](#api-03), [API-04](#api-04), [REC-02](#rec-02) to [REC-06](#rec-06), [DOC-01](#doc-01) to [DOC-03](#doc-03), and the Medium drifts in 10.4 as their pages are next touched.
6. **Fix the budget units.** Measure an H3 with its whole subtree. Budget the three unbudgeted per-edit files. Make B965's text name the map instead of a count. When to split the nine sections stays the owner's call. Saves: once the sections are split, the largest single loads (21 to 29 KB) fall to budgeted leaves. Resolves [COR-25](#cor-25), [COR-28](#cor-28), [COR-32](#cor-32).
7. **Treat delivered.md as a dated record.** Exempt it from the cited-test check. Its header says that figures and test names are as delivered. New records link the spec instead of restating it, and name their guards by package. Saves: 20% to 29% of each new record's bytes. Precision: the specs stay sole owner, and the normative bits found only there move to their specs first ([COR-10](#cor-10), [COR-11](#cor-11), [COR-55](#cor-55), [COR-84](#cor-84)). Resolves [COR-49](#cor-49), [COR-52](#cor-52), [COR-54](#cor-54), [COR-58](#cor-58), [COR-60](#cor-60).
8. **Keep item detail to outcome, exit evidence, remaining work and a delivered-record link.** Fold the narrative into delivered.md. Move m1's eleven open-item sections back under Item detail. Compress answered Q and OD rows to the question and its answer, keeping the meaning of the letters that D183 and D160 record. Add a check that refuses "Delivered in-tree" or "Closed (D" paragraphs on milestone pages. For [COR-13](#cor-13) the fix is narrower: replace the restated protocol with links to the owning spec sections, and drop the version moves and test inventories. Saves: 15% to 66% of each item read (lanes M23 and M31), about 13.7 KB on m1, up to about 28 KB on m2 and part of the 37.5 KB backlog Q table. Resolves [COR-13](#cor-13), [COR-45](#cor-45), [COR-66](#cor-66), [COR-67](#cor-67), [COR-68](#cor-68), [COR-81](#cor-81), and the stale-state group in 10.5.
9. **Cite by anchor and symbol, never by `:line`, on milestone pages, and optionally add a check for it.** In the same pass, re-point the cross-links that resolve nowhere or to the wrong table. Saves: reads of the wrong target. Resolves [COR-09](#cor-09), [COR-47](#cor-47), [COR-53](#cor-53).
10. **Give knowledge a retirement rule.** Retiring deletes the page and its row. Delete the superseded API page. Bring the dated audit current in place. Move the specialization procedure into extend-implementation. Split the Ceph recovery row and link it from the continuation page. Keep each catalog cell to one key, and move the misfiled lesson. Saves: misrouted hits on generic terms. Resolves [COR-07](#cor-07), [COR-08](#cor-08), [COR-35](#cor-35), [COR-37](#cor-37), [COR-38](#cor-38), [COR-39](#cor-39).

## 11. Skills and agent harness

### 11.1 Current state

The harness is small, and tests hold most of it in place. The skills, references, wrappers, rules, root files and hook and permission files add up to 77,482 bytes. Only about 3.9 KB of that loads on every session: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and the six skill descriptions (lane G03). Tests already hold four things:

- wrapper parity (.agents/skills/index.md:3-10);
- byte budgets that ratchet down, so a budget can never sit far above its file (test/architecture/docs_test.go:22-43);
- the ask list, checked against the command catalog (.claude/settings.json:30-51; test/architecture/docs_test.go:1067-1091);
- an end-of-turn hook that both runtimes share and that only advises (.agents/skills/code-implementation/references/verification.md:65-80).

Three defects bear on safety:

- The effect ban in AGENTS.md is an inline list. It leaves out `controller rebind`, and nothing decides whether irreversible local commands such as `context delete --purge --allow-orphans` fall under it. The ask-rule test exempts those commands through askRuleNoAsk, so no prompt fires ([COR-01](#cor-01), High).
- Codex has no tracked command guard ([SKL-01](#skl-01)).
- The git patterns miss the `-C` form and a `--force` placed at the end ([SKL-02](#skl-02)).

The other problems are drift: copies of rules that live elsewhere have started to disagree with them. No skill needs to be removed.

### 11.2 Proposed portfolio

The audit proposes keeping the six skills and adding two references. It proposes no new top-level skill. The verified recommendations for audits ([SKL-16](#skl-16)) and slice planning ([SKL-17](#skl-17)) both ask for a reference or a section, not a skill. The index keeps a provisional skill only while a measured comparison shows it beats a reference linked from an existing skill (.agents/skills/index.md:21-23). The budgets below are the audit's proposal: each is close to today's size, under the existing ratchet.

### 11.3 One contract for Claude Code and Codex

Each runtime cell gives the documentation page that lane G02 checked it against, in brackets. "Unverified" means lane G02 found no page that states it, or the claim rests only on outside runtime behaviour. The audit builds nothing on an unverified cell.

| Mechanism | Claude Code | Codex | Repository setup | Works as intended? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Root instructions | CLAUDE.md, with `@` imports expanded [memory page] | AGENTS.md, from the root down to cwd, 32 KiB cap [agents-md page] | CLAUDE.md:1 imports AGENTS.md | Yes |
| Skill discovery | `.claude/skills/<n>/SKILL.md`; may be a symlink [skills page] | `.agents/skills`; symlinks followed [build-skills page] | Canonical skills plus wrappers, held by a test | Yes, at the cost of one extra read per load ([SKL-13](#skl-13)) |
| Skill references | Read on demand [skills page] | On-demand loading: unverified | Relative links | Yes for Claude Code; not established for Codex |
| Path-scoped rules | `.claude/rules` with `paths:`, matched against the session's project [memory page] | No equivalent [agents-md page] | Three rule files | Partly: [SKL-09](#skl-09), [SKL-12](#skl-12), [SKL-18](#skl-18) |
| Stop hook | `hooks.Stop`; `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` stays at the original root [hooks page] | `.codex/hooks.json`, needs trust, runs in cwd [hooks page] | Both call scripts/hooks/stop-check | Yes, but it depends on cwd ([SKL-09](#skl-09)) |
| Hook timeout | Behaviour on expiry: unverified | Behaviour on expiry: unverified | 300 s in both files, against a 900 s focus lane bound | No: an overrun records no key, so focus reruns ([SKL-10](#skl-10)) |
| Bootwright command guard | ask rules, glob match [permissions page] | `.codex/rules/*.rules` prefix_rule [rules page] | Claude Code only, tested against the catalog | No on Codex ([SKL-01](#skl-01)); the inventory is narrower than the prose ([COR-01](#cor-01)) |
| git and Ansible guard | Rules anchored to leading text [permissions page] | none tracked | settings.json:27-29, 52-59 | Partly: `git -C` and trailing `--force` forms miss the rules, ad-hoc `ansible` is unguarded, the rebase prompt is undocumented ([SKL-02](#skl-02), [SKL-11](#skl-11), [SKL-07](#skl-07)) |
| Bypass modes | Skip ask rules [permissions page] | Full access skips rules [rules page] | Acknowledged in index.md:32-34 | Documented, no fix |

The common contract the audit proposes (smallest change, one owner for each fact):

1. AGENTS.md stays the only root instruction, and CLAUDE.md only imports it. The forbidden set points to the catalog's Effects column. It names `controller rebind`, the irreversible local commands and ad-hoc `ansible` ([COR-01](#cor-01), [SKL-11](#skl-11)).
2. Code owns one guard inventory. TestDocsAskRulesCoverEveryEffectfulCommand checks it against both .claude/settings.json and a tracked .codex/rules/bootwright.rules (decision "prompt"), with the matching .gitignore exception ([SKL-01](#skl-01)). The git forms get a table-driven test ([SKL-02](#skl-02)). A shared PreToolUse script is optional later work.
3. The irreversible local commands (context delete, secret delete, secret encryption rotate, media delete) leave askRuleNoAsk and gain ask rules ([COR-01](#cor-01)).
4. The owner decides whether the task-branch rebase prompts. The answer is written either in the ask list or in git-integration.md ([SKL-07](#skl-07)).
5. Rule files only point to owners. The version-constant convention moves to specs/index.md Conventions, and Runtime parity may say that .claude/rules files only point to canonical owners ([SKL-12](#skl-12)).
6. A session runs in the task worktree. Otherwise the agent runs `make focus` there before ending a turn ([SKL-09](#skl-09)).
7. stop-check stops focus at its own 270 s deadline, below the 300 s runtime timeout, and records the timeout as advisory ([SKL-10](#skl-10)).
8. Skills stay canonical in .agents/skills. Wrappers turn into symlinks only after both runtimes are checked ([SKL-13](#skl-13)).

### 11.5 Measurements that would show the portfolio works

These measurements are the audit's proposal. Lane G03 suggested them; the audit set the thresholds.

- **Trigger accuracy.** Replay a fixed set of about 20 recorded task prompts: Go fix, role change, spec edit, item move, slice plan, audit lane, add-on package. Threshold: each skill loads on every prompt of its own kind and on none of the others. Record the result in the [SKL-15](#skl-15) item.
- **Load cost.** Count bytes loaded per accepted task, from the runtime's usage logs. Threshold: within 10% of the "After proposal" column in 11.4.
- **Budgets.** Every per-edit file and every skill body has a docsByteBudgets entry under the existing ratchet. Threshold: `make docs-check` passes ([COR-25](#cor-25)).
- **Guard parity.** The catalog-derived test passes for both .claude/settings.json and .codex/rules/bootwright.rules, and the git form table passes. Threshold: zero effectful catalog commands or git forms left unguarded ([SKL-01](#skl-01), [SKL-02](#skl-02), [COR-01](#cor-01)).
- **Hook verdicts.** Count turn ends where stop-check produced no recorded key. Threshold: zero after the [SKL-10](#skl-10) change.
- **Drift.** Threshold: 'Planned slices row' appears only in AGENTS.md ([COR-24](#cor-24)), and grep finds no restated touch set in skills ([ARC-06](#arc-06)).

## 12. Findings catalog

Every entry below passed the verification that section 16 describes: an
independent refuter and an independent judge, an arbiter where they disagreed
about the defect or about its extent, a third reading for every finding that
stood at High or Blocking after merging, and a mechanical check of each
citation against the audited commit. One finding, [REC-41](#rec-41), reached High later,
when its extent was arbitrated and a final arbiter agreed.

An id is stable within this report. Its prefix names the area: SCO scope, CON
concepts and names, API the desired-state API, CLI the command line and its
output, ARC architecture and extension, REC the reconciliation, safety and
security rules, LNG language responsibility, COR the spec corpus, SKL skills
and agent instructions, DOC operator documentation and examples. "Source"
names the lane and candidate that raised the finding; the lanes are in
[Appendix A](#appendix-a-lane-records).

Blocking and High findings are printed in full. Medium findings are printed in
a standard form with at most three citations. Low findings are printed one per
table row with their first citation; their acceptance criteria and decision
checks were produced and verified like the others and are left out for size.
A text field that ran long is cut at a sentence end, or at a word with an
ellipsis where no sentence ended nearby.

Every entry describes the audited commit. An entry or a row marked "After the
baseline" was resolved, changed or moved by a commit that landed while the
audit ran; [section 17.2](#172-what-the-later-commits-do-to-the-findings) has
the details, and section 17.3 holds the findings in the text those commits
added, whose ids begin with NEW.

A recommendation is a proposal. It authorizes nothing: the owner decides which
findings become items.

### 12.3 Objectives, scope and domain

<a id="sco-01"></a>

#### SCO-01 Physical-node coverage still claims an emulated tier that D224 abolished

High; contradiction; changes spec-text; effort S; source S02-2; related [COR-02](#cor-02), [COR-91](#cor-91), [DOC-01](#doc-01), [SCO-02](#sco-02).

**Claim.** D224 removes every emulated stand-in for the physical path, retires B496 and makes B67's acceptance the owner's run on real hardware. B67's own exit evidence follows that decision. B251's exit evidence and B730's operator gate in m3.md still name "B67's emulated rehearsal", and the openshift-coverage Physical nodes row still lists an emulated CA-issued-leaf qualification that no longer has a run.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/milestones/backlog.md:6878-6879`: "No case, example or gate emulates a physical host to stand in for the physical path"
- `specs/milestones/backlog.md:6881-6881`: "B73's and B67's acceptance is the owner's run on real hardware."
- `specs/openshift-coverage.md:101-101`: "in-tree; emulated with a CA-issued leaf; real hardware B730"
- `specs/milestones/m3.md:1442-1443`: "The emulated rehearsal of the same path is B67's."
- `specs/milestones/m3.md:911-912`: "an end-to-end run of the physical pre-boot refusals in B67's emulated rehearsal."
- `specs/milestones/m3.md:872-874`: "the real-hardware row of B730, with no emulated rehearsal of the physical path (D224)."

**Consequence.** An agent planning M3d could rebuild the removed lab-baremetal-rehearsal case or the retired B496 leaf emulation to meet these exit lines. Alternatively, an item's exit evidence can never be met because the gate it names no longer exists. The coverage page also overstates the evidence for the physical row.

**Recommendation.** openshift-coverage.md:101: change the Qualification cell to "in-tree; real hardware [B730] (D224)". m3.md:911-912 (B251): change the exit to "an end-to-end run of the physical pre-boot refusals in B730's real-hardware run". m3.md:1442-1443 (B730): replace "The emulated rehearsal of the same path is B67's." with "This run is B67's acceptance (D224)." Mark D235 (1)'s session clause about B67's emulated rehearsal as moot under D224.

**Acceptance.** grep -n 'emulated' over specs/openshift-coverage.md and specs/milestones/m3.md finds no physical-node gate, profile or exit line that calls for an emulated run.

**Decisions and principles.** Decisions read by the judge: D224, D235. Principles applied: none recorded. Finder's check: Read D224 (owner, 2026-11-03) and D235 (1) (owner answer plus a pending session clause naming B67's emulated rehearsal, dated after D224). The session clause contradicts the owner decision D224, which binds. Searched not-yet-met.txt: no item tracks this cleanup.

**Verification.** refuter confirmed; judge confirmed at High; third reading: holds.

**Demonstration (third reading).** The state that gets two answers is B67's acceptance path. B67's exit (m3.md:872-874) says "no emulated rehearsal of the physical path (D224)". B251's exit (m3.md:911-912) requires "an end-to-end run of the physical pre-boot refusals in B67's emulated rehearsal", and B730 (m3.md:1442-1443) says "The emulated rehearsal of the same path is B67's." D224 removed the lab-baremetal-rehearsal case, so B251's exit names a run that cannot happen. An agent closing B251 either rebuilds the removed case, which D224 forbids, or decides on its own where the refusals get proved, since nothing names B730 as the replacement. The coverage row (openshift-coverage.md:101) promises an emulated CA-issued-leaf qualification, but B496, whose remaining gate was that rehearsal, was retired (backlog.md:3543).

<a id="sco-02"></a>

#### SCO-02 D235's move of B883 and the physical profile missing from coverage pages

High; contradiction; changes spec-text; effort S; source S02-3; related [API-32](#api-32), [DOC-01](#doc-01), [SCO-01](#sco-01).

**Claim.** D235 (2), an owner answer, amends B730 and B883: lab-physical has no fixed node count, its compact-host run makes the bonded VLAN install interface and a secondary network required rows, and it installs nmstate and kubevirt, which accepts B883. specs/openshift-coverage.md:158 is the page m3.md names as owner of profile node shapes, and it still requires at least 3 physical control-plane nodes and 2 workers with none of those rows. specs/add-on-coverage.md:43 still qualifies the kubevirt package only on B732's nested host and leaves out B730's run.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/add-on-coverage.md:43-43`: "package qualification in-tree; the nested host of lab-kubevirt-nested (B732)"
- `specs/milestones/m4.md:1880-1881`: "awaiting operator acceptance on B730's physical run (D235 (2))."
- `specs/openshift-coverage.md:158-158`: "at least 3 physical control-plane nodes and 2 physical workers through their BMCs, on real hardware only (D224)"
- `specs/milestones/m3.md:1443-1446`: "the profile names no fixed node count, and its run on the owner's compact host makes the bonded VLAN install interface and a secondary network ..."
- `specs/milestones/m3.md:159-159`: "(b) B730's profile as written, which needs two physical workers"

**Consequence.** An operator who prepares lab-physical from the coverage page provisions two worker servers that the owner's compact-host run does not need, and leaves out the nmstate, kubevirt and secondary-network rows that now gate B730 and B883. A reviewer checking B883's acceptance looks for a B732 nested row that will never close it.

**Recommendation.** Rewrite the lab-physical node-shape cell at openshift-coverage.md:158: physical control-plane nodes, and workers if any, in any shape the installer accepts (D235 (2)). On the owner's compact host, the bonded VLAN install interface and a secondary network are required rows, then the nmstate and kubevirt packages install ([B883]); real hardware only (D224). In add-on-coverage.md:43, name B730's physical run (D235 (2)) as the kubevirt row's gate and keep B732 as further evidence. Also update the Submilestone cell "none (D193)", the "optional evidence" sentence at m3.md:320-322, and the example README's "three masters and two workers" and lab-sno/lab-compact prerequisites (waived by D235 (1)).

**Acceptance.** The kubevirt package row and the lab-physical profile both name B730 and D235 (2). No coverage page names B732 as B883's gate.

**Decisions and principles.** Decisions read by the judge: D193, D224, D235. Principles applied: none recorded. Finder's check: Read D235 clauses (1) and (2) at backlog.md:7129-7150; clause (2) is an owner answer amending D193 (3). Read the B730 and B883 sections, which are already amended. The coverage pages are the only stale owners. No item tracks the propagation.

**Verification.** refuter narrowed; judge confirmed at High; recommendation amended by the judge; third reading: holds.

**Demonstration (third reading).** The coverage page, which owns profile node shapes (m3.md:325-330), sets lab-physical to "at least 3 physical control-plane nodes and 2 physical workers" with no package rows. B730, amended by D235 (2), says "the profile names no fixed node count" and makes the bonded VLAN interface, a secondary network, nmstate and kubevirt required, which accepts B883. Q140 at m3.md:159 rejected option (b), "B730's profile as written, which needs two physical workers". So an operator preparing the owner's compact host, or an agent checking B883's gate, gets two answers: the coverage page says two workers are needed and the run includes no packages, while B730 says no workers are needed and the run installs nmstate and kubevirt. The add-on-coverage kubevirt row names only B732, while B883 (m4.md:1880) names B730's physical run as its gate.

**Low findings: objectives, scope and domain.** Each was verified like the others and is given in one row with its first citation; the Value column is the judge's estimate of what fixing it is worth to the owner.

### 12.4 Concepts and names

<a id="con-01"></a>

#### CON-01 Per-site VLAN rule makes one Network span disjoint libvirt bridges

Medium; contradiction; changes spec-text; effort M; source A04-1; related [API-69](#api-69).

**Claim.** The per-site 802.1Q-domain rule does not fit a host with several libvirt bridges. Each bridge is its own tagging domain, but two such domains cannot be modelled as two Networks that share a VLAN ID. So the shipped libvirt-network-variants example declares one Network, nv-guest, across two bridges that cannot reach each other. The rule refuses too much in libvirt labs, and Network membership there stops meaning layer-2 reachability. Nothing unsafe is admitted, and the case is limited to emulated rehearsals.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/api/networks.md:3-3`: "'Network' declares one layer-2 network: at most one VLAN, at most one subnet per"
- `specs/api/networks.md:68-69`: "are refused on each of them, naming both, when they declare the same 'vlan', or when their CIDRs of one family overlap. This assumes one ..."
- `specs/api/networks.md:92-93`: "The bridge carries the guest VLAN tags of 'taggedNetworkRefs' between guests only"

**Consequence.** In the example, nv-bond (203.0.113.11 on virbr-nv VLAN 140) and nv-vlan (203.0.113.12 on br-nv VLAN 140) pass admission as members of one L2 Network, but no frame can pass between them.

**Recommendation.** Raise this as an open question on D240 (9), which is still pending owner review, rather than changing admission ahead of the owner. Propose that a Network carried only on libvirt segments (managed Networks, provider segments and their taggedNetworkRefs, all of which admission can derive) takes its 802.1Q domain from its bridge set on that host instead of from the site. VLAN and CIDR conflicts would be checked per shared bridge, and per site for everything else. If the owner accepts, update networks.md and split nv-guest into two Networks, one per bridge.

**Acceptance.** networks.md states the domain of a Network carried only on libvirt bridges. The example declares one Network per bridge domain. An admission test admits two VLAN-140 Networks carried on disjoint libvirt segments of one host and still refuses them when one segment carries both.

**Decisions and principles.** Decisions read by the judge: D240. Principles applied: none recorded.

**Verification.** refuter narrowed; judge narrowed at Medium; recommendation amended by the judge.

<a id="con-02"></a>

#### CON-02 Log root declared outcome-free yet refuses setup, deletion and writes unrepaired

Medium; contradiction; changes spec-text; effort S; source L07-3, D10-2; related [CLI-45](#cli-45), [REC-20](#rec-20).

**Claim.** "Losing logs changes no outcome" is not contradicted, because refusing an unsafe object is a security posture, not log loss. Three real defects remain. (1) The mode/owner/type refusal at log-root.md:35-37 names only the path and "nothing repairs it". It does not give the held owner and mode, the required root:root 0700, or a repair. A freshly made filesystem mounted as the log root (0755 by default) therefore blocks every command with no exit. The store-root refusal in contexts.md:307-319 does name these.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/contexts/log-root.md:7-7`: "nothing reads it back for a decision, and losing it changes no outcome."
- `specs/contexts/log-root.md:35-37`: "of another owner or mode, or of another type refuses 'context.state' naming its path and saying that nothing repairs it"
- `specs/contexts/log-root.md:116-117`: "A name a setup output takes that is no private regular file within its bound refuses setup"

**Consequence.** An operator mounts a dedicated log filesystem, which the page explicitly allows. Its root is mode 0755 by default, so every lifecycle command refuses with "nothing repairs it" and offers no chmod remedy. Separately, a stray file under the context's log directory stops a deletion that is already marked `deleting` at its last step.

**Recommendation.** Keep "nothing is chmodded or chowned". That is the stated rule: reject unsafe objects without repairing them. Make the log-root refusal match the store root's refusal (contexts.md:307-319): name the type, the uid:gid owner and octal mode it holds, the root:root 0700 directory it must be, and the repair (make it that, for example chown/chmod a mounted root, or remove the entry), then repeat the command. Give the deletion walk's foreign-entry and mount refusal the same kind of exit that the store's deletion walk got under F005/B455.

**Acceptance.** log-root.md no longer says "nothing repairs it". Each log-root refusal names a repair. output.md and log-root.md give the same answer for a foreign setup-output name. A test covers a deletion that meets a foreign log entry and names the exit.

**Decisions and principles.** Decisions read by the judge: D244, D249. Principles applied: P26, P36, P40.

**Verification.** refuter narrowed; judge narrowed at Medium; recommendation amended by the judge; merged from 2 candidates (L07-3 Medium, D10-2 Medium).

**Merged candidates.** The entry states the defect as its clearest candidate put it; these raised the same defect, sometimes a further instance or aspect of it: D10-2: Setup output failures both refuse setup and never change it.

<a id="con-03"></a>

#### CON-03 Renewing a generated CA leaves its leaves' status unspecified

Medium; ambiguity; changes spec-text; effort S; source L10-2; related [API-133](#api-133).

**Claim.** specs/secrets.md never says what status `secret check` and bind give a generated leaf whose stored chain ends in a CA version that is no longer the issuer's current one. Under the fingerprint rule (D71) the leaf stays current. Line 230 covers only a stale issuer, not a stale leaf. Line 236 ('validated on use') does not say what the chain is validated against. A fresh binding can therefore pair the new CA with the old leaf.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/secrets.md:242-243`: "Renewing a CA alone leaves issued leaves unchanged. Explicitly renew its leaves afterward, then replace consumers"
- `specs/secrets.md:236-237`: "Its chain, signature, serving identity and key are validated on use."
- `specs/secrets.md:337-338`: "A Secret declaration's fingerprint drops its provenance and covers type, source and parameters only (D71)"

**Consequence.** After a CA renewal, a fresh apply binds the new CA, which consumers trust, together with the old leaf signed by the retired CA key. One implementation validates the leaf against its own chain and binds a mismatched trust pair, so the failure appears only at a TLS handshake late in the run.

**Recommendation.** After the sentence 'Its chain, signature, serving identity and key are validated on use.', add: 'A leaf whose stored chain does not end in its issuer's current certificate fails that validation: `secret check` reports it as `invalid`, and bind refuses it before reading other material, with the remedy `secret generate --name <leaf> --renew`. Generate without `--renew` leaves it unchanged.' Keep `stale` for a fingerprint change. Add a named test that renews only the CA and then checks the leaf and binds it.

**Acceptance.** secrets.md defines the leaf's status after an issuer renewal, and a named test shows `check` and bind behaving that way after a CA-only renewal.

**Decisions and principles.** Decisions read by the judge: D71, D175. Principles applied: P26, P44.

**Verification.** refuter narrowed; judge narrowed at Medium; recommendation amended by the judge.

<a id="con-04"></a>

#### CON-04 Realized target has five drifting field lists and a self-contradiction

Medium; contradiction; changes spec-text; effort M; source S04-1, L15-5; related [REC-42](#rec-42), TRK-03.

**Claim.** Two real defects. First, substrates.md:61-63 says a KubeVirt/vSphere realized target 'names no management controller', while substrates.md:1265-1267 says it names kubevirt:&lt;namespace>/&lt;vm> as its management controller. Second, the owner enumeration at substrates.md:44-47 leaves out 'whether it is physical' (and the placement Machine), which the glossary, managed-os.md:170-172 and openshift-clusters.md:19-21 all say the target supplies. Those pages also link to #selection-and-refusal instead of #implementations.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/glossary.md:16-17`: "Realized target: what a substrate derives for a Machine: the management controller it boots through, its identity channel, whether it is physical"
- `specs/substrates.md:44-47`: "the Machine's substrate arm, its management controller, its identity channel, the interfaces the machine presents with the hardware addresses they report, and the block"
- `specs/substrates.md:61-63`: "Their realized target names no management controller: it names the arm's own management API and access, an identity channel of none"

**Consequence.** This record is the seam that lets a VMware or cloud arm arrive without changing consumers. An implementer adding an arm cannot tell from the owner page which fields to fill: 'whether physical' is missing from the owner list, and the management-controller slot is both empty and filled for KubeVirt.

**Recommendation.** Rewrite substrates.md:61-63 to say that on an API-managed arm the management-controller slot holds the arm's management API endpoint and credential (for KubeVirt, kubevirt:&lt;namespace>/&lt;vm> and its kubeconfig) instead of a BMC. Add 'whether it is physical' and 'the Machine whose host reaches its controller' to the owner list at substrates.md:44-47. Point the realized-target links in specs/glossary.md, specs/managed-os.md and specs/openshift-clusters.md at substrates.md#implementations.

**Acceptance.** grep for 'realized target' finds exactly one field enumeration (the table in substrates.md). The table names every exported field of substrate.Target. substrates.md no longer says a KubeVirt target 'names no management controller'.

**Decisions and principles.** Decisions read by the judge: none found to bear on it. Principles applied: P41.

**Verification.** refuter narrowed; judge narrowed at Medium; recommendation amended by the judge; merged from 2 candidates (S04-1 Medium, L15-5 Medium).

**Merged candidates.** The entry states the defect as its clearest candidate put it; these raised the same defect, sometimes a further instance or aspect of it: L15-5: General power contract names arms and BMC vocabulary, so vSphere falls through.

<a id="con-05"></a>

#### CON-05 device-not-empty and foreign-osd refusals name neither host nor disk

Medium; design; changes spec-text; effort S; source L23-4; related [CLI-31](#cli-31), [REC-124](#rec-124), [REC-126](#rec-126).

**Claim.** The device-not-empty and foreign-osd refusals do not name the disk. The refused per-host Ceph block still identifies the host, so the real gap is the disk. The device-serial-* refusals on the same binding path name the Machine and its authored serials, so naming the authored selector is consistent with the redaction rule.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/ceph.md:1321-1321`: "Their remedy names 'wipefs --no-act &lt;disk>' to see what the disk holds"
- `specs/ceph.md:1326-1328`: "refusal's detail names the token and the code site that refused, never the disk: a native worker's cause carries no value, so the host and ..."
- `specs/ceph.md:1223-1224`: "names the Machine and the serials its host selects"

**Consequence.** On an eleven-host physical cluster with fifteen disks per host, an operator must inspect up to 165 disks by hand to find the one dirty disk. They may then clear the wrong disk, or declare many disks in clearOnInstall, which widens destructive scope instead of narrowing it.

**Recommendation.** In specs/ceph.md 1326-1328, keep the rule that the native cause carries no value. Add that the refusal's coordinate names the Machine and the declared OSD selector that matched the disk (the serial or path the operator authored, exactly as the device-serial-* refusals do), and never a kernel path, alias or native output. Show both placeholders in the remedy text, and add a test asserting that the selector appears.

**Acceptance.** The device-not-empty and foreign-osd rows name Machine and declared selector placeholders, consistent with the device-serial-* refusals, and a test asserts the selector appears in the diagnostic.

**Decisions and principles.** Decisions read by the judge: D141, D225. Principles applied: P12, P15, P26, P40, P44.

**Verification.** refuter narrowed; judge narrowed at Medium; recommendation amended by the judge.

<a id="con-06"></a>

#### CON-06 Glossary's closed 'always' sets for Evidence and Receipt are false

Medium; contradiction; changes spec-text; effort S; source S06-1; related [CON-24](#con-24), [CON-29](#con-29), [CON-30](#con-30).

**Claim.** The Receipt entry's 'always' two-member set is false: owner pages define ownership receipts (add-ons.md), erase/physical-erase receipts (state-reconciliation.md), and native-absence and media receipts, among others. The Evidence entry's link for block evidence goes to #block-transitions (state-reconciliation.md:834-878), and that section never says 'evidence'; the term is defined at architecture.md:685. The Evidence list is less clearly wrong.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/glossary.md:102-102`: "**Evidence**: always context mutation evidence"
- `specs/glossary.md:107-107`: "**Receipt**: always the lifecycle receipt, the four final lines of an"
- `specs/index.md:13-13`: "What a term means: context, controller, BMC, substrate, binding, profile, capability, implementation, evidence, receipt"

**Consequence.** An agent routed by specs/index.md reads that a receipt is either the four output lines or the setup receipt. When it changes an add-on ownership receipt or a Ceph erase receipt, it applies the wrong owner's rules, and the safety class, which keys on ownership 'proof', may not trigger.

**Recommendation.** Remove 'always' from both entries. Define a receipt as a durable record of one completed effect that later work checks before it acts. Name the setup/install receipt, ownership receipts (add-ons.md#ownership-receipts), erase receipts and native-absence receipts, each with a link to its owner, and keep the lifecycle receipt as the separate presentation sense. Under Evidence, name host evidence and installation evidence with owner links. Repoint the block-evidence link to the architecture.md passage near line 685 that defines it. Leave out the long prose definitions; the owner pages carry those.

**Acceptance.** Every '&lt;qualifier> receipt' and '&lt;qualifier> evidence' noun phrase in specs/ outside milestones/ that names a durable record uses a qualifier the glossary lists, and each listed qualifier links to a section whose text uses that phrase.

**Decisions and principles.** Decisions read by the judge: D50, D55, D165, D167, D177, D209. Principles applied: P40.

**Verification.** refuter narrowed; judge narrowed at Medium; recommendation amended by the judge.
