#### REC-32 Matching-backup remedy silently rolls back every context's evidence

Medium; unsafe-rule; changes spec-text; effort S; source L07-1, X05-2, X06-4.

**Claim.** The matching-backup definition (specs/contexts.md:872-878) does not say that restoring the image rolls back every context's evidence, reservations and the controller record to when it was taken, and it sets no recency condition. Four remedies offer this restore, two of them for damage to a single context. Line 868 governs a future restore command, not the operator's own act outside any command, so there is no contradiction, only a missing warning.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/contexts.md:868-869`: "An old snapshot cannot silently become current writable state."
- `specs/contexts.md:873-875`: "is an image of the whole state root, taken while no command holds its root lock or any context lease, whose restoration keeps the device ..."
- `specs/contexts.md:917-919`: "then 'bootwright context delete --name &lt;name> --purge --allow-orphans', or restore the whole store from a [matching backup]"

**Consequence.** An operator follows the remedy for one context's unreadable mutation.json and restores last week's image. Every other context on the host loses the operations, ownership evidence, controller-record bindings and host reservations recorded since then. Nothing detects this: the Not-yet-met line covers only seal counters.

**Recommendation.** Add one sentence to the matching-backup definition in specs/contexts.md#format-and-restore-boundary: restoring an image rolls every context, its mutation evidence and reservations, and the controller record back to the moment the image was taken, so a matching backup is one taken after the last mutation of any context in the store. Leave the four remedies linking to the definition unchanged (one owner per fact), with no extra diff step and no golden test, because the restore is outside every command.

**Acceptance.** specs/contexts.md#format-and-restore-boundary states the rollback consequence and the recency condition. Every remedy that names a matching backup (contexts.md lines ~423, ~732, ~919, ~930) carries that condition. A refusal golden test shows the warning text.

#### REC-33 Store binds directories by device number but never names a reboot-stable device identity

Medium; gap; changes spec-text; effort M; source L07-5.

**Claim.** The registry, the Controller descriptor and the tool-area entries bind directories by device and inode (contexts.md:231-232, 290; controller-record.md:39-41, 69-72). Every registry transaction checks those bindings, and a replaced directory has no supported exit (contexts.md:411-425). No passage says which device identity is meant or what happens when the device number changes across a reboot or remount.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/contexts.md:232-232`: "configured secret-store type and reserved directory device/inode."
- `specs/contexts.md:419-423`: "a replaced directory, a damaged reservation, ... is resolved only by restoring the whole store from a [matching backup]"
- `specs/controller.md:937-938`: "Btrfs uses its real block source rather than treating an anonymous subvolume device number as the filesystem identity."

**Consequence.** An implementer who compares the raw st_dev, which the text allows, can see every context and the controller record refuse as replaced directories when a qualified Btrfs or device-mapper root gets a different device number after a reboot. The context-incarnation check (openshift-clusters.md:477) breaks the same way.

**Recommendation.** In contexts.md 'Storage, locking and publication', define the device half of every directory binding as a reboot-stable filesystem identity: the filesystem UUID, plus the subvolume id on Btrfs. Do not use the raw st_dev, just as controller.md:937-938 already avoids it for host identity. State that a mismatch under this identity is a replaced directory. Point controller-record.md and the openshift-clusters.md incarnation rule at that definition. Record a backlog item for the device-number change that the delivered record lists as not handled.

**Acceptance.** contexts.md 'Storage, locking and publication' names the device identity that directory bindings compare and says it stays the same across an ordinary reboot on ext4, XFS and Btrfs. controller-record.md and openshift-clusters.md:477 link to it.

<a id="rec-34"></a>

#### REC-34 Fixed 16 MiB byte admission does not cover the plan-dependent removal reserve

Medium; ambiguity; changes spec-text; effort S; source L08-5.

**Claim.** The entries rule is computed from the frozen plan, but the byte rule is a fixed 16 MiB with no derivation. That figure has to cover the apply's records and the removal's reserve (its plan, its 32 KiB-per-block first pass and its resolutions). At the documented maxima (a 6 MiB plan, 256 blocks) that sum can exceed 16 MiB.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/contexts.md:652-654`: "The removal's first pass at 32 KiB a block, its one entry more, its registration's bytes, a resolution per apply block unknown, running or in ..."
- `specs/contexts.md:672-674`: "A fresh apply needs 16 MiB of them free, which hold its records and those of the removal that takes it back"
- `specs/contexts.md:646-647`: "the next fresh apply refuses at its claim, before it raises evidence or binds anything, never at one of its block writes"

**Consequence.** For a 256-block plan, the removal reserve alone (256 x 32 KiB plus a plan of up to 6 MiB) is about 14 MiB, and the apply's own plan of up to 6 MiB also comes out of the 16 MiB. An apply admitted with exactly 16 MiB free then refuses at its first attempt, naming destroy as its only way on.

**Recommendation.** In specs/contexts.md (the byte admission paragraph), state the fresh-apply byte requirement as computed from the frozen plan: its plan and operation record, its first pass at 32 KiB a block, the removal's plan and registration, and the removal's first pass at 32 KiB a block. Keep 16 MiB only as a stated floor, if it is one. Name the test that admits a maximum plan at that computed line and runs its first pass without a reserve refusal.

**Acceptance.** The byte rule is stated as a function of the frozen plan, or the 16 MiB figure is shown to cover the maximum plan. A test admits a 256-block maximum-size plan at the byte line and runs its first attempt.

**Decisions and principles.** Decisions read by the judge: D52, D105. Principles applied: none recorded.

**Verification.** refuter confirmed; judge narrowed at Medium; recommendation amended by the judge.

<a id="rec-35"></a>

#### REC-35 Shared record publication primitive never states its durability point

Medium; gap; changes spec-text; effort S; source X01-2, L08-2.

**Claim.** The shared record publication rule in specs/contexts.md#storage-locking-and-publication (stage, prove, rename) leaves out its durability point: syncing the stage and then the containing directory before it returns. The implementation already does this (Replace syncs the stage and its directory; see .agents/knowledge/operation-store-entry-confirmation.md), so the gap is in the spec text only. No current power-loss defect follows from it.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/contexts.md:498-500`: "stages its bytes beside its target, proves right before one rename that the destination still holds what it replaces or renames without replacing anything"
- `specs/contexts/controller-record.md:297-299`: "Publication writes and syncs an exclusive private staging file, revalidates the held directory and previous record identity, then renames and syncs its parent."
- `specs/state-reconciliation.md:1428-1429`: "The executor allocates the next attempt number and durably records 'running' before a block's first side effect."

**Consequence.** An implementer can follow contexts.md:497-501 exactly and rename without syncing `blocks/<id>/`. A block starts (for example a Redfish power-on or a disk erase), the host then loses power, and the rename of the `running` block record is not yet on disk.

**Recommendation.** Extend the existing publication sentence at specs/contexts.md:497-501 rather than adding a new paragraph. A record publication syncs its stage before the rename and the containing directory after it, and the record counts as published, and any dependent publication or guarded effect may start, only once both syncs return. A sync failure after the rename reports uncertain durability, as line 74 already says. Cite this rule from state-reconciliation.md#record-encoding-and-versions.

**Acceptance.** contexts.md#storage-locking-and-publication names the durability point of the shared primitive. state-reconciliation.md:536-557 links to it. A named test, along the lines of `TestARecordPublicationSyncsItsDirectoryBeforeReturning`, is cited.

**Decisions and principles.** Decisions read by the judge: D85, D127, D177. Principles applied: P26, P44.

#### REC-36 Registry-login rebind ignores the copy cephadm keeps on each host

Medium; contradiction; changes spec-text; effort M; source L10-4; related [CON-10](#con-10), [REC-100](#rec-100), [REC-83](#rec-83).

**Claim.** The guest record is specified as written: core authorization publishes podman-auth.json as a reserved, bound inode (specs/ceph-native-api.md:164-172). What is missing is narrower. No page says that an attempt presenting a rebound registry login (D183) republishes that record. ceph.md 122-128 and 241 say guest delivery uses the 'original' binding, which conflicts with the rebind that state-reconciliation.md 2747-2749 grants the Ceph blocks.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/state-reconciliation.md:2747-2749`: "the KubeVirt blocks their 'kubeconfigRef', and the Ceph cluster, host and image blocks the registry login"
- `specs/ceph.md:123-123`: "guest delivery uses that exact reference and original credential binding."
- `specs/secrets.md:423-425`: "each Ceph host keeps it in cephadm's registry login file '/etc/ceph/podman-auth.json', which cephadm reads for its own image pulls."

**Consequence.** An operator rotates the registry password and continues an interrupted Ceph apply with `--authorize rebind=<secret>`. Bootwright's own pulls succeed. Every cephadm-initiated pull, such as a daemon deploy or redeploy, still reads the stale podman-auth.json and fails, and continuation cannot fix that.

**Recommendation.** In ceph.md, replace 'original credential binding' and 'original binding' (lines 122-128 and 241) with 'the operation's current binding (the original or its access-credential rebind)'. In the core authorization text (ceph-native-api.md 164-172, or the ceph.md section that owns it), state that an attempt presenting a rebound registry login republishes the protected guest registry record under its existing reservation and descriptor binding before any native pull. Leave secrets.md unchanged: the block reserves that file path itself.

**Acceptance.** ceph.md names the phase that writes and refreshes podman-auth.json and its removal on data hosts, or says it goes with the hosts. ceph.md and state-reconciliation.md agree on which binding guest delivery presents.

<a id="rec-37"></a>

#### REC-37 A setup-format discard relabels Bootwright's packages 'present before bootwright'

Medium; gap; changes stored-state; effort M; source L11-3; related [ARC-83](#arc-83), [CLI-54](#cli-54), [REC-08](#rec-08), [REC-38](#rec-38), [REC-72](#rec-72).

**Claim.** After a setup-format discard, setup's re-inspection sees every provider an earlier install added as already present and records it `present before bootwright`. That label is false, and uninstall then keeps those packages without saying why. Worse, the uninstall refusal for an unreadable receipt gives the remedy 'run controller install, then run controller uninstall again', and following it leads to an uninstall that removes nothing. The outcome is fail-safe because packages are kept.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/controller.md:1026-1027`: "Setup plans "Discard setup state another Bootwright build wrote ('&lt;format>')", removes the subtree after confirmation"
- `specs/contexts/controller-record.md:243-244`: "'requested' freezes the requirements absent before this setup's package transaction."
- `specs/controller.md:382-384`: "so the host is as it was before its first install apart from what the operator or a context's controller stage added"

**Consequence.** Pre-1.0 format moves are frequent (D241, D249). After one, `controller uninstall` reports `openssh-clients` and `python3.12` as 'present before bootwright' and leaves them, although an earlier Bootwright install added them. The report is false, and the operator has no way to know these packages are Bootwright's.

**Recommendation.** Do not add a separately versioned packages.json. A frozen side schema that must survive format moves is compatibility machinery, which P20 rules out before 1.0. Instead, when setup discards another build's record, it attributes every requirement already present to a distinct marker, `attribution lost (<format>)`, never `present before bootwright`. Uninstall keeps those packages and lists them separately under what stays. Reword the unreadable-receipt remedy so it says that reinstalling makes uninstall keep the packages an earlier build added, and that the operator removes them by hand.

**Acceptance.** controller-record.md names the separately versioned attribution file and states that a format discard keeps it, or states the `unknown` marker. The uninstall 'what stays' list distinguishes `unknown` from `present before bootwright`. A test covers a discard followed by uninstall.

**Decisions and principles.** Decisions read by the judge: D152, D209, D241, D244, D247, D249. Principles applied: P12, P15, P19, P20.

**Verification.** refuter narrowed; judge narrowed at Medium; recommendation amended by the judge.

#### REC-38 Format discard's behavior when a runtime is in use is undefined

Medium; ambiguity; changes spec-text; effort S; source L11-4, X01-4; related [CLI-54](#cli-54), [REC-37](#rec-37).

**Claim.** Format healing says the discard takes every runtime's lock first, but not how it takes them (blocking or LOCK_NB) or what a held lock does. Retention defines a skip, which a whole-subtree removal cannot use. The spec does not have to define a rename-aside step. A partly removed subtree still reads as another build's, so the next setup discards it again.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/controller.md:1027-1029`: "removes the subtree after confirmation, taking every runtime's lock first so it never removes one in use, and proceeds"
- `specs/contexts/controller-record.md:268-269`: "retirement takes the lock exclusively without waiting, so a runtime in use is skipped"
- `specs/controller.md:1025-1026`: "a setup subtree holding an entry this build does not list, is another build's"

**Consequence.** An operator runs a newer build's `controller install` while an older build's apply is inside an Ansible block. One implementer blocks setup indefinitely, another refuses, a third skips the runtime and leaves a subtree that the next read judges foreign again.

**Recommendation.** Add to 'Format healing': the discard takes flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB) on each runtimes/*/.lock it finds. One a running command holds refuses controller.install as busy, removes nothing, and names the runtime and the remedy of waiting for that command, in line with the rule that a busy lock refuses. Add that an interrupted discard leaves a subtree that still reads as another build's, so the next setup discards it again. Leave out the rename-aside step.

**Acceptance.** specs/controller.md states the held-lock outcome and the rename-aside step for the discard. A test refuses a discard while a launch holds a runtime lock and leaves the subtree intact.

**Decisions and principles.** Decisions read by the judge: D152, D154, D244, D249. Principles applied: none recorded.

**Verification.** refuter narrowed; judge narrowed at Medium; recommendation amended by the judge; merged from 2 candidates (L11-4 Medium, X01-4 Low).

The power-off step, and the &lt;recovery> text that branches by substrate, exist only in Network convergence (lines 853-866). #### REC-47 Pending retry does not say the commented dnf transaction decides the reboot

Medium; gap; changes spec-text; effort S; source L18-2; related [REC-114](#rec-114).

**Claim.** specs/managed-os.md step 5 and Ownership and continuation reboot when "the transaction" changed a package, and a retry reading `pending` "runs the upgrade again". The text never says which transaction counts after that rerun. Only the observation clause names the history transaction carrying the `bootwright:<request digest>` comment, so an implementation can count the second, empty dnf run and skip the reboot after dnf succeeded but the record stayed `pending`.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/managed-os.md:1683-1684`: "When the transaction changed at least one package, the installation asks the installed system to power off"
- `specs/managed-os.md:1702-1703`: "A retry resumes from the state it reads: 'pending' runs the upgrade again, 'upgraded' reboots when the transaction changed a package and proves,"
- `specs/managed-os.md:1706-1708`: "An observation reads the record, 'VERSION_ID' and the history transaction carrying the comment, changing nothing"

**Consequence.** A worker built from the spec alone can record `complete` with update.rebooted false, update.packages 0 and the old running kernel after a session loss between dnf success and the `upgraded` write.

**Recommendation.** In specs/managed-os.md, Ownership and continuation: say that a retry reading `pending` first looks up the dnf history transaction commented `bootwright:<request digest>`; when it finds one, it records that transaction, writes `upgraded` and continues from it, else it runs the upgrade again. In step 5 and the `upgraded` rule, say the recorded commented transaction decides whether to reboot.

**Acceptance.** specs/managed-os.md Ownership and continuation names the commented history transaction as the one a `pending` retry looks up before rerunning dnf, and step 5 and the `upgraded` rule both say that transaction's package count decides the reboot.

**Decisions and principles.** Decisions read by the judge: D152, D190, D209. Principles applied: P9, P26, P33, P40.

#### REC-48 Known-hosts remedy says 'bound again' but trust anchors are never rebound

Medium; contradiction; changes spec-text; effort S; source L19-3; related [CON-10](#con-10).

**Claim.** The remedy in specs/infrastructure-services.md:98-100 ('until its Secret is corrected and bound again') contradicts specs/secrets.md:325-333 and state-reconciliation.md Access-credential rebind, which say a knownHostsRef trust anchor is never rebound and a continuation or removal presents the version its operation bound. Correcting the Secret cannot fix the frozen operation. Only a new operation, after the old one is removed or the context is deleted, binds the corrected material.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/infrastructure-services.md:98-100`: "an operation whose frozen Secret holds more than one entry refuses until its Secret is corrected and bound again."
- `specs/secrets.md:327-329`: "the 'known_hosts' entry that pins an SSH host key is: it is never presented to an endpoint and never rebound."
- `specs/infrastructure-services.md:253-255`: "This enforces the one-entry rule of addresses and access for a placement Machine whose blocks publish claims at the apply's registration"

**Consequence.** An SSH placement whose blocks publish no claim can register with multi-entry material, because registration checks only claim-publishing placements. Every run of that operation then refuses, its removal included. An operator who corrects the Secret, as the text says, still sees the refusal.

**Recommendation.** Replace the sentence with: 'an operation whose frozen Secret holds more than one entry refuses each such run; a trust anchor is never rebound, so correct the Secret and apply again after that operation is removed, or delete the context, the exits a lost binding names.' Also extend the registration-time one-entry check (infrastructure-services.md:249-258) to every SSH placement, not only claim-publishing ones, so such an operation never registers. Add a test for a placement that publishes no claim.

**Acceptance.** No sentence in infrastructure-services.md promises rebinding a known-hosts Secret. Either the remedy names a real path, or the binding-time check covers every SSH placement and a test proves that multi-entry material refuses before registration for a placement that publishes no ...

#### REC-50 Resolution and replay define completion without the node placement D199 requires

Medium; contradiction; changes spec-text; effort S; source L21-1; related [API-52](#api-52), [REC-01](#rec-01), [REC-119](#rec-119).

**Claim.** In specs/openshift-clusters.md, Node placement adds a condition to completion: every declared node must carry its placement. D199 clause 6 says a cluster that is otherwise complete but lacks placement is a partial realization. Two sections on the same page leave placement out: Unknown resolution lists the conditions for positive completion, and Replay lists the "only differences it converges". Neither mentions placement, so an implementer who reads only those sections would record the block done before placement is written.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/openshift-clusters.md:1068-1068`: "completion also requires every declared node to carry its placement"
- `specs/openshift-clusters.md:1007-1010`: "A cluster answering with this operation's identity at the declared release, reporting its installation completed, whole and with its media released, is positive completion"
- `specs/openshift-clusters.md:978-979`: "The only differences it converges are media it did not finish releasing and each node's BMC pointed at its installed disk"

**Consequence.** Suppose an attempt releases the media and its reply is lost before the placement patch. Its resolution then reads identity, release, completion and released media and records the block done with custody. The next apply is a settled apply, which reaches no host, so the infra role label and authored taints are never written.

Alternatively, move the placement condition into the Completion paragraph so that every section citing Completion inherits it.

**Claim.** specs/ceph.md makes Ceph package acquisition go "without proxy", and its registry broker connects only to the registry authority. Its refusal table and trust sections do not say what happens to a Ceph host whose Machine has an effective spec.proxy naming a Proxy. specs/api/machines.md leaves each consumer to define its use of that choice, and specs/managed-os.md refuses the matching registration case at plan time.

- `specs/ceph.md:198-200`: "Acquisition reads the authored 'packageRepository', or its source default, over HTTPS without proxy or redirect and never from another repository"
- `specs/ceph.md:828-829`: "Authentication, token exchanges and manifest reads connect only to the frozen registry authority."
- `specs/api/machines.md:492-498`: "A Machine choice carries controller acquisition and installed-system repository traffic ... Each executable consumer defines how it uses this Machine-owned egress choice."

#### REC-54 Ingress firewall check reads only runtime state, passing permits cephadm's reload erases

Medium; unsafe-rule; changes spec-text; effort S; source L25-3; related [ARC-15](#arc-15), [REC-115](#rec-115).

**Claim.** The ingress check reads only the runtime zone. cephadm then reloads firewalld with --permanent rules after the check, so a VRRP or port permit that exists only at runtime passes the check and is lost before keepalived runs. ceph-coverage.md:396-397 also says the check catches every drop, but rich-rule rejects and source-bound drop zones are not evaluated. The enabled-but-inactive case concerns a reboot after hand-off, which is outside the day-0 scope, and the check runs again on every apply.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/ceph.md:2060-2061`: "It reads each one's runtime firewalld zone, or the default zone for an interface bound to none, and refuses"
- `specs/ceph.md:2078-2079`: "so a permit given only that way refuses. An inactive or failed 'firewalld.service' passes"
- `specs/ceph-coverage.md:387-389`: "opens each deployed daemon's TCP endpoint ports with 'firewall-cmd --permanent --add-port' in firewalld's default zone and then reloads"

**Consequence.** An operator on a host Bootwright did not install opens VRRP with a runtime-only `firewall-cmd --add-protocol=vrrp`. The check passes, then cephadm deploys keepalived and reloads firewalld, which drops VRRP. The result is a split brain that the holder proof finds only after effects, as holders@.

**Recommendation.** In ceph.md, under Ingress host firewall, require each permit in both the runtime and the permanent configuration of the evaluated zone, the same way os-host-firewall-evidence-v1 already does. Refuse `ingress-firewall` naming 'runtime only' when the permanent configuration lacks a permit. State that denials from rich rules, source-bound zones, policies and direct rules are not detected, and that the virtual IP holder proof is the backstop. Change ceph-coverage.md:396-397 to 'when an evaluated zone does not permit any of them'.

**Acceptance.** ceph.md states that permits are checked in runtime and permanent configuration and how enabled-inactive firewalld is handled. ceph-coverage.md no longer promises detection of every drop. The shared fixture corpus has a runtime-only-permit case that refuses.

<a id="rec-55"></a>

#### REC-55 Stale-condition rule has no threshold and an unclear effect

Medium; ambiguity; changes spec-text; effort S; source L26-4.

**Claim.** specs/add-ons.md Readiness says a condition 'unchanged long after its object's other conditions' is stale but gives no interval, no timestamp field to compare, and no outcome for an observation. 'Never decides' does mostly mean that the condition neither satisfies nor fails the check, but the `condition` row of the check table does not say so.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/add-ons.md:402-403`: "A condition unchanged long after its object's other conditions is reported as stale and never decides."
- `.agents/knowledge/kubernetes-object-ownership-with-oc.md:157-158`: "flagging conditions more than five minutes behind it (L1-09); no remedy was built."

**Consequence.** One implementer treats a stale Available=True as not ready, so the check fails at the deadline. Another skips it, so the check passes on other conditions. A third picks a different threshold. Readiness verdicts then differ between builds, which also breaks the 'same request' continuation guarantee across builds.

**Recommendation.** In add-ons.md Readiness and in the `condition` row, define staleness only for objects whose conditions report a heartbeat (lastHeartbeatTime or lastUpdateTime). A condition is stale when its heartbeat is more than a fixed program-version interval (five minutes) behind the newest heartbeat among the object's other conditions. A stale condition neither satisfies nor fails its check, so in an apply the check stays unmet, and in an observation it is unknown. Without heartbeat fields, staleness does not apply. Cover the interval with a program-version constant and a test.

**Acceptance.** add-ons.md states the threshold, the clock it is measured against and the effect on the check. A program-version constant and test hold it.

**Decisions and principles.** Decisions read by the judge: D11, D99, D173. Principles applied: P28, P29, P33, P40.

#### REC-56 Interrupted first binding leaves an unattributable controller directory with no exit

Medium; gap; changes spec-text; effort S; source X01-1; related [REC-05](#rec-05), [REC-72](#rec-72).

**Claim.** The Descriptor section opens a crash window: the reservation is published, then `controller/record/` is created, then a second publication records its identity. A crash inside that window leaves a directory that is refused as unattributable, and no exit is named. `controller uninstall --discard-unreadable` does not cover this case, because it refuses while the registry names a context, and the first binding happens during a context's apply. This is a recovery gap that fails closed, not a false promise.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/contexts/controller-record.md:40-42`: "Its reservation precedes directory creation; a second publication records the actual directory identity, and the mode becomes 'ready' once the first record is"
- `specs/contexts/controller-record.md:43-45`: "An unattributable directory after a crash is preserved and refuses adoption with 'context.state', "existing controller directory cannot be adopted""
- `specs/contexts.md:289-289`: "or a 'record/' no descriptor declares refuses the store"

**Consequence.** Suppose a SIGKILL or power loss hits the first `apply` on a fresh controller after `mkdir controller/record/` but before the registry records its identity. From then on, every apply on that host that needs a binding refuses with `context.state`, "existing controller directory cannot be adopted", and no remedy is given.

**Recommendation.** In the Descriptor section, attribute an unrecorded directory by its emptiness instead of refusing it. Sentence to add: "While the descriptor reads `initializing` with no directory identity, a `controller/record/` that is a private root `0700` directory on the store's device and holds nothing is what an interrupted first binding left: the next binding records its identity and proceeds. **Acceptance.** specs/contexts/controller-record.md#descriptor states the outcome of a crash between directory creation and the identity publication, and the refusal it keeps names an exit. A test along the lines of `TestAnInterruptedFirstBindingIsFinishedByTheNextBinding` is cited.

<a id="rec-61"></a>

#### REC-61 Reinstalled-guest removal records unregistration complete while the service consumer remains

Medium; gap; changes stored-state; effort S; source X04-4; related [REC-112](#rec-112).

**Claim.** A registering installation's removal treats a Machine that answers with another marker, or none, as holding nothing of this installation, and records its completion. The subscription-service consumer that the apply created and recorded is never removed and is never reported.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/managed-os.md:632-633`: "a Machine that answers with another marker or none holds nothing of this installation"
- `specs/managed-os.md:687-689`: "no registration of this installation left, which is an 'absent' or 'foreign' registration or a Machine holding another marker or none, is its completion"
- `specs/managed-os.md:1141-1142`: "removes only a consumer this installation's record names, owned or 'pending', with 'subscription-manager unregister'"

**Consequence.** Someone reinstalls a bare-metal Machine outside Bootwright after a completed apply. Destroy reads the new marker, withdraws the content and records completion. The consumer (with its recorded UUID) stays registered on the subscription service, holding an entitlement and colliding with a later registration of the same hardware.

**Recommendation.** In managed-os.md Registration Removal, add: when the guest answers with another marker or none, and the apply recorded a consumer UUID, the removal still completes and withdraws the content, but records the registration `orphaned` with that UUID. Its human and JSON result name the consumer, with the remedy 'remove it with the subscription service's own tools'. Add `orphaned` to the completing outcomes listed at managed-os.md:1157-1159.

**Acceptance.** A removal test over a guest answering with another marker records `orphaned` with the consumer UUID, and the human result names it. managed-os.md:1157-1159 lists the new outcome.

**Decisions and principles.** Decisions read by the judge: D37, D38, D167, D192. Principles applied: none recorded.

**Verification.** refuter confirmed; judge confirmed at Medium; recommendation amended by the judge.

<a id="rec-62"></a>

#### REC-62 An interrupted destroy has no exit under build or runtime skew except orphaning

Medium; gap; changes spec-text; effort M; source X05-1; related [REC-96](#rec-96).

**Claim.** controller.md's execution-closure paragraph lists "the destroy that takes back what it owns" as a remedy for every continuation refused for another lock or ABI. The owning text in state-reconciliation.md gives that remedy only for an apply. The state table and cli.md's status rules let a running or unknown destroy only be continued, and under closure skew they offer it no other step. So for an interrupted destroy, the controller.md remedy just repeats a continuation that refuses again.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/state-reconciliation.md:1901-1903`: "A running or unknown removal is continued rather than replaced, because a removal that lost an outcome is resolved by repeating itself."
- `specs/state-reconciliation.md:1348-1349`: "when this build's runtime carries another closure (another runtime lock or another interpreter ABI), naming the build that registered it"
- `specs/state-reconciliation.md:1351-1352`: "and for an apply the removal that takes back what it owns"

**Consequence.** Durable state: a destroy registered under build A is interrupted (Ctrl-C, host reboot) halfway through a Ceph and OpenShift fleet. Event: the operator upgrades to build B, whose runtime lock differs (the recent wheel-trim change moved it), or the OS upgrade moves the Python ABI to one A carries no wheels for, or A has been replaced on ...

**Recommendation.** In specs/controller.md:983-984, change "or the destroy that takes back what it owns" to "and, for an apply, the destroy that takes back what it owns", so the summary matches state-reconciliation.md:1351-1352. Whether a fresh removal should supersede a running removal under closure skew is a separate design question for the owner; raise it as its own backlog item, not as a correction to this text.

**Acceptance.** The state-machine rows for destroy running and destroy unknown name a superseding fresh removal under skew. controller.md:977-983 and state-reconciliation.md:1346-1352 give the same exits for both verbs.

**Decisions and principles.** Decisions read by the judge: D41, D142, D145, D146, D152, D248. Principles applied: P22, P26, P40.

**Verification.** refuter narrowed; judge confirmed at High; third reading: holds-lower, then arbitrated: keep at Medium.

<a id="rec-63"></a>

#### REC-63 A failed add-on addition forces destroying the whole environment

Medium; design; changes spec-text; effort S; source X05-3, X09-3; related [DOC-16](#doc-16), [REC-03](#rec-03), [REC-13](#rec-13), [REC-14](#rec-14), [REC-64](#rec-64), [REC-70](#rec-70), [REC-91](#rec-91).

**Claim.** The exit design is decided. What is missing is disclosure: neither the additive-apply section nor the operator guide's 'Add one later' bullet says that a failed or interrupted addition cannot be fixed by editing the input, because the update guard refuses while the operation is failed. Its only exits are continuing over the frozen input, a destroy of the whole lineage, or an orphan-acknowledged deletion. An operator has to piece this together from the guard rule and the lifecycle table.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/state-reconciliation.md:204-206`: "One 'destroy' takes the whole lineage back (removal over a lineage); no removal takes back an additive apply alone."
- `specs/state-reconciliation.md:313-313`: "The guard allows update only without pending, failed or unknown operations;"
- `specs/state-reconciliation.md:577-577`: "every fresh destroy these rows start also takes back the whole frozen plan of each predecessor"

**Consequence.** Durable state: a completed apply of OpenShift, Ceph and Data Foundation. Event: the operator adds a GitOps binding with a typo in its channel. The additive apply fails at the Subscription. Retrying fails the same way, because the input is frozen. A context update to fix the typo is refused because the operation is failed.

**Recommendation.** Add one sentence to the Additive apply section of specs/state-reconciliation.md and to the operator guide's 'Add one later' bullet: a failed or interrupted additive apply admits no input update. It is continued over its frozen input, or taken back with its whole lineage by one destroy, so check the added binding (plan, validate) before applying. A plan-preview line and its golden are optional. Do not open a new item: extend B769's revive condition to name the head-only removal of a failed addition, since it shares that item's prerequisite (online instance removal).

**Acceptance.** The additive-apply section, the cli-plan-adds golden and the operator guide state the failure exits. A milestone item names the head-only removal, its prerequisite B769 and its owner decision.

**Decisions and principles.** Decisions read by the judge: D153, D173, D210, D211. Principles applied: none recorded.

**Verification.** refuter narrowed; judge narrowed at Medium; recommendation amended by the judge; merged from 2 candidates (X05-3 Medium, X09-3 Medium).

**Merged candidates.** The entry states the defect as its clearest candidate put it; these raised the same defect, sometimes a further instance or aspect of it: X09-3: A failed additive add-on can be abandoned only by destroying everything.

#### REC-64 Same-blocks proof does not say how it applies to additive applies

Medium; ambiguity; changes spec-text; effort S; source X05-4; related [CLI-01](#cli-01), [CLI-09](#cli-09), [REC-03](#rec-03), [REC-29](#rec-29), [REC-63](#rec-63), [REC-70](#rec-70), [REC-91](#rec-91).

**Claim.** Dependency safety proves that another build freezes the same blocks by planning the operation's frozen input again and getting exactly the operation's blocks. An additive apply freezes the whole selected revision but its plan holds only the added blocks, so a literal re-plan also produces the lineage blocks and can never match.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/state-reconciliation.md:1357-1359`: "a build freezes the same blocks when planning the operation's frozen input again gives exactly the operation's blocks, each with every member its plan froze ..."
- `specs/state-reconciliation.md:190-193`: "Its plan holds only the added blocks, and their edges into the lineage are frozen as 'prerequisites', which scheduling never counts. It freezes the whole ..."
- `specs/state-reconciliation.md:178-179`: "comparison of the lineage's plan with that plan shows every lineage block the same and at least one block added"

**Consequence.** An interrupted additive apply is continued under an automation-fix build. One implementer compares the full re-plan with the operation's plan, so the continuation always refuses and the fix cannot reach the failed added block: the operator has to reinstall the registering build or destroy the whole lineage.

**Recommendation.** In Dependency safety during recovery, add one sentence: for an additive apply, the proof plans its frozen input again and requires that the blocks the plan adds beyond its lineage, with their frozen prerequisites, are exactly the operation's blocks, each compared on every member except the words it is presented in. Link admission's "every lineage block the same" (state-reconciliation.md:177-180) to that same rule. In m4.md B987, replace "frozen byte for byte" with a link to the rule. Name no code symbol in the spec.

**Acceptance.** In specs/state-reconciliation.md, Dependency safety during recovery states the same-blocks proof for an additive apply in terms of the added blocks and their prerequisites, using the presentation-word exclusion. The Additive apply admission bullet links to that rule.

#### REC-65 A vanished keyring in a ready context reads as uninitialized

Medium; ambiguity; changes spec-text; effort S; source X06-3.

**Claim.** Lifecycle verbs are already covered: a store never initialized lists none, and a listing that answers without the binding is a lost binding (state-reconciliation.md continuation and removal, D37), so destroy and continuation already name the two exits. The gap is the other commands. Over a ready context whose secrets/ is empty or absent, secret encryption status, list, set, capture and init treat the store as uninitialized rather than lost, and init silently creates a fresh keyring inside a context that already has effects.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/secrets.md:17-19`: "Context creation initializes that implementation through a transaction-scoped Workspace area before ready publication"
- `specs/secrets.md:447-447`: "of the enclosing registry format. Empty or absent means uninitialized."
- `specs/secrets.md:298-299`: "reveals no material or version, and a store never initialized lists none."

**Consequence.** Walkthrough. A cleanup script, or a restore that missed the directory, empties `contexts/<name>/secrets/` of a context with a done apply. `secret encryption status` reports `initialized: false`, `secret list` is empty, `cluster kubeconfig` returns `access.unavailable` with the next action `apply`, and `secret set` returns ...

**Recommendation.** In secrets.md Local keyring, after 'Empty or absent means uninitialized.', add: 'only inside context creation's transaction. In a context the registry records as ready, an empty or absent secrets/ is a lost keyring: every access, secret encryption init included, refuses with secret.store.corrupt and names the same two exits, and a lifecycle verb or status that meets it reports a lost binding as for corruption.' Then change the 'store never initialized' wording at lines 135, 298 and 368 to point to this rule. Add a test showing that init refuses over a wiped keyring in a ready context.

**Acceptance.** secrets.md distinguishes 'never initialized' (only during creation) from 'lost' (in a ready context), and a test (for example TestAWipedKeyringOfAReadyContextIsLostNotUninitialized) asserts that init refuses.

**Decisions and principles.** Decisions read by the judge: D25, D37, D68, D85, D118. Principles applied: none recorded.

#### REC-66 MAC-set predicate never says which Redfish MAC property counts

Medium; ambiguity; changes spec-text; effort S; source X07-4; related [REC-85](#rec-85).

**Claim.** The one MAC-set predicate in state-reconciliation#physical-disk-safety, and the Redfish target proof in substrates.md that relies on it, compare "the MACs the system reports" with the declared set for exact equality. Neither says whether a member's MACAddress, its PermanentMACAddress or both count. The Redfish adapter adds both to the observed set, so a member whose two values differ contributes an address the Machine does not declare, while the kernel-side proof takes one address per port: the permanent address for a bond port.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/state-reconciliation.md:2446-2448`: "The live MAC set matches when the MACs the system reports for its own network ports, a management controller's host interface excepted, are exactly those ..."
- `specs/substrates.md:777-778`: "reads the system's complete 'EthernetInterfaces' collection and requires the MACs it reports to equal the set the Machine declares"
- `ansible/collections/ansible_collections/bootwright/core/plugins/module_utils/redfish_discovery.py:383-383`: "found = [canonical_mac(member.get(field)) for field in ("MACAddress", "PermanentMACAddress")]"

**Consequence.** The text calls this one predicate, but the controller-side Redfish proof and the in-OS proof implement it differently. A BMC whose MACAddress differs from PermanentMACAddress, whether through a configured or virtual MAC or by reporting the current address after MAC-changing bonding (which the qualification matrix says to re-prove), gets ...

**Recommendation.** In the MAC-set predicate at state-reconciliation#physical-disk-safety, define each port's address as its permanent hardware address. On Redfish that is PermanentMACAddress when the member reports one, else MACAddress. On the kernel side (installer %pre, RAM erase worker, Ceph host runtime) it is the device's permanent address, perm_hwaddr for a bond port, never an OS-assigned one. Point substrates#physical-machine-realization to this rule. Change redfish_discovery to take one address per member instead of the union.

**Acceptance.** state-reconciliation#physical-disk-safety names the per-port address source for Redfish and for the kernel side, and substrates.md's target proof links to it. redfish_discovery.py adds one address per member, preferring PermanentMACAddress.

<a id="rec-67"></a>

#### REC-67 Erase refusal on a replaced or removed target names no next action

Medium; gap; changes spec-text; effort S; source X07-5.

**Claim.** The erase section already says a missing or replaced target refuses before the first write: a serial-only target with no matching disk refuses, drift refuses, and every target is opened before any write. The gap is narrower than claimed. No passage names the next action for that refusal, as Mutation safety requires. A changed disk cannot be put into the frozen plan. So the only remedies are to restore the original disk and repeat destroy, or to abandon the context with --allow-orphans, and neither is stated.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/state-reconciliation.md:2587-2589`: "Identity drift, short writes, failed readback and unavailable probes refuse without selecting another disk."
- `specs/state-reconciliation.md:2313-2314`: "Every refusal identifies the target, evidence, safety reason, and safe next action. It never invents a force command."
- `specs/substrates.md:1005-1007`: "A block changed after installation reaches the machine only through destroy and a fresh installation, because a context continues its frozen plan."

**Consequence.** A data disk fails in service and is swapped, so its serial changes. `bootwright destroy` reaches the erase block, the RAM worker refuses before the first write, and every retry refuses the same way. The context cannot be removed.

**Recommendation.** In state-reconciliation#opt-in-physical-logical-overwrite, add one sentence: a target that no whole disk matches by its frozen identity (missing or replaced) refuses with nothing written. The refusal names the target and its next actions: restore the original disk and repeat destroy, or run `context delete --purge --allow-orphans`, which abandons every erase target unerased. Do not add a separate erase inventory to the orphan confirmation. That confirmation already cites status and diff as the inventory, and they show the erase block as not done.

**Acceptance.** The erase section names the refusal code and both remedies. The contexts.md orphan inventory lists unerased erase targets. A failure-injection test removes a target between installation and destroy.

**Decisions and principles.** Decisions read by the judge: D177, D198, D225. Principles applied: P15, P22, P26, P31.

**Verification.** refuter narrowed; judge narrowed at Medium; recommendation amended by the judge.

Medium; gap; changes api-shape; effort S; source Z01-2; related [API-145](#api-145), [COR-16](#cor-16), [COR-88](#cor-88).

**Claim.** The removal of a provided tiebreaker refuses `tiebreaker-foreign` when the host holds any daemon or `/var/lib/ceph` directory of another FSID. No rule states that a Machine serves as a node of only one CephCluster, and nothing before the claim checks a provided tiebreaker for another FSID's layout: the positive-absence proof covers only the bootstrap target, and the reservation sentence defers coordination between contexts to B79.

- `specs/ceph.md:2361-2363`: "Reservations prevent conflicting local contexts from claiming the same target; a native name, process-local mutex or context lease alone cannot coordinate another controller."

**Consequence.** An operator points stretch clusters in two contexts at one third-site provided host. The second cluster's host block claims that host and places its own daemons there (its crash collector at least), because no step refuses the first cluster's MON.

**Recommendation.** In secrets.md 'Material placed in a cluster', change the first sentence to: 'A declared Secret reaches a cluster as an owned Secret of a block that binds it, or as an installer input the installation's native installer places itself: the install pull secret with its mirror entries and, on vSphere, the cluster's vcenterCredentials (effect material, see api/openshift-clusters.md#platform-union-and-derivation).' Then extend the outside-custody and rotation sentences to cover these copies. Link the embedded image's confidentiality to openshift-clusters.md#boot-media.

**Acceptance.** secrets.md no longer says 'only as an owned Secret'. It names the installer-placed pull secret and vCenter credentials and states what renewal does to them. state-reconciliation.md's rebind section classifies the vCenter login the installation embeds.

**Decisions and principles.** Decisions read by the judge: D4, D124, D138. Principles applied: none recorded.

**Verification.** refuter narrowed; judge narrowed at Medium; recommendation amended by the judge.

<a id="rec-76"></a>

#### REC-76 Orphan deletion confirmation omits declared recovery passphrases abandoned Machines still need

Medium; gap; changes spec-text; effort S; source Z08-3; related [REC-12](#rec-12), [REC-60](#rec-60).

**Claim.** An orphan-acknowledged deletion abandons running objects but still removes the keyring, and its confirmation names only produced material such as the administrator kubeconfig with its export command. It names no declared effect-material Secret an abandoned Machine still depends on, notably a generated disk recovery passphrase that is lost with the keyring.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/contexts.md:956-958`: "It still removes the keyring, and with it the produced material no completed removal withdrew, such as the administrator kubeconfig"
- `specs/secrets.md:321-323`: "Effect material is placed in or derived into an effect, as a disk recovery passphrase, a delivered host key or a generated certificate is"
- `specs/managed-os.md:1540-1541`: "Bootwright offers no command that reveals a bound version, so the operator keeps the value the installation bound."

**Consequence.** Take an operator who orphan-deletes a context whose Machines still run TPM-bound encrypted roots with a generated recovery passphrase. The confirmation tells them to export the kubeconfig and nothing else. After the deletion the keyring is gone, and so is the only copy of the passphrase.

**Recommendation.** In contexts.md permanent deletion, after the produced-material sentence, add one sentence. The orphan confirmation also names each declared effect-material Secret an abandoned object bound, such as a disk recovery passphrase, with the export `bootwright secret show --name <secret> --part <part>`, which reveals the bound value only while the declaration is unchanged. A lost context's confirmation names none. Extend TestTheOrphanAcknowledgementAbandonsAContextWhoseEvidenceCannotBeRead to assert the Secret's name. In the managed-os.md Custody paragraph, link to this exit.

**Acceptance.** contexts.md permanent deletion says the orphan confirmation names declared effect-material Secrets of abandoned objects, with the `secret show` export and the lost-context exception. managed-os.md Custody links to it. The named test asserts the Secret's name in the confirmation.

**Decisions and principles.** Decisions read by the judge: D4, D25, D37, D38, D88, D89, D123, D124. Principles applied: P1, P26, P40.

**Verification.** refuter narrowed; judge confirmed at Medium; recommendation amended by the judge; extent arbitrated: a narrower claim at Medium.

<a id="rec-77"></a>

#### REC-77 Pool readiness reads rule, profile and compression; diff never compares them

Medium; gap; changes spec-text; effort M; source Z13-2; related [CLI-10](#cli-10), [REC-52](#rec-52).

**Claim.** The CephPool projection covers six fields, but readiness and the pool-drift refusal cover more: compression options, rule, EC profile and stripe unit, bulk and PG count. So `diff --observe` lists those paths as not compared, even when their drift is exactly what blocks the next apply or what a D230 disaster-recovery drill must bring back into the desired state. The diff is honest: those paths are reported as not compared, not hidden. This is a coverage gap, not a contradiction.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/ceph.md:1471-1473`: "Pool readiness compares every frozen attribute (type, rule, size, minimum size, profile and stripe width, overwrites, bulk, autoscale mode"
- `specs/state-reconciliation.md:2248-2248`: "'spec.replicated.size', 'spec.replicated.minSize', 'spec.application', 'spec.autoscale.mode', 'spec.quota.maxBytes', 'spec.quota.maxObjects' | a pool's own block"
- `specs/state-reconciliation.md:2196-2198`: "Every authored leaf path of the applied object that no fragment carries, shallowest first, is listed as not compared"

**Consequence.** Suppose a pool is moved to another CRUSH rule by hand, or its compression or EC profile is changed. `diff --observe` shows the CephPool as unchanged with those paths 'not compared', and at most a 'not ready' note.

**Recommendation.** Record a new M2 item that follows B600 instead of editing the specs directly. It covers: return the live rule, EC profile name and stripe unit, bulk flag, PG count when the autoscaler is off, and each declared compression option in the pool observation; extend the storage-ceph-core-v1 CephPool row in specs/state-reconciliation.md with spec.erasure.stripeUnit, spec.autoscale.bulk and spec.compression.* (dataChunks and codingChunks only through the profile readback); report a rule or placement mismatch as a note, never a projected reference.

**Acceptance.** The observable-fields row lists the added paths. A projection test on a pool whose live rule or compression mode differs from the frozen value yields a field difference or the rule note, not 'not compared' alone.

**Decisions and principles.** Decisions read by the judge: D153, D155, D230. Principles applied: none recorded.

**Verification.** refuter narrowed; judge narrowed at Medium; recommendation amended by the judge.

<a id="rec-78"></a>

#### REC-78 Controller record's 4 MiB bound pre-empts the 256-reservation bound and its remedy

Medium; gap; changes spec-text; effort S; source Z14-3; related [CON-22](#con-22).

**Claim.** controller-record.md admits that the 4 MiB state bound is reached before 256 reservations of maximal keys. That publication refuses only 'as an encoding-limit state error', while the 256-entry bound refuses with controller.conflict, the entries other contexts hold, and the remedy to take back a context. The worst-case exhaustion therefore gets the remedy-less outcome.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/contexts/controller-record.md:134-136`: "The 4 MiB state bound is reached before 256 reservations of 128 maximal keys, and a publication past it refuses as an encoding-limit state error, ..."
- `specs/contexts/controller-record.md:137-139`: "An apply whose reservations would take the record past 256 entries refuses with 'controller.conflict' before it publishes them, naming that bound"

**Consequence.** A controller hosting many contexts with large SSH-placed claims (about 128 reservations of 128 keys of 256 bytes) fails apply with an opaque state error. The operator gets no hint that deleting another context frees room, and the documented 256 bound and its test cover a case that cannot be reached first.

**Recommendation.** Keep the 256-entry bound and drop the option of lowering it, because lowering it would cut capacity for the common case of small claims. In specs/contexts/controller-record.md, replace 'refuses as an encoding-limit state error, writing nothing' with: an apply whose reservations would take the encoded record past 4 MiB refuses with controller.conflict before it publishes them, naming the byte bound, the bytes it needs and the bytes other contexts hold, with the same take-back remedy (destroy --context or context delete --purge).

**Acceptance.** Both exhaustion paths of a reservation publication yield controller.conflict with the take-back remedy, and a test like TestReservationsPastTheRecordByteBoundRefuseBeforePublication pins it.

**Decisions and principles.** Decisions read by the judge: D38, D92, D184, D186, D188. Principles applied: P12, P15, P26, P36.

**Verification.** refuter confirmed; judge confirmed at Medium; recommendation amended by the judge.

<a id="rec-79"></a>

#### REC-79 Insert bound differs between substrates and managed-OS by seven minutes

Medium; duplication; changes spec-text; effort S; source Z14-5; related [REC-145](#rec-145).

**Claim.** The insert figure in substrates.md:1503 (39 minutes 20 seconds) is stale. ControllerInsertBound in internal/substrate/redfish.go always includes the certificate-import allowance of 14 requests at 30 s, and redfish_test.go pins it as 46m20s in a test named 'the figures the specifications state'. Delivered B449 also records 46m20s. The arm therefore publishes an understated insert bound, and managed-os.md has to restate the seven minutes. There is no conditional second bound.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/substrates.md:1454-1456`: "Each arm publishes the worst-case bound of every entry point and the share of a boot budget one node's boot takes, as constants its consumers ..."
- `specs/substrates.md:1503-1504`: "an insert by 39 minutes 20 seconds, the release of any other media before its first attach, three attaches with their polls"
- `specs/managed-os.md:535-536`: "fourteen bounded requests, seven additional minutes at the thirty-second request timeout"

**Consequence.** A consumer that sums the published constants as substrates tells it to (an OpenShift node on another Machine that freezes importCertificate) under-counts its insert by seven minutes; the two pages drift whenever the certificate flow changes.

**Recommendation.** In substrates.md#identity-and-power-operations, replace 'an insert by 39 minutes 20 seconds' with 'an insert by 46 minutes 20 seconds' and add certificate import to its list: eight collection members, five setup requests and one 412 retry. In managed-os.md:534-536, drop the separate seven-minute recount and say that the insert bound includes certificate import. Do not introduce two conditional bounds, because the code has one unconditional bound.

**Acceptance.** One page owns the insert bound with its certificate-import term; managed-os.md's 1 h 17 min 20 s arithmetic cites it.

**Decisions and principles.** Decisions read by the judge: D103, D104, D121. Principles applied: P22.

**Verification.** refuter confirmed; judge narrowed at Medium; recommendation amended by the judge.

### 12.9 Language responsibility

<a id="lng-01"></a>

#### LNG-01 Remote-run Python copy worker sits outside every language row and test

Medium; gap; changes code-structure; effort S; source R11-4; related [ARC-17](#arc-17), [LNG-03](#lng-03), [LNG-04](#lng-04).

**Claim.** internal/machine/sshlocal/copy_worker.py (419 lines) runs on a Machine through the pinned SSH session, with a stated 3.9 floor. It matches no language row (the Python row is 'in the collection'). The language-row test does not scan internal/. Neither test_remote_python_floor.py nor test_python_sites.py references it. So the floor, process-start and encoding rules the spec states for managed-host Python are not held for it.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/architecture.md:175-176`: "Explicit file copying uses its fixed descriptor-relative Python worker through that same pinned session,"
- `specs/architecture.md:782-784`: "A module runs under the managed-host Python floor, 3.9, which 'test_remote_python_floor.py' holds; a shipped worker runs as '/usr/bin/python3'"
- `specs/cli/machine-copy.md:34-34`: "Both endpoints require Linux with Python 3.9 or newer and procfs; no remote sudo occurs."

**Consequence.** An edit that adds a 3.10 construct such as match or a parenthesized context manager, or a subprocess call, to the copy worker passes every gate. It then fails or misbehaves on a RHEL 9 guest during an operator's machine copy, on a path that writes to the target's filesystem.

**Recommendation.** Add 'Python in the executable' to the table: Holds 'a fixed worker Go ships as source and runs on a Machine or locally (machine/sshlocal)', Never 'imports beyond the standard library, starts a process, or uses syntax above the managed-host floor'. Extend inSourceRoot to `internal/**/*.py`, and add the file to the floor and sites tests or a Go-side ast check.

**Acceptance.** TestEveryCollectionAndScriptSourceMapsToALanguageRow maps internal/machine/sshlocal/copy_worker.py to a named row. A floor test parses it under the 3.9 grammar.

**Decisions and principles.** Decisions read by the judge: none found to bear on it. Principles applied: P40.

**Verification.** refuter confirmed; judge confirmed at Medium.

**Low findings: language responsibility.** Each was verified like the others and is given in one row with its first citation; the Value column is the judge's estimate of what fixing it is worth to the owner.

### 12.10 Spec corpus as an agent harness

<a id="cor-01"></a>

#### COR-01 Agent effect ban omits destructive local commands that refusals themselves recommend

High; unsafe-rule; changes agent-guidance; effort S; source Z11-1, H01-1; related [CLI-20](#cli-20), [COR-36](#cor-36), [COR-90](#cor-90), [SKL-01](#skl-01), [SKL-02](#skl-02), [SKL-11](#skl-11).

**Claim.** AGENTS.md defines the commands an agent may not run unasked as "a Bootwright command with effects", followed by an inline list. The list leaves out `controller rebind`, which .claude/settings.json asks for, even though the skill index says settings asks before exactly the commands AGENTS.md forbids. Read literally, "with effects" also covers Local-class commands such as `context delete --purge --allow-orphans`, which permanently abandons live objects and deletes the context's secrets/. But askRuleNoAsk exempts that command, along with secret delete, encryption rotate and media delete, so the agent is never asked. Nothing decides which reading is meant.

**Evidence.**

- `AGENTS.md:29-31`: "Agents never run 'ansible-playbook' against a host, or a Bootwright command with effects ('apply', 'destroy', 'controller install'/'uninstall', 'media add', 'machine' or 'cluster' sessions, power or ..."
- `.claude/settings.json:47-47`: ""Bash(*bootwright *controller rebind*)","
- `specs/cli/commands.md:88-88`: "required '--name &lt;name>' and '--purge'; '--allow-orphans' and '--yes' false | permanent local deletion summary, saying whether it abandoned objects"
- `specs/contexts.md:711-711`: "'--allow-orphans', which abandons what the context may still own, and then the"
- `e2e/lab-rhel/runbook.md:349-349`: "./bin/bootwright context delete --name "$CONTEXT" --purge --yes"
- `.agents/skills/index.md:33-34`: "Codex needs the same commands under its own approval policy, which this repository does not track."

**Consequence.** Suppose an agent follows a refusal's printed remedy or a runbook's cleanup step. It can run `context delete --purge --allow-orphans --yes` without asking anyone. That permanently drops the ownership evidence for VMs, disks and clusters that still exist, so `destroy` can no longer remove them. Codex reads only AGENTS.md and gets no prompt at all, and Claude Code gets none either because no ask rule matches.

**Recommendation.** In AGENTS.md, define the forbidden set by pointing to the catalog's Effects column instead of an inline list, or name `controller rebind` and irreversible local changes (context delete, secret delete, secret encryption rotate, media delete) explicitly. Leave context init/update and secret set/generate unasked. Add ask rules for those four commands to .claude/settings.json in the B1219 grouped form (for example `Bash(*bootwright *context *delete*)`), and move them from askRuleNoAsk to a marker class for irreversible local changes.

**Acceptance.** AGENTS.md names, by class, every catalog command whose Effects cell is a write. settings.json has an ask rule for each of them. TestDocsAskRulesCoverEveryEffectfulCommand fails if a catalog row with a local write or deletion has no rule.

**Decisions and principles.** Decisions read by the judge: D37, D38, D69, D88, D89, D155, D182, D183. Principles applied: P32, P42, P44. Finder's check: Searched the skills and docs/development.md for any fuller list of effects: there is none, and code-implementation only says it 'never authorizes ... a command with effects'. X161 (delivered.md:8618) defines the test's notion of effects as 'planned mutation, host packages, downloads, SSH, power or a reveal', which leaves out local deletion. B1219 tracks only the group-flag position gap.

**Verification.** refuter narrowed; judge narrowed at High; recommendation amended by the judge; third reading: holds; merged from 2 candidates (Z11-1 High, H01-1 High).

**Demonstration (third reading).** AGENTS.md forbids any command "with effects" and lists apply, destroy, controller install/uninstall, media add, sessions, power and trust. Both commands below have effects in the catalog. 1. `controller rebind` performs a "host identity rewrite" (commands.md:149). settings.json:47 asks for it and the skill index says that set equals what AGENTS.md forbids, but the AGENTS.md list omits it. A Codex agent, whose approval policy the repository does not track, gets two answers. 2. `context delete` performs a "guarded removal" (commands.md:88). Read literally, AGENTS.md forbids it. The test treats it as Local and exempts it, so Claude Code runs `context delete --purge --allow-orphans --yes` with no prompt. That run abandons live Machines and deletes secrets/, the only copy of generated material. contexts.md:905 names this command as the exit an agent sees in the refusal.

**Merged candidates.** The entry states the defect as its clearest candidate put it; these raised the same defect, sometimes a further instance or aspect of it: H01-1: AGENTS.md effect ban omits context deletion and diverges from ask list.

<a id="cor-02"></a>

#### COR-02 Not yet met lines stay linked to items whose code is already delivered in-tree

High; contradiction; changes spec-text; effort S; source H03-1; related [COR-33](#cor-33), [COR-65](#cor-65), [DOC-01](#doc-01), [SCO-01](#sco-01).

**Claim.** The Not yet met lines for B721 (security.md), B67 (openshift-coverage.md) and B760 (api/environment.md) still describe code behaviour that each item's own page says was delivered in-tree on 2026-10-23 (the items are now 'awaiting operator acceptance'). So the specs give opposite answers about current behaviour: physical nodes install and also refuse, and the image build uses the proxy route and also runs direct. TestDocsNotYetMetNamesAnUndeliveredItem rejects only rows whose Delivery cell starts 'completed', so make docs-check passes these stale lines.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/security.md:420-421`: "Not yet met: the image build runs direct; tracked as B721."
- `specs/milestones/m3.md:1214-1215`: "**In-tree delivery, 2026-10-23:** implementation and host-independent probes are delivered"
- `specs/openshift-coverage.md:70-71`: "Not yet met: a physical node and a multi-node vSphere cluster refuse; tracked as B67"
- `specs/openshift-clusters.md:39-40`: "A node whose realized target is physical installs through its management controller under the trust its Machine declares"
- `specs/api/environment.md:215-216`: "Not yet met: a package's configuration retains no export; tracked as B760."
- `specs/milestones/m4.md:1165-1165`: "**Delivery:** in-tree implementation complete; awaiting operator acceptance on B761."

**Consequence.** An agent asking 'is the physical-node install implemented?' reads 'refuse' on one page and 'installs' on the next. The delivered record says only the image build carries the proxy route, yet security.md says it runs direct, and the owner's acceptance gate then hides the contradiction. B301's stated aim, that specs record only what is still unmet, is unmet for every item that has passed its in-tree gates.

**Recommendation.** Retire the line at in-tree delivery: in specs/index.md Conventions and the milestones-and-knowledge skill, say that a Not yet met line is deleted or re-scoped in the commit that moves its item to 'awaiting operator acceptance'. The operator residue stays on the item, and D2's support claim stays in qualification and acceptance. Make notYetMetParagraph also flag a linked item whose Delivery cell starts 'awaiting operator acceptance'. Then delete the B721 and B760 lines, and cut the B67/B733 line down to the vSphere part (B733 is not started). Also fix the stale "A physical node refuses before registration" sentence at openshift-clusters.md:627.

**Acceptance.** specs/index.md and the skill name the trigger. Adding a test case 'awaiting row' to TestDocsNotYetMetMatcherRejectsBadParagraphs fails before the fix and passes after. make docs-check passes with no Not yet met line linking a row whose Delivery starts 'awaiting operator acceptance'.

**Decisions and principles.** Decisions read by the judge: D2. Principles applied: none recorded. Finder's check: Searched decisions.md and the backlog for B301 (delivered.md:3894-3900), which set the test to reject only 'completed'. Searched not-yet-met.txt and the items for a tracker of this test gap: none. milestones.md:76-78 makes in-tree delivery a distinct state, so the test rule is the gap.

**Verification.** refuter confirmed; judge confirmed at High; third reading: holds.

**Demonstration (third reading).** Question: does the image build run through the proxy today? security.md:415-418 says the installer "reaches the release payload through the controller Machine's proxy choice". Its line 420 says "Not yet met: the image build runs direct". B721 (m3.md:1212-1247) records that work as delivered in-tree, and the media role does pass request.buildEgress. Question: do physical nodes install? openshift-clusters.md:39-41 says they "install through [their] management controller". openshift-coverage.md:70 says a physical node "refuse[s]", and openshift-clusters.md:627 still says "A physical node refuses before registration, as selection states". B67 (m3.md:837-841) is delivered in-tree. B760 (m4.md:1165: "in-tree implementation complete") is contradicted the same way by environment.md:215.

<a id="cor-03"></a>

#### COR-03 Spec sentences that parked items call false carry no Not-yet-met line

High; contradiction; changes spec-text; effort S; source M03-1; related [COR-06](#cor-06), [COR-09](#cor-09), [COR-34](#cor-34).

**Claim.** Parked items B576 and B571 each record that a normative spec sentence is false: specs/substrates.md:588 says libvirt Machine completion requires the domain defined with the frozen definition, and specs/state-reconciliation.md:2362 says Bootwright removes only what is out of use. Neither sentence has the 'Not yet met: ...; tracked as B&lt;n>' line that specs/index.md requires, and no spec page outside the backlog links B571 or B576. Both items also cite stale spec line numbers (336 and 1787).

**Evidence.**

- `specs/milestones/backlog.md:1475-1475`: "The spec says completion "requires the domain defined with the frozen"
- `specs/milestones/backlog.md:1479-1480`: "It never reads back vCPU, memory, interfaces and MACs, TPM or boot order."
- `specs/substrates.md:588-588`: "**Evidence.** Completion requires the domain defined with the frozen definition"
- `specs/milestones/backlog.md:1435-1435`: "the consequence is not, and "removes only what is"
- `specs/state-reconciliation.md:2362-2362`: "Bootwright removes and replaces only what is out of use."
- `specs/index.md:52-53`: "A rule the code does not yet meet carries one line, "Not yet met: ...; tracked as B&lt;n>""

**Consequence.** An operator or coding agent reads state-reconciliation.md and believes destroy never takes a service from under a retained physical host, or that a completed libvirt Machine was read back field by field. B571 itself records that a retained bare-metal host loses DNS and NTP on destroy. Since AGENTS.md routes agents to specs and not the backlog, they will cite the false rule as a contract.

**Recommendation.** Add one Not-yet-met line after specs/substrates.md:588-605 (the Evidence paragraph). It says that completion evidence proves the domain name, ownership, unit, image, system UUID, power state and disks but not vCPU, memory, interfaces, TPM or boot order, that a redefinition reports unchanged, and that this is tracked as B576. Add one after specs/state-reconciliation.md:2362. It says that a retained physical Machine always answers quiescent, so destroy can remove a DNS, NTP or artifact server it still uses, and that this is tracked as B571. In both items, correct the stale line citations: 336 becomes 588 and 1787 becomes 2362.

**Acceptance.** specs/substrates.md and specs/state-reconciliation.md each hold a 'Not yet met' line linking B576 and B571; make docs-check passes. A grep of every parked item of Kind defect or safety whose body says a spec sentence is overstated finds a matching line in the owning spec.

**Decisions and principles.** Decisions read by the judge: D102, D153, D155. Principles applied: none recorded. Finder's check: Grepped specs for backlog.md#b576 and #b571 (no hits outside the backlog). D155 (decisions.md) accepts B576's correction for a future named slice, but that defers the code and spec fix, not the marker the Conventions section requires. Not-yet-met.txt has no B576/B571 line. Checked specs/substrates.md:365-375, where B567 does carry the line, so the convention is applied inconsistently.

**Verification.** refuter confirmed; judge confirmed at High; recommendation amended by the judge; third reading: holds.

**Demonstration (third reading).** The specs and the backlog give two answers for the same state. Case 1: a destroy that keeps a running physical host which uses a managed DNS or NTP service. specs/state-reconciliation.md:2362 says "removes and replaces only what is out of use", so the service stays. B571 says "Destroy therefore removes DNS, NTP and the artifact server from under a running, retained physical host". Case 2: a libvirt Machine reported complete. specs/substrates.md:588 says completion "requires the domain defined with the frozen definition". B576 says the evidence "never reads back vCPU, memory, interfaces and MACs, TPM or boot order", and that a redefinition is reported unchanged. specs/index.md:52-54 requires a Not-yet-met line for each such sentence. A grep of specs for b571 or b576 outside the backlog finds nothing, while the B567 and B568 lines nearby show how the marker is used.

#### COR-10 Pool-adoption relaxations from X81 are normative but live only in delivered.md

Medium; gap; changes spec-text; effort S; source M12-2; related [API-50](#api-50).

**Claim.** specs/ceph.md says a retry adopts a same-name pool on its attempt record and the frozen shape, naming PG count as part of that shape. X81 relaxed this on a safety path: a moved PG count is accepted when pg_autoscale_mode is on, and a same-name pool with no recorded ID but this operation's own attempt record is partial work, not an identity refusal. X81 also made a pool_id that is not a non-negative integer refuse native-output. None of these three rules appears in specs/ceph.md, and delivered.md is not a normative page.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/ceph.md:1444-1445`: "A retry adopts a same-name rule, profile or pool only with that record and the frozen shape"
- `specs/ceph.md:1447-1447`: "defaults, and the pool's type, rule and PG count."
- `specs/milestones/delivered.md:5116-5117`: "a moved count is accepted only when the entry's 'pg_autoscale_mode' is 'on'"

**Consequence.** A later change to the pool block, or a second Ceph implementation, built from specs/ceph.md will reject an autoscaler-moved PG count. It will also treat an unrecorded same-name pool as a foreign pool-identity refusal, which is the bug X81 fixed.

**Recommendation.** In the pool-adoption paragraph of specs/ceph.md, write the PG-count part of the frozen shape as 'and the PG count unless the listing reports pg_autoscale_mode on'. Add: 'A pool's native ID must be a non-negative integer, else native-output. A same-name pool with no recorded ID is unfinished work only when this operation's attempt record names it; any other unrecorded or different ID refuses pool-identity.' Link B540 as the open fingerprint gap. Leave out the pool_id listing-key detail, which belongs to the adapter. Shorten X81's Outcome to a link to this paragraph.

**Acceptance.** specs/ceph.md contains the three rules, checkable by grep for pg_autoscale_mode and pool_id in the pool-adoption paragraph. X81's Outcome no longer restates the rules and links the ceph.md anchor. The cited guard tests still resolve.

**Decisions and principles.** Decisions read by the judge: D155. Principles applied: P22, P40.

**Verification.** refuter confirmed; judge confirmed at Medium; recommendation amended by the judge.

<a id="cor-11"></a>

#### COR-11 Delivery limitations with safety effect exist only inside delivered records

Medium; gap; changes spec-text; effort S; source M19-2.

**Claim.** The X326 delivered record's Limitations says filesystem identity is the statfs f_fsid, so on btrfs each subvolume is its own check. The capacity-admission spec (specs/substrates.md:703-718) never says what identifies a filesystem. An operator reading 'that filesystem' as the whole btrfs volume is wrong. Writes on another subvolume are not gated, and guest disks on two subvolumes become two checks that each measure the same shared free space. No item or Not-yet-met line records this.

**Evidence.**

- `specs/milestones/delivered.md:12513-12514`: "the local filesystem identity is the statfs 'f_fsid', which btrfs gives each subvolume its own"
- `specs/substrates.md:715-716`: "A write joins a check only when that filesystem holds a counted guest disk on the same host"
- `specs/milestones.md:62-63`: "Record discovered work as an item on the page of the earliest milestone not done whose scope it blocks, or as a parked item"

**Consequence.** An operator on a btrfs host who puts the hosted package tree or the media pool on a different subvolume from the guest disks passes capacity admission with no check, which is the failure B1213 was opened to prevent (the apply overran the disk). Only a reader of a 799 KB history page learns this.

**Recommendation.** In substrates.md#capacity-admission, state that a backing filesystem is identified by its statfs identity, so btrfs subvolumes are separate checks that each see the shared free space. Add a 'Not yet met' line linking a new parked defect item for keying disk checks by the whole filesystem. Optionally extend the milestones-and-knowledge skill rule at line 40: a limitation that changes what an operator may rely on links its spec line or item.

**Acceptance.** substrates.md#capacity-admission names the subvolume boundary, or a parked B item does. Each X326 to X341 Limitations sentence has a spec line or item link, or a record note that it is internal only. The skill carries the sentence.

**Decisions and principles.** Decisions read by the judge: D228, D242. Principles applied: none recorded.

**Verification.** refuter narrowed; judge narrowed at Medium; recommendation amended by the judge.
