<a id="lane-l22"></a>

#### Lane L22: Ceph: ownership, release trust, plan and stretch topology

Auditor model: opus. Assigned: `specs/ceph.md:1-769`.

Good: the slice is unusually strict about effects and trust. Every coordinate is frozen by digest. Package trust has one anchor, a same-origin key and no fallback, and retries cover only transport loss. Global settings have one writer that refuses foreign values. Stretch activation is a recorded, non-repeating staged procedure with distinct drift, foreign and interrupted refusals. Probe containment is proved by inspection, and version compatibility is consistently left to native tools. Needs improvement: image supply-chain trust is promised ('publisher authenticity', 'a digest does not substitute') but undefined. No image signing input exists, and the guest signature policy has no stated contents, while RPMs get a pinned fingerprint. Ceph acquisition is direct, and nothing refuses a host whose Machine declares a Proxy. Several plan-time refusals live only in prose, outside the test-bound table. Bad: the generic libvirt capacity rules are owned by the Ceph page and substrates.md defers to it, an ownership inversion against the generic-flow goal. The stretch section makes release-specific native commands, rule text and unverified JSON keys normative, despite free version selection and the version-specialization port. The NVMe-oF stretch rationale reintroduces a size gate the page disclaims. Run-on trust sentences (88-96) and duplicated retry text add a drift cost.

Candidates after verification: L22-1 ARC-24; L22-2 REC-51; L22-3 ARC-19; L22-4 decided; L22-5 REC-121; L22-6 REC-122. Named and not pursued: 4 further points.

<a id="lane-l23"></a>

#### Lane L23: Ceph: bootstrap identity, continuation, devices and destructive ownership

Auditor model: opus. Assigned: `specs/ceph.md:770-1414`.

Good: the slice is unusually rigorous about identity and destructive custody. The FSID is bound before effects and never derived from names, foreign or ambiguous clusters are refused without adoption, device sets are bound before the first write, and serial resolution refuses by name. Erase receipts gate claim release, interruption exits are stated honestly, and every worked deadline figure is arithmetically correct. Needs improvement: delivery of D239 (root optional at retirement) left two stale sentences, one in ceph.md:1277 and one in state-reconciliation.md:2491, plus a disk-bound rationale that still assumes a root target, so the destructive-path contract now gives two answers. The owned OSD clear is carefully bounded against Bootwright's own state, but it does not exclude the cephadm manager, which the spec itself says may recreate the OSD, so there is a race window with a dead-end outcome. The general rule that zap needs separate authorization is not amended for that clear. Weak: refusal-token coverage is scattered, and partial-cluster, pool-drift and the DB/WAL refusal have no stated code or token. Dirty-disk refusals withhold the very identity their remedy needs. The by-serial pseudo-path is a misleading second spelling, a pending D229 clause, with a narrower grammar than Machine serials. Prose density is very high: rules such as the enrollment budget are hard to audit without re-deriving them.

Candidates after verification: L23-1 REC-02; L23-2 REC-123; L23-3 REC-124; L23-4 CON-05; L23-5 API-135; L23-6 CLI-24. Named and not pursued: 3 further points.

<a id="lane-l24"></a>

#### Lane L24: Ceph: resources, readiness and access

Auditor model: opus. Assigned: `specs/ceph.md:1415-2050`.

Good: the slice has a rigorous ownership core. Every create is bracketed by an attempt record, adoption needs the record plus the frozen shape, and the single-writer guarantee is stated explicitly. Data-bearing resources are never deleted or reshaped, and removal goes to one item (B491). Secret leaves are handled one way everywhere: placeholders in records, spliced in memory, keys lent to apply only. Readiness proves usability (TLS pin, HTTP status, VIP holder, SigV4 policy read as the owner, the deployed oauth2-proxy configuration), and observation copes with cephadm races in a bounded way. Needs improvement: the section is roughly 635 lines of per-family special cases written as prose, mostly duplicating ceph-resources.md promotion records. The drift outcome (refuse, not ready, or re-apply) is chosen per kind with no table, and refusal codes for a recorded object that is gone mix `-foreign` and `-identity`. Bad: three rules promise the "next apply" repairs drift (NFS export, default realm, SSO), which a settled apply cannot do. The opening "inverse" claim and the ceph-resources.md statement that destroy removes the subvolume, then the filesystem, then the pools contradict the never-remove rule in every family paragraph. A move to one general resource contract plus per-kind tables, owned by ceph-resources.md, would fix both and cut what agents must read.

Candidates after verification: L24-1 REC-52; L24-2 REC-125; L24-3 REC-52; L24-4 REC-53; L24-5 REC-126. Named and not pursued: 2 further points.

<a id="lane-l25"></a>

#### Lane L25: Ceph: firewall, custody, removal and concurrency, replication, coverage limits

Auditor model: opus. Assigned: `specs/ceph.md:2051-2488`; `specs/ceph-coverage.md:323-559`.

Good: the destructive paths in this slice are strong. Provided-tiebreaker removal has an explicit proof, effect, absence, recovery and evidence cycle; it refuses foreign state, never reads unreachable as absent, and orders itself before any data-site deletion. Secret custody and the RBD replication credential boundary are precise and anchored in upstream source. The RGW multisite blocker declines a refuse-at-execution design on principle. The removal rules keep a native removal command separate from its proof. Needs improvement: the ingress firewall check reads only runtime firewalld state and passes an enabled-but-stopped firewalld. cephadm's own `--reload` can therefore erase a permit the check accepted, and the coverage page overstates what the check detects. The claims and throttle text has drifted from the code: 'three claims' is really four, `ceph/<cluster>` names both a claim and a throttle, and the concurrency bound is overstated for a replication's peer cluster. Bad: ceph-coverage.md describes an NVMe-oF stretch acceptance profile and a native-judges-size rule, while ceph.md and api/ceph.md refuse every stretch NVMe-oF service and B935 has not started. The Unsupported combinations register also leaves out the stretch refusals that cite IBM, so its fixture test does not guard them.

Candidates after verification: L25-1 API-45; L25-2 REC-127; L25-3 REC-54; L25-4 CON-14. Named and not pursued: 2 further points.

<a id="lane-l26"></a>

#### Lane L26: Add-ons: trust boundary, lifecycle, ownership, handoff

Auditor model: opus. Assigned: `specs/add-ons.md:1-617`; `specs/deferred/add-ons-design.md:1-285`.

Good: add-ons.md is a rigorous, mostly self-consistent contract. It is create-only with no removal entry point, so deletion safety holds by construction. Ownership by recorded uid comes with an explicitly bounded mark-recovery rule. Manual OLM approval uses a tested JSON patch, so the plan checked is the plan approved. Bootwright never approves an upgrade, which honours the no-day-2 scope. A replacement-chain proof is built only from surviving objects. Secret placement keeps every value out of digests and evidence. The GitOps bootstrap object is a single, non-finalized pointer. Needs improvement: attempts and observations use different installed-CSV predicates, so a retry after an owner-approved upgrade can never complete. A routine channel move after handoff reads unknown and is told to destroy, a destructive remedy for a healthy state. The stale-condition rule has no threshold, and the identity collision refusal lives only in a delivery record. Bad: specs/deferred/add-ons-design.md, the page B90 is said to revive, still describes a driver/host-interface, invertible, release-pinned architecture. That contradicts the live lifecycle, project.md's statement that B90 compiles into the same program, and D163. It should be cut down to the open questions for manifest sets and catalogs.

Candidates after verification: L26-1 ARC-25; L26-2 TRK-02; L26-3 decided; L26-4 REC-55; L26-5 API-50; L26-6 ARC-54. Named and not pursued: 2 further points.

### Failure-scenario attacks across pages

<a id="lane-x01"></a>

#### Lane X01: Attack: crash consistency of durable transitions

Auditor model: opus. Assigned: `specs/state-reconciliation.md:210-893`; `specs/contexts.md:228-824`; `specs/contexts/controller-record.md:295-311`; `specs/controller.md:992-1080`.

Good: the slice is unusually crash-aware. Each durable transition in context state names its order: claim before evidence, evidence before binding and registration, the attempt record before the block record, custody before `done`, and withdrawal before release. Each also names its interrupted shape and the command that finishes it. Re-runnable finalization, the narrow adoption of an interrupted start, the D124 custody ordering and the guard against a lost index are sound under SIGKILL. The retained-operation reserve guarantees that destroy remains an exit. Needs improvement: correctness depends on durability ordering under power loss, and the shared publication primitive never states its fsync point, although sibling stores do. The controller descriptor's first binding has a crash window that leaves a directory refused with no exit, unlike the context init rules, which name both exits. The replay-safe inconclusive retry trusts \"an attempt was recorded\" as ownership, even though another rule records attempts that never ran. Bad: the prose is extremely dense. Single sentences carry four to six conditions (for example lines 249-280 and 282-311), so verifying any one scenario takes many cross-reads. That raises the risk of divergence between agents more than any one gap does.

Candidates after verification: X01-1 REC-56; X01-2 REC-35; X01-3 refuted; X01-4 REC-38. Named and not pursued: 1 further point.

<a id="lane-x02"></a>

#### Lane X02: Attack: unknown outcomes and attempts

Auditor model: opus. Assigned: `specs/state-reconciliation.md:559-893`; `specs/state-reconciliation.md:1426-1628`; `specs/managed-os.md:551-714`; `specs/substrates.md:1439-1696`; `specs/ceph.md:770-1128`; `specs/openshift-clusters.md:601-1036`.

Good: the general engine is rigorous about unknown outcomes. A typed failure never proves no effect, cancellation stays unknown, an inconclusive removal gets one replay-safe retry, custody ordering never loses the only access, the log fault is sticky, and interrupted starts are adopted narrowly. BMC resend rules and the Ceph identity rules (FSID never re-allocated) are sound. Managed OS's Q66 before-state is the right pattern. Needs improvement: per-capability observations are not held to the engine's standard everywhere. Silence from a powered-off target is read as absence or as 'never installed' wherever no durable before-state was recorded. Two pages give different outcomes for an expired boot budget, and Ceph's readiness-timeout and partial-cluster rows overlap on the same durable state. Bad: the OpenShift install observation can read a fully installed, powered-off cluster as positive no effect, and a continuation then reinstalls it. Separately, a destroy's removal-check reading is recorded on the apply's block as 'no effect' and survives a refused destroy into a later apply retry. Both put the 'unknown read as absence' failure on a destructive path. The general fix is one rule: an observation reads positive no effect only when the attempt's durable preparation records show the effect never began.

Candidates after verification: X02-1 REC-01; X02-2 REC-130; X02-3 REC-57; X02-4 REC-58; X02-5 REC-44; X02-6 REC-46. Named and not pursued: 2 further points.

<a id="lane-x03"></a>

#### Lane X03: Attack: concurrency, locks and reservations

Auditor model: opus. Assigned: `specs/contexts.md:228-824`; `specs/infrastructure-services.md:118-323`; `specs/ceph.md:2164-2365`; `specs/state-reconciliation.md:6-209`; `specs/controller.md:87-126`; `specs/contexts/log-root.md:1-140`.

Good: the locking contract is unusually explicit. One table maps every command to its root-lock and lease mode. Deadlock freedom is argued, waits are bounded and their outcome named. Cross-context host reservations carry a precise conflict relation per key class, SSH qualification by address and pinned host key, and a durable releasing mark that closes the registration-to-effect race. Media acquisition, runtime retirement and the restore and clone boundary are carefully honest about what they cannot detect. Needs improvement: the reservation model protects only what lifecycle blocks claim. Operator utilities (power commands) and some capabilities (Ceph hosts on provided Machines) sit outside it, while other passages promise that two contexts never drive one server or one SSH host. Setup and the controller stage coordinate only with each other, not with running operations, and launch diagnostics misreport a live setup. Lock fairness is unspecified, so read-only utilities can make lifecycle transactions refuse. A few rules state a general timing or writer requirement that specific passages contradict: late reservation keys, and trust writes without the lease. Bad: the cross-context power gap is the one scenario where the text determines an unsafe outcome on physical hardware that the contract claims to prevent.

Candidates after verification: X03-1 REC-10; X03-2 ARC-82; X03-3 REC-59; X03-4 REC-102; X03-5 REC-131; X03-6 ARC-12. Named and not pursued: 4 further points.

<a id="lane-x04"></a>

#### Lane X04: Attack: destroy and removal safety

Auditor model: opus. Assigned: `specs/state-reconciliation.md:1629-1954`; `specs/state-reconciliation.md:2297-2678`; `specs/ceph.md:1144-1414`; `specs/ceph.md:2164-2365`; `specs/managed-os.md:609-636`; `specs/managed-os.md:1194-1230`; `specs/managed-os.md:1378-1442`; `specs/contexts.md:886-1016`; `specs/add-ons.md:509-527`.

Good: the core removal engine is unusually rigorous. Ownership comes from what an operation started. Removal is planned from the frozen plan and request versions. State is re-proved under the exclusive lock before every transition. Unknown is never read as absence. Lost bindings have exactly two exits. Physical erase binds identity end to end with receipts, and holder release is bounded tightly. Walking twenty failure scenarios through these rules mostly gave a determined, safe outcome. Needs improvement: the physical retirement rules are spread over api/machines.md, state-reconciliation.md, ceph.md and m2.md, and they disagree on whether the root disk must be in the erase policy, which decides whether a cluster's keys survive on disk. Two traps reach the operator only at removal and should be warned at plan time: physical Ceph without erase coverage, and loss of a surviving physical cluster's kubeconfig. The subscription removal can record a clean outcome while a service-side consumer remains. Bad: the no-bypass rule leaves no narrow exit for one permanently gone target, so every such case escalates to abandoning the whole context, and B938 is about to add a one-off bypass. A lost evidence file, which is only a derivable projection, also forces abandonment.

Candidates after verification: X04-1 REC-02; X04-2 REC-60; X04-3 REC-15; X04-4 REC-61; X04-5 decided; X04-6 REC-132. Named and not pursued: 2 further points.

<a id="lane-x05"></a>

#### Lane X05: Attack: frozen intent, continuation identity and build skew

Auditor model: opus. Assigned: `specs/state-reconciliation.md:6-209`; `specs/state-reconciliation.md:339-558`; `specs/state-reconciliation.md:1317-1425`; `specs/contexts.md:187-227`; `specs/project.md:137-184`; `specs/architecture.md:1102-1254`.

Good: the frozen-intent core is strong. A removal is derived from the frozen plan with the frozen binding, ownership is every started block, every transition re-proves its state under the exclusive lock, and continuation across builds is keyed on contract digests guarded mechanically rather than on automation bytes. Admission copies the input and never reads the source again. These rules held across most scenarios I walked. Needs improvement: recovery under build skew is asymmetric between the verbs. An interrupted removal can neither continue under a new closure nor be superseded, so orphaning is its only exit. The additive apply, the newest scenario, is under-specified for cross-build continuation and does not disclose that a failure stakes the whole lineage. Remedies name the registering build rather than the latest one that worked the operation. Bad: the lost-binding remedy offers a "complete backup" restore as one of only two exits. contexts.md defines that restore as a whole-root image, declares it unsupported, and the image silently rolls back every context's records, which is exactly the lying evidence the rest of the contract is built to prevent. The prose is also very dense: long single sentences carry several conditions each, which raises the cost for agents and the risk of misreading.

Candidates after verification: X05-1 REC-62; X05-2 REC-32; X05-3 REC-63; X05-4 REC-64; X05-5 REC-133. Named and not pursued: 3 further points.

<a id="lane-x06"></a>

#### Lane X06: Attack: secrets under failure

Auditor model: opus. Assigned: `specs/secrets.md:1-654`; `specs/contexts.md:854-1016`; `specs/state-reconciliation.md:723-833`; `specs/security.md:105-197`; `specs/cli.md:1104-1142`; `specs/cli.md:1428-1470`.

Good: the crash windows of custody are closed with care. These include the publish-before-done rule, the D124 hand-over ordering, keyring durability with commit, uncertain and cleanup outcomes, and reservations recorded before sealing. Binding classes and the refusal to re-bind lost bindings are strong. Secret input through sudo is guarded against input logging, and the threat model is honest. Needs improvement: the reveal and lifecycle-mutation side is weaker than the input side. Sudo output logging is not considered for any raw reveal. `generate --renew` and replacement do not check whether a live effect-material binding still needs the old version, even though managed-os promises that the recovery passphrase is never renewed and that no bound version can be revealed. That combination can lose a physical disk's only recovery key. Bad, but cheap to fix: a wiped keyring in a ready context reads as uninitialized instead of lost; the restore remedies say 'complete backup' and 'restore the keyring' where contexts.md defines a whole-root 'matching backup' that is not a supported exit; and the Ceph unproved-reveal rows describe a state nothing creates. Same-name adoption of native retention is tracked under B568, so it is not reported.

Candidates after verification: X06-1 REC-12; X06-2 CLI-26; X06-3 REC-65; X06-4 REC-32; X06-5 CON-09. Named and not pursued: 3 further points.

<a id="lane-x07"></a>

#### Lane X07: Attack: physical safety and controller-host self-harm

Auditor model: opus. Assigned: `specs/state-reconciliation.md:2297-2678`; `specs/managed-os.md:1194-1468`; `specs/substrates.md:763-1020`; `specs/api/machines.md:581-779`; `specs/api/environment.md:365-476`; `specs/controller.md:922-991`.

Good: the physical-safety slice is unusually rigorous. One MAC-set predicate is applied on every side. The controller's last proof, the in-installer re-proof and the residual race are each stated honestly. `data-loss` never selects a target. Serial selection and holder release fail closed on ambiguity. Several layers keep the controller host from harming itself: provided Machines are never realized, power commands refuse the host's own identity, and every pre-boot effect requires power Off. Needs improvement: the root-disk contract has drifted. D239's derived `bootVolume` and `volumeRef` selectors appear only in machines.md, while the owning safety sections (state-reconciliation physical disk safety, managed-OS physical installation and %pre) still promise exactly two forms and a refusal. Separately, the erase contract and the API disagree on whether the root target is mandatory. Bad: the bare-metal claim promises that two contexts never drive one server, but power commands ignore other contexts' claims, and a server that reports no UUID can be claimed under two address spellings. These are smaller gaps: the MAC property is unspecified on Redfish, an erase whose target was replaced has no remedy, and pending firmware writes are not surfaced at destroy.

Candidates after verification: X07-1 API-03; X07-2 REC-02; X07-3 REC-10; X07-4 REC-66; X07-5 REC-67; X07-6 REC-43. Named and not pursued: 3 further points.

<a id="lane-x08"></a>

#### Lane X08: Attack: trust, authorization and privilege

Auditor model: opus. Assigned: `specs/security.md:9-104`; `specs/security.md:240-745`; `specs/state-reconciliation.md:2679-2763`; `specs/cli.md:245-432`; `specs/contexts.md:76-152`; `specs/cli.md:1471-1538`.

Good: this slice is mature. The attacker model is explicit and narrow, remote principals have stated blast radii, and both binary pinning across sudo and template-injection closure in Ansible are rigorous. The authorization model is strong: digest-bound data-loss under --yes, inapplicable tokens refuse, the access-credential rebind is gated by three checkable conditions, and every transition re-proves its state under the exclusive lock. Host-key trust never records an observation by itself and requires operator fingerprints when unattended. Controller rebind is honest about the clone it cannot detect. Needs improvement: the CLI never defines what an "interactive" invocation is. As a result, the fingerprint and data-loss confirmations can be accepted after the plan went to a redirected stdout, which undercuts "confirmation of the displayed fingerprint". The sudo-entry guard's allowlist ("what sudo sets") lives only in code, and stock RHEL env_keep makes the difference operator-visible. Bad: little. Two cheap text fixes are a mis-named preflight flag that trusts nothing (with a refusal rule stated differently on two pages) and an over-broad "no password in memory" sentence. Much of the prose is dense and test-name heavy, which costs readers, but I found it internally consistent.

Candidates after verification: X08-1 CLI-27; X08-2 CLI-28; X08-3 CLI-29; X08-4 REC-134. Named and not pursued: 2 further points.

<a id="lane-x09"></a>

#### Lane X09: Attack: desired-versus-real, readiness and ownership after handoff

Auditor model: opus. Assigned: `specs/state-reconciliation.md:1955-2296`; `specs/cli.md:839-1003`; `specs/add-ons.md:451-584`; `specs/project.md:63-110`; `specs/project.md:167-184`; `specs/state-reconciliation.md:159-209`.

Good: the comparison is strictly read-only, and its observation boundary is enforced at the port and runner level, not left to convention. Unknown is never absence. Ownership after handoff is uid-based and does not move. The bootstrap Application is a pointer with no finalizer. Projection admission keeps Secrets out. These are mature and must survive any restructuring. Needs improvement: the drift signal. Add-on and readiness drift surfaces as `partial`, but `--exit-code` ignores partial while still advertising drift detection. The status Handoff line also reads as a live claim when only the records prove it. project.md states early GitOps handoff both as decided (D246) and as pending (Q60). Bad: two failure paths end in disproportionate remedies. OLM's five-InstallPlan retention guarantees that routine owner-approved upgrades eventually read unknown, with the remedy "destroy and apply again", which contradicts project.md's promise. A failed additive apply, the one admitted day-2 path, has no withdrawal: its only exit is destroying the whole environment. Both are fail-closed, but they push operators toward data-destroying actions for benign or local faults.

Candidates after verification: X09-1 CLI-10; X09-2 REC-13; X09-3 REC-63; X09-4 SCO-10; X09-5 REC-99. Named and not pursued: 2 further points.

<a id="lane-x10"></a>

#### Lane X10: Attack: ordering and dependency safety across domains

Auditor model: opus. Assigned: `specs/state-reconciliation.md:894-1425`; `specs/cli.md:649-664`; `specs/ceph-resources.md:1679-1749`; `specs/api/environment.md:149-217`; `specs/add-ons.md:51-213`; `specs/api/addons.md:280-323`.

Good: ordering is graph-only. Stages and `--until` gate which ready blocks start and never relax dependencies, recovery or refusals. Requirements are typed object references, narrowed by family and inverted for removal, and the physical-retirement and online-removal sequences come out correctly from those inversions. Removal fails closed wherever a consumer survives or a host is unreachable. Needs improvement: the engine has no rule of its own for cross-family cycles; two paragraphs disagree on requirements whose target nothing realizes; the cluster-selection omitted-root refusal applies to attachments only; and the plan's start-order promise is looser than its admission rules. Bad: the GitOps handoff exclusion set counts only add-on instance evidence. The cluster network block's NMState objects and hosted KubeVirt objects are owned but fall outside it, and the early last-package handoff lets Argo CD run while those cross-stage blocks still work on the same API. That is a false promise of no co-management. The rest of the slice is sound and dense. The density costs readability but hides no defect beyond these.

Candidates after verification: X10-1 REC-30; X10-2 REC-68; X10-3 REC-69; X10-4 API-13; X10-5 REC-135. Named and not pursued: 3 further points.

### The desired-state API

<a id="lane-a01"></a>

#### Lane A01: API grammar

Auditor model: opus. Assigned: `specs/api.md:1-622`; `specs/api/input.md:1-196`; `api/v1alpha1/object.go`; `api/v1alpha1/schema.go`; `api/v1alpha1/value.go`; `api/v1alpha1/lexical.go`; `api/v1alpha1/scope.go`; `api/v1alpha1/families.go`; `api/v1alpha1/jsonschema.go`; `api/v1alpha1/unrealized.go`.

Good: the grammar is unusually rigorous for a pre-1.0 declarative API. Decoding is strict and safe for credentials, null is never a fallback, explicit empties are preserved, and the catalog, naming and families are single-sourced. Most rules are tied to architecture tests over the Go schema, so the stated grammar and the code can be held together. The unrealized table keeps admission truthful, and the family registry gives cluster kinds a generic extension path. Needs improvement: the tests that guard references and unions are weaker than the prose. Untyped fields (CephNFSExport `serviceID`) and enum-plus-suppressed-sibling shapes (endpoint `source.type`, BMC `tls.trust`) pass them, so the 'holds every registered schema' claims are false today. The reference exception list says 'sole' while the schema has three external references. `dataPoolRefs` combines a polymorphic element with a silent rewrite of authored input. The scope sentence 'Environment's directory' contradicts multi-source `validate -f`. Bad: `metadata.labels` is an envelope field with no consumer, no grammar and an undefined change effect, and an example uses it to restate a spec fact. Nothing in the slice is unsafe on a destructive path.

Candidates after verification: A01-1 API-09; A01-2 API-10; A01-3 API-11; A01-4 API-56; A01-5 API-60; A01-6 API-57; A01-7 API-58; A01-8 API-59. Named and not pursued: 5 further points.

<details>
<summary>Working table of lane A01</summary>

| Kind or surface | Verdict | What is right | What misleads, leaks or repeats | Recommended shape |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Envelope (`apiVersion`, `kind`, `metadata`, `spec`) | adequate | One version, closed metadata, one DNS-label name rule for every kind; no namespace because one Environment is one scope | `metadata.labels` has no consumer, no key grammar and no stated diff/plan effect; an example duplicates `placement.site` in a label | Remove labels, or declare them inert with Kubernetes label grammar and 'no block identity effect' |
| YAML decoding | good | Strict, safe diagnostics, no value echo, null always refused | `%YAML 1.1` accepted and `%YAML 1.2` refused, which inverts the stated semantics | Refuse or ignore every directive, with one stated reason |
| References (classes, Ref/Refs) | needs work | Typed classes, one diagnostic and suppression model, suffix test | `serviceID` is listed as a native-service ref but is untyped and unsuffixed; 'sole' external ref is false (`volumeRef`, `storageClassRef`); `dataPoolRefs` is polymorphic | `serviceRef: nfs.<id>`; a general External class; `defaultDataPoolRef` |
| Unions | needs work | One rule, a test, stated omission arms | Endpoint `source.type` and BMC `tls.trust` are enums with arm-only fields; the test checks only enum-equals-block | Presence arms; the test flags enum-keyed suppressions |
| Collections, enablement, reserved words | good | Named sets as `[]{name}`, `enabled` only with a stated omission meaning, `management` axis fixed | — | Keep |
| Naming rules | good | lowerCamel, native spellings exempt and tested, one-legal-value fields need a named consumer | — | Keep |
| Kind catalog | good | Single table, order and page rows tested | — | Keep |
| Family registry | adequate | Category-named selection, roles, layout accessors | Cites a nonexistent profile `static.clusters`; graph validation re-names two cluster kinds | Point at `steps[].target.static`; make the graph bullet generic |
| Graph validation | adequate | Collision: no value wins, every side diagnosed | Restates the cluster namespace concretely | Link to the registry |
| Defaults, normalization, effective | adequate | Partial specs keep absence; whole-value lists; derived values are overrides that refuse on disagreement | CephFilesystem rewrites an authored `default: false` | Refuse a disagreeing override |
| Native/open fields | good | Exact open points, integer precision preserved, open never widens its container | — | Keep |
| Input discovery and selection | adequate | Bounded, deterministic, reserved payload roots | 'Environment's directory is the scope' is false for multi-source and single-file `validate -f` | 'The source universe is the scope', plus a stated import relation |
| Go schema data (`api/v1alpha1`) | adequate | Shape helpers mirror the grammar; JSON Schema export is labelled advisory | Untyped `serviceID`; enum-plus-suppression pattern; layouts keyed by concrete kind (acceptable inside the registry) | As above |

**Endpoint source as a presence union**
```text
# before
api:
  address: 192.0.2.10
  source:
    type: installer
ingress:
  source:
    type: loadBalancer
    loadBalancerRef: edge-lb
    bindAddressRef: vip-a
# after
api:
  source:
    installer:
      address: 192.0.2.10
ingress:
  source:
    loadBalancer:
      loadBalancerRef: edge-lb
      bindAddressRef: vip-a
```

**BMC virtual-media trust**
```text
# before
virtualMedia:
  tls:
    trust: importCertificate
    removeCertificateAfterBoot: true
# after
virtualMedia:
  tls:
    trust:
      importCertificate:
        removeAfterBoot: true
```

**NFS export service reference**
```text
# before
spec:
  clusterRef: ceph-a
  serviceID: files
# after
spec:
  clusterRef: ceph-a
  serviceRef: nfs.files
```

**CephFilesystem default data pool**
```text
# before
dataPoolRefs:
  - name: files-data
    default: true
  - files-ec
# after
dataPoolRefs:
  - files-data
  - files-ec
defaultDataPoolRef: files-data   # optional; derived as the first entry
```

**Metadata labels (option b, if kept)**
```text
metadata:
  name: edge-a-01
  labels:                 # inert operator metadata; label-key/value grammar
    team.example.io/owner: platform
# no fact that a spec field owns (site, role) belongs here
```

</details>

<a id="lane-a02"></a>

#### Lane A02: Environment kind, selection and defaults

Auditor model: opus. Assigned: `specs/api/environment.md:1-502`; `specs/api.md:385-600`; `api/v1alpha1/environment.go`; `specs/contexts.md:153-227`.

Good: Environment is one explicit root. The controller is never selected implicitly. Category-keyed selection and domain fields line up with the family registry. The kind-defaults algorithm is unusually precise: whole values, arm protection, origin tracking and no I/O. The refusal table and context freezing are tied to tests and are exemplary. Needs improvement: kind defaults cannot state a fleet fact once. Proxy, bypass lists and NTP are repeated per consumer kind and on the controller, and each new cluster kind adds another copy. Cluster lists do not bound the install set: KubeVirt host clusters and replication peers widen silently while attachments refuse, and some closure text describes cases that always refuse. 'Selected' is overloaded, which leaves condition scopes ambiguous. Bad: dependencyVersions and downloads hard-code per-implementation fields that have already drifted from the controller tool table (no govc or kubectl mirror), which taxes every new substrate or cluster kind. Smaller issues are OpenShift and Ceph details on the general page, a redundant defaults.Environment, a misleadingly named fleet key, and a controller-runtime sentence that contradicts service placement on the controller.

Candidates after verification: A02-1 API-61; A02-2 API-13; A02-3 API-62; A02-4 API-12; A02-5 ARC-39; A02-6 API-63; A02-7 API-64; A02-8 API-65. Named and not pursued: 4 further points.

<details>
<summary>Working table of lane A02</summary>

| Kind or surface | Verdict | What is right | What misleads, leaks or repeats | Recommended shape |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Environment as entry point | adequate | Exactly one root; closed shape; explicit controller; name is a label, context owns identity | Grab-bag of ten fields, three of them implementation-named records; Kinds table omits fleet key, downloads, versions, lifecycle | Group into domains, sites, selection, fleet (key and services), tools, controller |
| `spec.domains` | good | One composition rule, one `fqdn` override, single-zone needs only `base` | Rows name install-config `baseDomain` and `OpenShiftCluster`/`CephCluster` names | Compose from `<cluster metadata.name>`; move render notes to the family pages |
| `spec.sites` | adequate | Registry with silent unused entries | "rendered as the CRUSH site bucket name" puts Ceph in the general field | Generic identity; Ceph page states its rendering |
| `spec.containerClusters`/`storageClusters` | needs work | Category-keyed, no CLI narrowing, warnings for excluded roots | hostClusterRef and CephReplication silently widen an authored list while attachments refuse; dead "retained only through" text | One rule: every retained cluster root must be listed when a list is authored |
| Selection vocabulary | needs work | Closure table is explicit | "selected" means both file-loaded and cluster-retained | Define loaded and retained, and use each where it applies |
| `spec.defaults` | needs work | Precise ordering, whole-value rules, origin tracking, no I/O | Keyed by kind only: multidc repeats noProxy three times and NTP twice; `defaults.Environment` is a second home for every field of a singleton | Add `spec.fleet` service selections; drop `defaults.Environment` |
| `spec.remoteMachinesAccessKey` | needs work | Key-distinctness rules; effect-material custody | Name says "remote machines access" but it is the bootwright-account fleet key; heading promises install defaults; condition omits stretch tiebreaker | `spec.fleetKey.keyRef`, with a requirement that covers both uses |
| `spec.dependencyVersions` + `spec.downloads` | needs work | Exact-pin grammar, publisher checksums never from mirror, host prerequisites excluded | Per-tool fields drifted: govc and standalone kubectl have no mirror, kubectl has no version key; libvirt key admits a grammar that always refuses (B676) | One registry-keyed `spec.tools` map |
| `spec.controller` | good | Explicit ref, sole local access, not a node, refusal table tied to test | Runtime sentence (374-376) reads as "never" but services may place on it | Fix the sentence |
| `spec.lifecycle.rescue` | adequate | Refused until a journey exists (D29), so it is explicit | Dead schema names RHEL/Anaconda in the root kind | Leave per D29; revisit when the journey lands |
| Context configuration | good | Separate document, closed, immutable fields, exact-byte frozen manifest | none in this slice | keep |

Fleet selections (fixes the repetition):

```text
# before
spec:
  defaults:
    OpenShiftCluster:
      install:
        proxy: {proxyRef: default, noProxy: [.example.com, 192.0.2.0/24]}
        ntp: [{serverRef: ntp-01}, {serverRef: ntp-02}]
    MachineInstallProfile:
      proxy: {proxyRef: default, noProxy: [.example.com, 192.0.2.0/24]}
      ntp: [{serverRef: ntp-01}, {serverRef: ntp-02}]
# plus the same proxy on the controller Machine
# after
spec:
  fleet:
    proxy: {proxyRef: default, noProxy: [.example.com, 192.0.2.0/24]}
    ntp: [{serverRef: ntp-01}, {serverRef: ntp-02}]
  # kind defaults and per-object values still override, as whole values
```

Tools map (fixes the per-tool drift):

```text
# before
spec:
  dependencyVersions: {helm: "4.3.0", govc: latest, virtctl: "1.9.0"}
  downloads:
    helmMirror: https://mirror.example.test/helm
    virtctlMirror: https://mirror.example.test/kubevirt
    # no govc or kubectl mirror possible
# after
spec:
  tools:              # keys validated against the controller tool registry
    helm:    {version: "4.3.0", mirror: https://mirror.example.test/helm}
    govc:    {mirror: https://mirror.example.test/govmomi}
    virtctl: {version: "1.9.0"}
    openshift-clients: {mirror: https://mirror.example.test/ocp}  # version refused: tied to release
```

  remoteMachinesAccessKey: {keyRef: bootwright-machine-key}
# after

  fleetKey: {keyRef: bootwright-machine-key}  # required by installed Machines or a provided tiebreaker

<a id="lane-a03"></a>

#### Lane A03: Secret and Entitlement kinds

Auditor model: opus. Assigned: `specs/api/secrets.md:1-213`; `specs/secrets.md:1-264`; `api/v1alpha1/secrets.go`.

Good: the Secret model is sound and safety-minded. Desired state holds only descriptors, and there is one material entry path with strict file and sudo-logging rules. Binding is immutable, with a class per reference (effect, access, trust) that governs rebinding. The backend sits behind a catalog seam, produced material and native-side retention are kept apart from declared Secrets, and the threat model is honest. The Go schema enforces the Entitlement arm sets as data. Needs improvement: two page-level contradictions or drifts. Registration is described as virtual-only, while managed OS says virtual or physical. The kind row says 'reads', which is stale since the file source was retired. Generated-certificate SAN derivation hard-codes two consumers and leaves the rest undefined. The specs never say how a Bootwright Secret differs from a Kubernetes Secret. Bad: Entitlement mixes three concepts (RHSM registration, a registry credential and license acceptance) behind a vendor product enum with vendor registry defaults. That duplicates CephCluster.distribution, the pairing between them exists only in code, and redhatCeph is dead admitted input with weaker Satellite checks. Its registry arm also repeats the Registry kind's credential and trust triple, and the Data Foundation example stores the same IBM key twice. A new product or registry consumer currently costs edits in general kinds.

Candidates after verification: A03-1 API-01; A03-2 ARC-01; A03-3 API-66; A03-4 API-67; A03-5 API-14; A03-6 API-68; A03-7 refuted. Named and not pursued: 5 further points.

<details>
<summary>Working table of lane A03</summary>

| Kind or surface | Verdict | What is right | What misleads, leaks or repeats | Recommended shape |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Secret.spec.type` | good | Closed, explicit, fixes legal sources and parts; never inferred | `opaque`/`dockerConfigJson` mirror Kubernetes Secret types, yet the kind holds no data and the specs never say so; `caBundle` means both a trust bundle and, when generated, a signing CA with a private key | Add a "not a Kubernetes Secret" sentence and a targeted `data`/`stringData` refusal; consider a `certificateAuthority` type later |
| `Secret.spec.source` | adequate | Two arms (`contextStore`, `generated`); copied-input rule; `source: {}` blocks inheritance | Kinds row says Bootwright "reads" material (stale since D36); the field page does not say material must exist before apply binds it | Drop "reads"; add one timing sentence linking binding |
| `source.generated` SAN derivation | needs work | Derives from consumers; authored lists override as a whole | Names ArtifactServer and the libvirt BMC by kind; other tlsCertificate consumers (Ceph services) derive an empty set with undefined outcome | Port rule: each serving field states its names; empty union refuses |
| Runtime custody (`specs/secrets.md`) | good | Backend catalog seam, immutable binding, binding classes, produced material, retention boundary, honest threat model | Opening scope sentence says "without lifecycle effects" yet the page owns binding, placement and retention | Reword scope line |
| `Entitlement.spec.type` | needs work | Closed arm set enforced as data; kind defaults never add a forbidden arm | Vendor product catalog plus vendor registry hosts in a general kind; duplicates `CephCluster.spec.distribution`; distribution-to-type pairing exists only in code | Product lives on the consumer; Entitlement becomes typed mechanism arms; consumer states required arms |
| `Entitlement` `redhatCeph` | poor | — | Admitted with required rhsm and registry, but its only consumer is refused; Satellite trust and contentBaseURL rules exempt it; no unrealized row | Remove pre-1.0, or add an unrealized row and type-free Satellite rules |
| `Entitlement.spec.rhsm` | adequate | Managed/external, Satellite with a required CA on RHEL, label validation | Field page says virtual Machines only (managed OS says virtual or physical); machines.md row omits Satellite; `connectToInsights` admitted only to refuse | Fix the two sentences; keep managed-os as owner |
| `Entitlement.spec.registry` | needs work | Scheme-less address grammar, explicit sole trust anchor | Same url/credentialsRef/trustBundleRef triple as the `Registry` kind ("consumers do not duplicate them"); IBM key also hand-merged into the OpenShift pull secret | `registryRef` to an external Registry |
| `Entitlement.spec.license` | adequate | Declarative acceptance kept distinct from command authority | Default `false` for a field whose only legal value (on the only permitting type) is `true` | Required `accept: true`, no default |

Entitlement: product on the consumer, mechanism arms only.

```text
# before
kind: Entitlement
metadata: {name: ibm-ceph}
spec:
  type: ibmStorageCeph
  registry: {url: cp.icr.io/cp, credentialsRef: ibm-registry}
  license: {accept: true}
---
kind: CephCluster
spec:
  distribution: {ibm: {callHome: disabled}}
  entitlementRef: ibm-ceph
# after
kind: Entitlement
metadata: {name: ibm-ceph}
spec:
  registry: {registryRef: ibm-entitled}   # Registry owns url, creds, CA
  license: {accept: true}
---
kind: CephCluster
spec:
  distribution:
    ibm: {callHome: disabled, entitlementRef: ibm-ceph}  # needs registry+license
```

Registry arm reuses the Registry kind.

```text
# before (Entitlement.spec)
registry:
  url: mirror.example.test/ibm
  credentialsRef: ibm-registry
  trustBundleRef: mirror-ca
# after
---
kind: Registry
metadata: {name: ibm-entitled}
spec:
  management: external
  url: mirror.example.test/ibm
  credentialsRef: ibm-registry
  trustBundleRef: mirror-ca
---
# Entitlement.spec
registry: {registryRef: ibm-entitled}
```

License with no misleading default.

```text
# before: default accept: false, refused unless true
license: {}
# after: block presence plus required literal true
license: {accept: true}
```

Generated TLS SAN derivation as a port, with refusal on an empty set.

```text
# before: rgw-objects-tls generated, no lists, consumed only by a Ceph RGW binding
source: {generated: {commonName: s3.lab.example.test}}   # SANs: undefined
# after: admission refuses unless a consumer field publishes names, or lists are authored
source:
  generated:
    commonName: s3.lab.example.test
    dnsNames: [s3.lab.example.test]
```

</details>

<a id="lane-a04"></a>

#### Lane A04: InfraProvider, segments, Network and NetworkConfig

Auditor model: opus. Assigned: `specs/api/machines.md:1-211`; `specs/api/machines.md:955-1055`; `specs/api/networks.md:1-149`; `api/v1alpha1/networks.go`; `api/v1alpha1/machines.go`; `specs/substrates.md:20-133`; `specs/api/environment.md:108-148`.

Good: the provider arm selects the substrate cleanly; MTU is modelled as capacity rather than use; provided versus managed Networks mirror os.provided; carriage checks the fabric without changing it; NetworkConfig is an honest native NMState escape hatch with a declared interpreted subset; and the substrate extension contract and the test-pinned refusal table are exemplary. Needs improvement: segments are declared in two kinds, because a managed Network doubles as a segment and repeats bridge, tagged carriage and capacity. Network's providerRef sits inside the libvirt arm, so the Machine schema hardcodes a libvirt path in what should be a generic join. NetworkConfig restates the Network's VLAN ID and gateway and only cross-checks them, which defeats template reuse. Site scoping is undefined for site-less Machines. The realized KubeVirt arm is documented on the refused-arms page. Bad: the 'one 802.1Q domain per site' assumption is false for libvirt bridges. It forces the shipped example to declare one Network across two unconnected bridge domains, which contradicts the definition of a Network as one layer-2 network and feeds false reachability to consumers that read Network membership.

Candidates after verification: A04-1 CON-01; A04-2 ARC-40; A04-3 API-69; A04-4 API-15; A04-5 API-16; A04-6 API-70; A04-7 API-71; A04-8 API-02. Named and not pursued: 4 further points.

<details>
<summary>Working table of lane A04</summary>

| Kind or surface | Verdict | What is right | What misleads, leaks or repeats | Recommended shape |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `InfraProvider` (name) | adequate | The glossary states that `Infra` means substrate (glossary 19-22) | The same glossary bullet has to separate it from "infrastructure service"; api.md files it under the category "Substrate" | Keep it, or rename to `SubstrateProvider` while pre-1.0 (taste; not filed) |
| `InfraProvider` arms | good | Arm is the selector; closed union; bare-metal defaults inherit only into omitted fields | The realized KubeVirt arm is documented on "Refused machine arms" and under the heading "Refused arms"; `libvirt.uri` is a one-value enum | Move the KubeVirt arm into api/machines.md; leave the deferred page vSphere-only |
| `segments[]` | needs work | Neutral `untaggedNetworkRef`/`taggedNetworkRefs`/`mtu`, plus one per-substrate arm (`bridge`, `portgroup`, native ref) | A segment can also be synthesized from a managed Network, which repeats `bridge`, `taggedNetworkRefs` and capacity; KubeVirt `networkRef` sits beside `untaggedNetworkRef` | Declare segments in one place; a segment over a managed Network omits `bridge`; rename to `hostNetworkRef` |
| `Network` | needs work | One L2 network, provided or managed, MTU as capacity, strict CIDR and gateway rules, per-site uniqueness | `providerRef` sits inside the `libvirt` arm, so the Machine segment join hardcodes `libvirt.providerRef`; "one 802.1Q domain per site" is false for libvirt bridges, so the example declares one Network across two bridges; site-less Machines are unspecified | Top-level `providerRef`; domain scoped to the carrying fabric; a site-less Machine matches only site-less Networks |
| Machine NIC → segment → interface | adequate | `hardware.nics` (neutral) → arm `nics[].segmentRef` → `interfaceMatches` → NMState; bond-across-segments refusal | Four hops for one cable; the sole-segment default is written on libvirt but only read on bare metal | Keep it; it is minimal given the hardware/OS split D240 asked for |
| `NetworkConfig` | good | Native NMState; declared interpreted subset; addresses injected from `network.addresses` | VLAN ID and gateway are restated from `Network` and only cross-checked, so templates are rarely reusable (one per Machine in the example) | Inject an omitted `vlan.id` and an omitted default-route `next-hop-address` from the assignment's Network |
| New-substrate impact | adequate | One dispatcher row, one schema arm, one segment arm, refusal-table rows | A substrate that manages networks would also need a Network arm, a second `ScopeJoin` path and new same-name collision rules | With top-level `providerRef` and one segment site, it adds only the arm |

**Network providerRef (finding 2)**

```text
# before
kind: Network
spec:
  provided: false
  ipv4: {cidr: 198.51.100.0/26, gateway: 198.51.100.1}
  libvirt:
    providerRef: lab-libvirt
    bridge: virbr-nv
    taggedNetworkRefs: [nv-guest]
---
# after
kind: Network
spec:
  provided: false
  providerRef: lab-libvirt      # arm must match the provider's arm
  ipv4: {cidr: 198.51.100.0/26, gateway: 198.51.100.1}
  libvirt:
    bridge: virbr-nv
    forward: nat
```

**One segment site (finding 3)**

```text
# before: segment nv-lab is implicit (the managed Network itself)
kind: InfraProvider
spec:
  segments:
    - name: nv-trunk
      taggedNetworkRefs: [nv-guest-trunk]
      libvirt: {bridge: br-nv}
---
# after: every segment is listed
kind: InfraProvider
spec:
  segments:
    - name: nv-lab
      untaggedNetworkRef: nv-lab   # managed here: bridge comes from it
      taggedNetworkRefs: [nv-guest-lab]
      libvirt: {}
    - name: nv-trunk
      taggedNetworkRefs: [nv-guest-trunk]
      libvirt: {bridge: br-nv}
```

**NetworkConfig injection (finding 6)**

```text
# before
interfaces:
  - {name: nic0.120, type: vlan, vlan: {base-iface: nic0, id: 120}}
routes:
  config:
    - {destination: 0.0.0.0/0, next-hop-interface: nic0.120,
       next-hop-address: 198.51.100.65}
---
# after: id and next hop injected from the assignment's Network
interfaces:
  - {name: nic0.120, type: vlan, vlan: {base-iface: nic0}}
routes:
  config:
    - {destination: 0.0.0.0/0, next-hop-interface: nic0.120}
```

**KubeVirt segment (finding 7)**

```text
# before
segments:
  - name: data
    untaggedNetworkRef: data
    kubevirt: {networkRef: {kind: ClusterUserDefinedNetwork, name: data}}
# after
segments:
  - name: data
    untaggedNetworkRef: data
    kubevirt: {hostNetworkRef: {kind: ClusterUserDefinedNetwork, name: data}}
```

<a id="lane-a05"></a>

#### Lane A05: Machine kind

Auditor model: opus. Assigned: `specs/api/machines.md:212-779`; `api/v1alpha1/machines.go`; `api/v1alpha1/machines_clear.go`; `api/v1alpha1/machines_erase.go`; `api/v1alpha1/machines_install.go`; `specs/deferred/machine-arms.md:1-122`.

Good: the Machine contract is unusually rigorous where it matters most. Destructive selection is fail-closed: it needs exact serial and size, WWN beside any path, never discovery and never a force path. BMC addresses have one spelling. Virtual arms exclude the physical fields their substrate would ignore. Roles are inferred from consumers, never declared. Network addressing has one owner and deterministic selection. Needs improvement: the page has drifted behind D239/X320. The 'exactly two root forms' text and the state-reconciliation sentence 'root must be listed' contradict the delivered logical-volume default and the retained root, both on the disk-erasing path. One physical disk's identity is restated across up to five fields with different grammars, and the bare-metal destructive policies sit in the 'substrate-neutral' hardware block, breaking the page's own split. Bad: fleet authoring. Bare metal has no profile, kind defaults are one global fragment, and firmware is barred from defaults, so a fifty-server estate is copy-and-paste. The OS lifecycle is a boolean plus an optional reference with three names, so a missing reference silently changes the lifecycle instead of refusing. The deferred vSphere arm's MAC rule contradicts its schema.

Candidates after verification: A05-1 API-03; A05-2 REC-02; A05-3 API-17; A05-4 decided; A05-5 API-72; A05-6 API-18. Named and not pursued: 3 further points.

<details>
<summary>Working table of lane A05</summary>

| Kind or surface | Verdict | What is right | What misleads, leaks or repeats | Recommended shape |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Machine.spec.substrate` arms | good | One arm per provider substrate. Virtual arms carry no MAC, BMC or physical root field. The arm must match the provider's. A bastion's bare-metal arm can stand without a provider. | Bare metal alone has no `profileRef`. vSphere `nics` reuses the bare-metal MAC record (MAC required) while its spec says the MAC is derived otherwise. | Give every arm `profileRef`. Give vSphere its own NIC record. |
| `Machine.spec.hardware` | needs work | `nics[].name` and neutral root hints are truly substrate-neutral. | Holds `eraseOnRemoval` and `clearOnInstall`, which are bare-metal-only destructive policies, contrary to lines 320-322. | Keep only `nics` and neutral `rootDevice` hints. Move the policies into `substrate.baremetal`. |
| Root device (`hardware.rootDevice` + `substrate.baremetal.rootDevice`) | needs work | Durable identity required, kernel names refused, serial uniqueness across Machines, logical-volume discovery fails closed. | One disk is split across two blocks. The 'exactly two forms' text contradicts D239's default `bootVolume: {}` and `volumeRef` (and managed-os.md:1265). | List four admitted forms in one place. The root becomes a `diskRef` into an inventory, or `bootVolume`/`volumeRef`. |
| `eraseOnRemoval` / `clearOnInstall` | adequate | Typo-proof selection by exact serial and size, WWN beside every path, opt-in, bounded counts, root protected from clear. | The same disk identity is restated in two to three lists plus Ceph by-serial paths with different grammars. state-reconciliation.md still says the root 'must be listed'. Undefined root target for a volume root. | A disk inventory plus references. Fix the stale sentence. Define the root target via the proved NAA. |
| `substrate.baremetal.bmc` | good | One canonical spelling, independent TLS legs, `disableVerification` only on the Machine, provider defaults for credentials and trust. | `virtualMedia.tls` suppression rules sit only in code (machines.go:13-17). | Keep as is. State the suppression table in the spec. |
| `firmware` | adequate | Atomic block, `prove` mode, password names refused, verbatim attributes. | Forbidden as a kind default, and there is no profile, so a fleet repeats it on every Machine. | Bare-metal provider `machineProfiles[].firmware`, merged atomically and visible in effective state. |
| `os` lifecycle | needs work | Lifecycle invariants are stated precisely, and an OS-ready `installProfileRef` refuses once. | Boolean plus optional ref encodes three lifecycles. Omitting the ref silently picks downstream-installed. Three names for one lifecycle. | A discriminated union, or one name per lifecycle defined in one table. |
| `network` | good | Single static-address owner, deterministic install-address selection, explicit merge rules, MTU checked against capacity, never derived. | Dense prose: refusal sites are spread over paragraphs rather than one table. | Keep the shape. Add a refusal table. |
| `access` / `proxy` | adequate | Derived access for installed Machines, pinned known_hosts grammar, D7 placement-host rule. | A Machine proxy kind default breaks mixed fleets (stated as a caveat, not fixed). | Lifecycle union arms carry their own proxy defaults. |
| Fleet authoring (50 Machines) | poor | NetworkConfig plus overrides, install profiles and provider BMC defaults share some intent. | Kind defaults are one global fragment. Bare metal has no profile. Firmware, NIC names, root form and profile references are copied per host. | Bare-metal `machineProfiles[]`, with per-host identity only on the Machine. |
| deferred/machine-arms.md | adequate | Clear about what is admitted but refused, and why. KubeVirt MAC derivation is explicit. | vSphere MAC 'else derived' and segmentRef text contradict the schema and machines.md:333. | Align with D240 (6): MACs authored. |

Disk inventory, before and after:

```text
# before
hardware:
  rootDevice: {deviceName: /dev/disk/by-id/wwn-0x5000c500a1b2c301}
  eraseOnRemoval:
    method: metadataClear
    targets:
      - {serialNumber: S1, sizeBytes: 3840755982336}
  clearOnInstall:
    targets:
      - {serialNumber: S1, sizeBytes: 3840755982336}
substrate:
  baremetal:
    rootDevice: {wwn: "0x5000c500a1b2c301"}
# after
substrate:
  baremetal:
    disks:
      - {name: root, wwn: "0x5000c500a1b2c301"}
      - {name: osd-1, serialNumber: S1, sizeBytes: 3840755982336}
    rootDevice: {diskRef: root}      # or bootVolume: {} / volumeRef
    eraseOnRemoval: {method: metadataClear, targets: [{diskRef: osd-1}]}
    clearOnInstall: {diskRefs: [osd-1]}
# CephCluster selects disk:osd-1
```

Bare-metal profile, before and after:

hardware: {nics: [{name: eno1}, {name: eno2}]}
# after: InfraProvider

        firmware: {mode: enforce, secureBoot: true, bootMode: UEFI,
                   biosAttributes: {ProcVirtualization: Enabled}}

# Machine

  baremetal: {profileRef: r650, bmc: {address: ...}, nics: [...MACs]}
```

<a id="lane-a06"></a>

#### Lane A06: MachineImage and MachineInstallProfile

Auditor model: opus. Assigned: `specs/api/machines.md:780-954`; `specs/managed-os.md:1-418`; `api/v1alpha1/machines_install.go`; `specs/api/secrets.md:103-213`; `specs/managed-os.md:1011-1193`.

Good: media custody, image pinning and release proof are rigorous and safe. Registration proves ownership before it changes anything and never runs clean or --force. The Kickstart token grammar closes injection, and the closed installer union with a tracked refused arm keeps the API shape stable. The image/profile/Machine split is mostly minimal: the image is a pinned pointer, the profile is the reusable OS intent, and the Machine overrides NTP and proxy and carries its host key. Needs improvement: extensibility. The generic os-install flow, the media-store refusals and the "neutral" customizations are all Anaconda/Kickstart/RHEL-specific, and the installer side has no counterpart to the substrate port. A second installer or OS family would mean editing general code, and the deferred templateClone page shows per-arm applicability that the active spec does not model. Shapes leak mechanics: `redfishVirtualMedia` names a delivery path in an OS profile and is "required on any substrate", contrary to B905's pushed delivery; the hosted-tree DVD avoids MachineImage and its pin; subscription repositories sit outside spec.subscription. Bad: little is actually wrong. One cross-page contradiction (secrets.md says registration is virtual-only), two fields that can only hold their default, and a deferred page that has drifted.

Candidates after verification: A06-1 refuted; A06-2 API-73; A06-3 API-74; A06-4 API-01; A06-5 API-19; A06-6 API-75; A06-7 API-76. Named and not pursued: 3 further points.

<details>
<summary>Working table of lane A06</summary>

| Kind or surface | Verdict | What is right | What misleads, leaks or repeats | Recommended shape |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `MachineImage` | adequate | Minimal (bootMedia + optional checksum); local-media only; plan pins size/digest and re-verifies | Only the boot ISO goes through it. The hosted-tree DVD that actually supplies packages is a raw string with no checksum pin | Every media-store image a profile uses goes through a MachineImage (`hostedTree.imageRef`) |
| `MachineInstallProfile.spec.os` | adequate | Exact `<major>.<minor>` identity, no compatibility pairing (D163); proved against `.treeinfo` | The family token `rhel` maps to the literal "Red Hat Enterprise Linux" only inside a plan refusal; family, arch and version checks are hard-coded, not owned by an implementation | Keep the fields; the selected installer implementation declares the families it installs and its release mapping |
| `spec.installer` (union) | needs work | Closed union; templateClone admitted and refused, tracked by B99 | The os-install flow has no installer port (the adapter always renders Kickstart and runs mkksiso), unlike the substrate dispatcher; per-arm applicability lives only in a deferred page, which has drifted | Installer registry keyed by arm name, with family, customization groups and entrypoint per implementation |
| `anaconda.redfishVirtualMedia` | needs work | Explicit server and endpoint, never inferred | Names a delivery mechanism in an OS profile; "required on any substrate" although B905 pushes the image on KubeVirt; the OpenShift counterpart is required only on bare metal | `installerPublication.artifactServerEndpoint`; required when the substrate's delivery or private material needs it |
| `anaconda.packageSource.hostedTree` | adequate | Exact choice; mirrors are kept apart from install sources | `fromMedia` string versus MachineImage ref; the cross-kind `os/<name>/` collision is a publication-path detail surfaced to authors (settled by D83) | `hostedTree.imageRef` |
| `spec.subscription` + `customizations.repositories.subscription` | needs work | Ownership-proven registration; Satellite reuse; frozen request | One registration fact in two subtrees joined by a cross-field rule; secrets.md says "virtual Machine" only; machines.md omits the Satellite route | `spec.subscription.{entitlementRef, repositories.{enable,disable}}` |
| `spec.customizations` | needs work | Closed groups, explicit defaults, injection-safe token grammar | Placed as OS-neutral but typed as "Kickstart token", with FIPS marked "RHEL-only"; `ssh.passwordAuthentication` admits only `false` | Neutral grammar; each implementation declares which groups it consumes; drop `ssh.passwordAuthentication` |
| `spec.updates` | good | Within-release default with explicit source rule and TPM2 PCR guard | A default that refuses a profile with no update source (settled by D190, not reported) | Keep |
| `spec.proxy` / `spec.ntp` | adequate | Shared choice and selection types; clear Machine override semantics | The credentialed-Proxy repository refusal is restated in machines.md:866-869 and managed-os.md:199-205 | State it once in managed-os.md and link to it from machines.md |
| `Entitlement` (rhsm) | adequate | References only, closed arms per type | `connectToInsights` always refuses, "none tracked" | Remove `connectToInsights` until a journey exists |

    entitlementRef: rhel-sat
    repositories: {enable: [rhel-9-baseos], disable: ["*"]}

    repositories:

```

# after

<a id="lane-a07"></a>

#### Lane A07: Infrastructure service kinds

Auditor model: opus. Assigned: `specs/api/infrastructure-services.md:1-291`; `specs/infrastructure-services.md:1-117`; `specs/infrastructure-services.md:324-711`; `api/v1alpha1/infrastructure_services.go`.

Good: the six kinds share one real pattern in schema code (one Go builder) and in the common spec (flat `management` discriminator, explicit references, no implicit selection, no environment fallback, no readiness edge for external services). The three network daemons share one capability and role, configuration is derived from the graph, and the runtime contracts for replay, inverse, private publication and reservations are rigorous. Needs improvement: the pattern breaks at the access surface. Managed services expose endpoints, while external forms use five different shapes, so every consumer branches on management mode and a seventh kind has nothing canonical to copy. A managed Proxy's consumer URL is unspecified. Endpoints are marked optional but are effectively required. The selection section lacks the Implementations and Supported-shape parts that the architecture template promises. LoadBalancer's bind vocabulary and the generic `serverRef` are naming outliers. Bad: `additionalIngressHosts` is a frozen, inert field with no warning. External ArtifactServer is dead public surface handled by a second unrealized mechanism, unlike managed Registry and LoadBalancer. Neither is unsafe, and every fix is cheap now that the project is pre-1.0.

Candidates after verification: A07-1 API-20; A07-2 API-79; A07-3 ARC-41; A07-4 ARC-02; A07-5 API-21; A07-6 API-77; A07-7 API-78; A07-8 API-80. Named and not pursued: 5 further points.

<details>
<summary>Working table of lane A07</summary>

| Kind or surface | Verdict | What is right | What misleads, leaks or repeats | Recommended shape |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Common `spec` (management, machineRef, implementation, image) | good | Flat discriminator, no wrapper or default flag; digest-pinned images; external grants no ownership; one Go schema function builds all six kinds | `implementation` is required although each kind has one legal value (defensible for extension); block prefixes are scattered on the api page | Keep. Move block prefixes and identities into an Implementations table in specs/infrastructure-services.md |
| Proxy | needs work | Atomic choice, no env fallback, derived client ACL | No rule turns a managed endpoint into httpProxy/httpsProxy URLs; openshift-clusters.md says an external Proxy is used at its "declared `address`", a field it lacks | State the managed URL derivation; use endpoints in both modes |
| DNSServer | needs work | Graph-derived records; storage contributes through composition | `port` has one legal value; `additionalIngressHosts` is admitted, frozen and inert with no `api.deferred`, and also accepted on external; an external resolver can have only one address | Drop `port`; remove or defer `additionalIngressHosts`; `endpoints[]` in both modes |
| NTPServer | adequate | Answers at local stratum, coexists with the host clock, readiness honest about sync | Same single-value `port`; external scalar `address` | Same as DNSServer |
| ArtifactServer | adequate | Listener and endpoint split, TLS coverage, consumer and private publication contracts | No `implementation` though it runs nginx; external arm fully specified yet refused at admission; that arm forces a kind-default exception and cross-mode suppressions | Remove the external arm (or list it as unrealized); optionally `implementation: nginx` for symmetry |
| Registry | adequate | Credentials and trust are service facts in both modes | Managed arm unrealized (correctly warned) but given a full deployment-defaults row; external `url` differs from every other shape | Fold `url` into an external endpoint |
| LoadBalancer | needs work | Sole-entry normalization | `bindAddresses`/`bindAddressRef` on an external LB where nothing is bound; the only kind not using `endpoints`/`endpointRef` | Rename to `endpoints[]{name,address}` and `endpointRef` |
| Consumer selections | adequate | Explicit refs, `direct: {}`, ordered sets, whole-value inheritance | `serverRef` names three kinds; a fleet proxy with its `noProxy` is repeated per consumer kind (Machine, MachineInstallProfile, OpenShiftCluster) | Kind-named refs; keep per-consumer scope (deliberate) |
| Endpoints and bindAddress derivation | needs work | Endpoints reference Machine addresses, not copies | `endpoints` marked optional, yet a "no endpoints" derivation always yields a refused wildcard | Make managed `endpoints` required |
| Adding a 7th kind | needs work | One capability and role for the network services; architecture recipe | No Implementations/Supported-shape table to extend; six external access shapes to choose from | One endpoint concept; template-complete selection section |

**Unify endpoints (Proxy shown; DNS/NTP/Registry the same)**

```text
# before (external)
spec:
  management: external
  connection:
    httpProxy: http://192.0.2.8:3128
    httpsProxy: http://192.0.2.8:3128
# consumer
proxy: {proxyRef: lab-proxy}
# after (external)
spec:
  management: external
  endpoints:
    - name: primary
      url: http://192.0.2.8:3128   # DNS/NTP: address: 192.0.2.53
  connection:                       # auth/trust stay service facts
    trustBundleRef: proxy-ca
# consumer (endpointRef normalizes when single)
proxy: {proxyRef: lab-proxy, endpointRef: primary}
```

**Managed endpoints required; drop single-value port**

```text
# before
kind: DNSServer
spec:
  management: managed
  machineRef: controller
  implementation: dnsmasq
  port: 53            # only legal value
  endpoints: [...]    # "optional", but refused if absent
# after
kind: DNSServer
spec:
  management: managed
  machineRef: controller
  implementation: dnsmasq
  endpoints:          # required, non-empty
    - {name: ip, addressRef: ip}
```

**LoadBalancer vocabulary**

```text
# before
kind: LoadBalancer
spec: {management: external, bindAddresses: [{name: api, address: 192.0.2.10}]}
# consumer
source: {type: loadBalancer, loadBalancerRef: lb, bindAddressRef: api}
# after
kind: LoadBalancer
spec: {management: external, endpoints: [{name: api, address: 192.0.2.10}]}
source: {type: loadBalancer, loadBalancerRef: lb, endpointRef: api}
```

**DNSServer ingress hosts**

```text
# before
spec: {management: external, address: 192.0.2.53, additionalIngressHosts: [a.example]}
# after: field removed until designed, or forbidden on external and warned api.deferred
spec: {management: external, endpoints: [{name: primary, address: 192.0.2.53}]}
```

</details>

<a id="lane-a08"></a>

#### Lane A08: OpenShiftCluster kind

Auditor model: opus. Assigned: `specs/api/openshift-clusters.md:1-566`; `specs/openshift-clusters.md:25-431`; `api/v1alpha1/openshift_clusters.go`; `specs/openshift-coverage.md:1-209`.

Good: the kind and family split is coherent. The roster is the single source of pools. Topology is a general rule with an artifact-keyed specialization hook and parity tests. The refusal table carries reasons, remedies, the lifting items and a test. Installer inputs are frozen, carry no secrets and are coercion-safe. Trust selection is per consumer and explicit. Needs improvement: the selection prose has gone stale against delivered work. "Direct access" contradicts the delivered proxy, the data-loss paragraph and the coverage page still say physical nodes refuse after B67, and a managed mirror refusal is missing from the table. The virtual-media requirement is keyed to bare metal rather than to delivery mode. Native-spelled installer fields are not marked as passthrough. Bad: an authored platform on a single-node cluster is silently discarded, and the kind's own Shape example models it. The endpoint-uniqueness rule makes the OpenShift page the registry of every other kind's address fields (Ceph, SMB, services), which taxes every future kind and has already drifted against the add-ons and secondary-network lists. The VIP rationale is repeated four times with a release range embedded in normative text.

Candidates after verification: A08-1 DOC-01; A08-2 API-24; A08-3 API-22; A08-4 API-23; A08-5 ARC-03; A08-6 API-82; A08-7 API-04; A08-8 API-81. Named and not pursued: 4 further points.

| Kind or surface | Verdict | What is right | What misleads, leaks or repeats | Recommended shape |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Kind and family split (`OpenShiftCluster` in category `containerCluster`) | good | One kind per distribution family (D183 Q77), OKD as a distribution value, membership published through the registry, and the general flow names no kind. | Nothing material. The family is coherent for adding a Kubernetes or Rancher kind. | Keep. |
| `spec.distribution` | adequate | An exact version or a pinned image; no release catalog (D163). | `channel` is admitted and fully inert on the only path. | Keep. Leave `channel` in the inert table (already done). |

"Direct access" in the supported shape contradicts the delivered proxy. `agent` defaults to `{}` although "its presence selects it". | Refuse a non-`none` arm on one node. Key the virtual-media requirement to delivery mode. Fix the supported-shape sentence. |
| `spec.install.endpoints` | adequate | One slot shape, typed sources (installer, external, loadBalancer, node), node-source SNO, VIP subnet and uniqueness checks. | Four fields (`port`, `scheme`, `prefixLength`, `interfaceNetworks`) exist only to refuse at plan (settled by D183 Q71). The uniqueness rule hard-codes other kinds' address fields (Ceph, SMB, services). The VIP rationale is repeated in four places with a release range. | Move the address-holder catalog to a general address-claims registry. State the VIP rule once, with no release range. |

<a id="lane-a09"></a>

#### Lane A09: CephCluster and native service documents

Auditor model: opus. Assigned: `specs/api/ceph.md:1-494`; `specs/ceph-native-api.md:1-1011`; `api/v1alpha1/storage_native.go`; `specs/deferred/ceph-api.md:1-73`.

Good: the native-service-document approach is principled. Identity uses qualified native names. Each non-core family has a closed member record whose refused members name an owner. Secrets arrive only through a fixed leaf registry. Placement freezes eligible sets, not assignments. Release pinning holds to D157/D163, with strong trust rules for package repositories. Needs improvement: the contract is spread out. The members Bootwright forbids, derives or rewrites are scattered over several pages. The CephCluster 'field record' has no table and is missing three admitted fields. OSD, the destructive family, has no member record, and its dynamic selectors pass admission and refuse at plan with no refusal-table row. Distribution arms leak IBM-specific package fields to the top level, and the default arm can never plan, which taxes adding a second Ceph distribution. Bad: the binding-routing rule is stated three ways, and the native-input page refuses bindings that a tested example needs. That page's examples and line 19 predate D185's flattening, and the deferred page holds a live grammar beside superseded camelCase shapes. Most fixes are text-only; the distribution reshape is the one API change, and it is cheap pre-1.0.

Candidates after verification: A09-1 API-05; A09-2 API-25; A09-3 ARC-04; A09-4 API-83; A09-5 TRK-01; A09-6 API-84; A09-7 API-26. Named and not pursued: 5 further points.

<details>
<summary>Working table of lane A09</summary>

| Kind or surface | Verdict | What is right | What misleads, leaks or repeats | Recommended shape |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `spec.services` native envelope | adequate | Native snake_case kept; qualified identity; `service_name` must agree; `unmanaged`/`preview_only` refused | Schema admits `config`, `extra_*_args` and `custom_configs`, while the page says 'where qualified' and admission refuses them; derived and rewritten members (crush_locations, enable_mtls, device aliases, crash, log_to_file, `_admin` rule) are spread over several sections | One 'Bootwright-owned native members' table: member, types, treatment, where visible |
| Core MON/MGR/MDS/OSD records | needs work | Explicit-path OSD profile with identity proofs; MDS bound to its filesystem by `service_id` | No member table, unlike every other family; the schema admits dynamic selectors, slots and sizes that refuse only at plan, and that refusal has no refusal-table row; ceph.md calls dynamic selectors both 'resolved' and 'unsupported' | A records table like RGW's, plus a refusal-table row for OSD options |

<a id="lane-a10"></a>

#### Lane A10: Ceph resource kinds, part 1

Auditor model: opus. Assigned: `specs/ceph-resources.md:1-923`; `specs/api/ceph.md:19-84`; `specs/api/ceph.md:335-494`; `api/v1alpha1/storage.go`.

Good: the shared contract is strong. Owners are explicit, every kind names its cluster through clusterRef, ownership is never inferred from a native name, defaults are frozen and observed, and native projections cite their upstream source. CephRBDImage, CephClient, CephFilesystem and CephSubvolume have precise promotion records with ownership proofs, lost-reply adoption rules and readiness that reports drift without repairing it. Removing a data-bearing object is never silent. Needs improvement: the page still carries its pre-approval "target" frame, which denies that these kinds are realized and says the examples cannot run. Three kinds keep duplicate field tables, and the two RBD image tables already disagree. The replica default is stated three different ways. The undocumented singleHostDefaults field feeds the default rule. Native identity follows three patterns (metadata.name, nativeName, a required ruleName). Bad: CephReplication spreads one mirroring choice over two pools and a `type` discriminator, which will need reshaping when another arm arrives. Several fields are admitted only so they can be refused or must equal a derived value. The storage pages do not say that leaf kinds (client, image, subvolume) are frozen at day 0, so adding one more client means destroying the environment.

Candidates after verification: A10-1 COR-04; A10-2 API-27; A10-3 API-26; A10-4 API-85; A10-5 decided; A10-6 API-87; A10-7 API-86. Named and not pursued: 5 further points.

| Retained owners table | adequate | One row per owner with the native-service relationship | Mixes lane kinds with gateway/consumer prose; duplicates field facts kept in records | Keep rows to responsibility only and link the records |
| CephPlacementPolicy | adequate | Owned CRUSH rule, reserved names, device-class host counting, stretch refusal | ruleName required and repeats metadata.name; failureDomain admits one value | ruleName optional (default metadata.name); drop failureDomain until site/rack land |
| Replicated protection | good | One default pair, native rationale for the host rule | Restated as 3/2 in CephPool and 2-else-3 in the PG budget; depends on undocumented singleHostDefaults | Single owner; others link; document or remove singleHostDefaults |
| CephPool | needs work | Presence arms for protection, role-derived application, closed EC rules, PG budget | application is a redundant field; mirroring.mode duplicated on two pools; EC parameters/crushRoot/clay/lrc/shec admitted only to refuse; role optional in schema but required at plan | Drop application and mirroring; parked EC options become unknown fields |
| CephReplication | needs work | Explicit directed relationship, both claims sorted, strict completion proof | `type: rbd` sibling discriminator against P13; mode lives on pools; arbitrary 1-3 image cap | rbd presence arm that owns mode and imageRefs |

CephReplication (mode single-owned, presence arm):

```text

kind: CephPool            # both pools
spec: {role: rbd, mirroring: {mode: image}}

  clusterRef: ceph-a
  type: rbd

  peerClusterRef: ceph-b

    poolRef: rbd-a
    peerPoolRef: rbd-b

    imageRefs: [disk-1]   # required for image, forbidden for pool
```

---

metadata: {name: ssd-hosts}
spec: {clusterRef: c, crushDeviceClass: ssd}   # ruleName defaults to metadata.name
---
